## 2026-11-04 — One band rule for urgency, deadlines and workload

A read-only audit of `internal/priority`, `internal/agenda`,
`internal/commitments` and `internal/action` reported the same high-signal
levels re-typed in three places: `scoreSignals`'s reasons, `Filter.matches`'s
buckets and `action.withDue`'s due source. The audit called the scoring and
filter rules one duplicated predicate; implementing it that way immediately
failed the ranking's golden snapshot (`reasons [… urgent deadline …], want
[… deadline …]`), which is the evidence that they are two different facts:

- the **reason** "urgent" means the message's own urgency is at the top level,
- the **bucket** "urgent" is *urgent now*, either because the message is urgent
  or because a deadline is at the top level.

So the round consolidated the thresholds and their composition instead of
merging the two:

- `internal/action` owns the levels (`UrgentLevel`, `DeadlineLevel`,
  `WorkloadLevel`), `Bands` (the four levels) and the three predicates
  `UrgencyHigh`, `DeadlineSoon`, `Workload`, plus `Urgent` defined as
  `UrgencyHigh() || DeadlineSoon()` — the bucket cannot disagree with the two
  reasons it composes.
- `priority.Signals.Bands()` (in `signals.go`, beside the other signal
  helpers) converts the stored ranking record once; `scoreSignals` reads
  `UrgencyHigh`/`DeadlineSoon`/`Workload` and `Filter.matches` reads
  `Urgent`/`DeadlineSoon`/`Workload`.
- `action.withDue` reads `Signals.Bands().DeadlineSoon()` instead of `>= 3`.

**Regressions.** `TestBandsAreOneRule` (action) tables every level edge and
pins the composition and the bulk veto; `TestSignalsBandsReadTheSameLevels`
pins the conversion; `TestDueSourceFollowsTheDeadlineBand` walks levels 0–5 and
requires `DueClassifier` exactly at the band; `TestFilterBucketsAreTheScoringReasons`
(priority) drives seven signal shapes through `Score` and requires each bucket
to equal the composition of the item's own reasons; `TestDueSourceIsTheSharedDeadlineBand`
ties the classifier's due source to the ranking's deadline band. Mutation
checks: a filter that reads the raw urgency fails with `urgent bucket false,
reasons [deadline recent]`; an `Urgent` that drops the deadline fails with
`Urgent false, want true`.

The file-size ratchet caught the first placement: adding the converter to
`priority.go` took it to 1,564 lines against the 1,558 budget, so it lives in
`signals.go` and the budget is unchanged.

**Evidence.** `go vet ./internal/action ./internal/priority`; `go test
./internal/action ./internal/priority ./internal/store ./internal/triage
-count=1` passes; `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet
configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

**Residual risk.** The ask→action table (`action.primaryFor` vs
`priority.actionAsk`) is the audit's other high finding and is still spelled
twice; it is the next round on these packages. The thresholds moved but their
values did not, so no stored ranking changes. The deployed build predates this
change.

## 2026-11-04 — The query-embedding cache is the shared view cache

The same audit's medium finding, one round after the worker: `search.qcache.go`
was a second hand-rolled bounded single-flight cache — its own entry map with a
`ready` channel, its own FIFO eviction, its own "a failed embed installs
nothing" rule — while `viewcache` documents exactly those invariants and every
other read service already uses it.

- **One option, not a variant flag.** `viewcache.Options.NeverExpires` is the
  one new semantic: an installed entry is served until `Keep` rejects it or it
  is evicted. It fits the query cache because its key (vector space + folded
  text) already covers every input that can change the vector, so a TTL would
  only re-derive an identical value.
- **One cache.** `Searcher.queries` is now
  `*viewcache.Cache[string, []float32]` (size 64, never expiring, component
  "search"); `qcache.go` is deleted and `similar` makes one `Get` with the
  embed as its build. `Searcher.Close` joins both this cache and the semantic
  worker, so shutdown reads the same `jobs` gate for both.
- **Panic text stays out of the notice.** `viewcache` recovers a panicking
  build (`safe.Value`), which turns an embedder crash into a degraded semantic
  leg rather than a dead process. `similar` now recognises a
  `*safe.PanicError`, logs it and reports the one honest sentence ("the
  semantic index is unavailable") instead of pasting `panic: …` into the
  user-facing reason.
- Regressions: `TestNeverExpiresServesAnOldEntryUntilEvicted` pins the new
  option (no rebuild 24 hours past the TTL, the size bound still evicts), and
  `TestQueryEmbedPanicKeepsTheNoticeHonest` pins the boundary (full-text answer
  kept, no "panic" in the reason or the notice). The existing query-cache
  tests (one model call per text, single flight) now exercise `viewcache` and
  pass unchanged. Mutations: dropping the `neverExpires` branch fails with
  `2 builds for a never-expiring entry, want 1`; making the search cache expire
  fails with `text-only search used the embedder: used false, 1 calls`.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/search ./internal/viewcache ./cmd/mailsense`;
`go test` for the three packages passes; `go test -race ./internal/search
./internal/viewcache` passes (60 s / 1.3 s); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all
fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: `NeverExpires` is a second way to express "the key is the whole
identity"; a cache that passes both a TTL and the flag silently ignores the TTL,
which the option's comment states. The deployed build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — The semantic search worker is detached and joinable

A read-only audit of `internal/hub`, `internal/brief`, `internal/world`,
`internal/conversations` and `internal/search` found one high-severity item:
`search.Search` started the semantic leg in a goroutine with its own
`context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), …)`, no join and no recovery.

Three consequences, all real:

- `internal/safe` is the documented owner of "a build that outlives its
  request" and says so verbatim, so this was a second implementation of the
  detach rule.
- The goroutine read the store after the request returned, and nothing could
  wait for it: `Searcher` had no `Close`, so the store owner could close the
  database under a running vector refresh.
- A panic in `similar` (a vector copy, a provider call, a store read) killed the
  process instead of becoming an error.

**One owner each.**

- `safe.Detached(ctx, s.base, …)` now builds the detached context, and
  `safe.Value` guards both legs, so a panic becomes a `*safe.PanicError`.
- `Searcher` gained `base`, `cancel` and a `join.Group` (`workers`). Both legs
  are tracked; a waiting search runs under the caller's context, an interactive
  one under `safe.Detached`, and after `Close` no new worker starts (the query
  answers from full text).
- `Searcher.Close(ctx) bool` refuses new workers, cancels the running ones and
  joins them. It is registered in the app's one read-model closer list
  (`cmd/mailsense/readmodels.go`) through `searchAPI`, so shutdown waits for it
  before the store closes, exactly like the other cached read models.

**Regressions.** `TestSemanticWorkerIsJoinable` blocks the embedder in a runtime
call that ignores cancellation, then requires `Close` to report a miss inside a
20 ms bound and to join once the call returns; `TestSearchAfterCloseStartsNoWorker`
requires a closed searcher to answer from full text without embedding;
`TestSemanticWorkerPanicIsRecovered` requires a waiting search to return a
`*safe.PanicError` and an interactive one to keep its full-text answer.
Mutation checks: a `Close` that returns true without joining fails with
`Close reported a join while the worker was still running`; dropping
`safe.Value` crashes the test binary with `panic: synthetic embedder crash`.

**Evidence.** `go vet ./internal/search ./cmd/mailsense`; `go test
./internal/search ./cmd/mailsense -count=1` passes; `go test -race
./internal/search` passes (41 s); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks
passed (9 vet configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

**Residual risk.** The detached worker is cancelled by `Close` rather than
allowed to finish, so a shutdown may still leave one vector refresh to redo on
the next start; that is the same trade-off `viewcache` makes. The query cache
(`internal/search/qcache.go`) is still a hand-rolled single-flight and the next
round on this package moves it onto `viewcache`. The deployed build predates
this change.

## 2026-11-04 — The shell search bar is the screen's own filter

A UI round that started from a pre-existing red end-to-end test and ended with
three defects fixed at one owner: the router's policy for focus and for
replacing the mounted screen, plus the scoped-search adoption rule.

**What was wrong.** `scripts/test-ui.sh` had a test failing on three of four
runs ("Companies keeps its placeholder, accessible name and filter across a
cached Back"). Instrumenting the router showed why: `live-refresh old=#2
new=#3` replaced the screen node after the test had marked it, so the cached
Back restored a different node. Chasing that led to the real defects:

1. **The router stole focus from the shell bar after every mount.** The fresh
   and cached paths both did `if (!dom.main.contains(document.activeElement))
   dom.main.focus()`, and the shell search input lives outside `#main`. A
   scoped query typed slower than the filter debounce kept only its first
   character: reproduced with `pressSequentially("Beta", { delay: 350 })`,
   which left `value: "B"` and `activeElement: "main"`.
2. **`canReplaceMain()` ignored the shell bar.** A background repaint could
   replace the screen while the owner typed in the bar that filters it.
3. **`activateScopedSearch` erased newer typed text.** It adopted the typed
   value only when the route had none, so a slow mount landing between two
   keystrokes overwrote the input with the previous query. Reproduced under the
   full suite: `Expected: "Beta"`, `Received: "Bea"`.

**One owner per rule.**

- `restoreNavigationFocus()` (`12-router.js`) is the one rule both mount paths
  call: ask-screen focus, else leave the shell bar alone, else return focus to
  `#main` for a link-started navigation.
- `canReplaceMain()` treats a focused shell bar like a focused control inside
  the screen, so `refreshActiveRoute` defers to the existing
  `deferRefreshUntilBlur()` path.
- `activateScopedSearch()` (`33-search.js`) adopts the bar's text whenever it
  holds focus and differs from the route, then filters with it.
- The two stale held tests that asserted the old inline code
  (`TestRouterActivatesScopedSearchOnEveryMount`,
  `TestUXRecoveryAndSelectionContracts`, `TestOwnerFacingJobAndScopeNamesAreLocalized`)
  now assert the owner instead.

**Regressions.** New e2e test *a scoped query keeps the caret in the shell bar
while it filters* types `Beta` at 350 ms per character and asserts the value,
the focus, the URL and the filtered rows; the cached-Back test is now stable
(4/4 runs, previously 3/4 red); new structural guards
`TestNavigationFocusKeepsTheShellSearchBar` and
`TestScopedSearchKeepsNewerTypedText` pin the three rules. Mutation check:
removing the shell-bar guard from `restoreNavigationFocus` makes the e2e test
fail with `Expected: "Beta" / Received: "B"`.

**Evidence.** `go test ./internal/ui -count=1` passes; `scripts/test-ui.sh`
reports **179 passed** (was 177, +2 new tests) on two consecutive full runs;
`scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87
packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

**Residual risk.** The full e2e suite still showed one unrelated spec failing
per full run under load while passing alone (`boot.spec.ts` scroll restore,
then `learning.spec.ts` certification gate); both are timing-sensitive tests
around held responses and boot events and are a separate de-flaking round. The
deferred refresh now waits for the shell bar to lose focus, so a screen that
stays in the bar for a long time is refreshed when the owner leaves it, not
during typing. The deployed build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — One precision rule and one subscription rollback

The layer1/triage/engine audit's two remaining lows.

**One answered-precision rule.** `layer1/requirements.go` and `stage.go` each
recomputed `1 - Errors/Answered`, while a certification already stores its
observed precision. A report written before that field existed carries
`Precision = 0` and its counts, so reading the field straight would have made
the same numbers 0 % precise on one surface and their real ratio on a fresh
one.

- `selective.Certification.AnsweredPrecision()` is the one accessor: the stored
  value when the report carries one (a billed precision can differ from the
  raw ratio), the counts' ratio for a legacy report, and 0 when nothing
  answered. `LabelNeed` reads it directly; the learning blocker keeps its
  "nothing answered is 1.0" default and asks the accessor otherwise.
- Regressions: `TestAnsweredPrecisionReadsLegacyCounts` pins the legacy report
  against a freshly finished certification (0.97 both), the unanswered case and
  the stored-value-wins case; `TestLabelNeedReadsALegacyCertification` pins that
  a counts-only report and the same report carrying its precision produce the
  same label request. Mutation checks: dropping the fallback fails with
  `legacy precision 0, want the freshly certified 0.97`; reading the field
  straight at the call site fails with `legacy {Need:292 Fixable:false}
  differs from a report carrying its precision {Need:1860 Fixable:true}`.

**One subscription install/rollback.** `AfterRuns` and `AutoLabels` each
spelled the same `[]func() (func(), error)` loop: install one, keep its stop,
stop everything installed when one fails.

- `subscribeAll(subs ...)` in `internal/layer1/subscribe.go` owns it. Both
  wirings pass their subscriptions and keep their own extra shutdown work
  (`stopRetrain`; the automatic loop's timer channel).
- Regression `TestSubscribeAllRollsBackOnFailure` asserts a failed install runs
  nothing after it, stops exactly the subscriptions already installed, returns
  no stop function, and that a complete install stops every subscription once.
  Mutation-checked by dropping the rollback loop: `stopped 0 installed
  subscriptions, want 1`.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/layer1 ./internal/selective`; `go test
./internal/layer1 ./internal/selective -count=1` passes; `scripts/test-fast.sh`
reports all fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race
qa+api`).

Residual risk: the accessor treats a stored `Precision` of 0 with answered rows
as "legacy" and recomputes; a genuinely 0 % report recomputes to 0 anyway, so
the branch is harmless. The subscription helper assumes each install returns a
distinct stop; both wirings do (the bus returns a new unsubscribe per
subscription). The deployed build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — The label ranking uses the shared view cache

The layer1/triage/engine audit's last medium: `layer1`'s `orderCache` was a
hand-rolled bounded single-flight cache (its own mutex, entry map, per-entry
`ready` channel, eviction of the oldest installed entry, error deletion) while
`labels_cache.go` already states that every read service uses `viewcache`.
Only the queue had been migrated.

- **One cache owner.** `Runner.orders` is now
  `*viewcache.Cache[orderKey, []LabelTask]`, built on first use exactly like the
  queue cache (`ordersOnce`, so a `Runner` literal still works), with
  `labelOrderTTL` (the queue's 30 s: generations carry correctness, the TTL
  bounds only what a generation cannot see) and `labelOrderSize` (4: the
  questions a reviewer cycles through). `orderEntry`, `orderCache` and its
  `installLocked` eviction are deleted (about 90 lines); `queueOrder` is one
  `Get` with `buildOrder` as its build.
- **Shutdown joins both.** `Close` now bounds-joins the queue and ranking
  caches and reports `true` only when both joined, so the store owner still
  never closes under a ranking rebuild.
- The ranking's error behaviour is preserved: `viewcache` fails the first
  build's waiters and installs nothing, which is what the hand-rolled cache
  did by deleting the entry.
- Regressions: `TestQueueOrderIsOneBuildForConcurrentCallers` runs one cold
  batch of eight concurrent `queueOrder` calls and asserts a single member
  read, identical task order for every caller, and that a warm batch reads
  nothing; `TestLabelQueueReusesTheOrderAcrossALabelWrite` was rewritten to
  count member reads instead of peeking into the deleted cache internals, and
  still proves a label write rebuilds the queue while reusing the ranking.
  Mutation-checked by bypassing the cache (`return r.buildOrder(...)`):
  `8 member reads, want 1`.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/layer1`; `go test ./internal/layer1 -count=1`
passes (31.6 s); `go test -race -run 'TestQueueOrder|TestLabelQueue'
./internal/layer1` passes; `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks
passed (9 vet configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: the ranking now expires after 30 s where it previously lived
until a generation changed; an expired entry is still served while one
background rebuild runs, so a reviewer sees no pause, but a rebuild can now
happen under an unchanged generation. The deployed build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — One routed-view session and one triaged population

The layer1/triage/engine audit's medium #4: `summarySession` and `pageSession`
were the same three fields (`profile`, `key`, `roles`) with `prepareSummary`
and `preparePage` spelled line for line, and the triaged-population filter
`store.MessageFilter{Roles: …, OwnerOnly: true}` was rebuilt at five sites.

  (`internal/triage/triager.go`); the page's `eachEligible` method moved to it.

- **One population filter.** `triagedFilter(roles)` owns the base — the triaged
  folder roles of owner-scope mail — and every read narrows its own copy:

  (`filter.RowIDs = rows`), the decision scope and its probe
  (`filter.RowIDs = o.MessageIDs`), the row stream behind `eachTriaged` /

- **The question-key projection is reused too** (audit low): the summary's
  inline profile→`[]store.QuestionKey` loop now calls the existing

- Regressions: `TestTriagedFilterIsOnePopulation` pins the base (roles +

  `TestOnlyTriagedFilterBuildsThePopulation` parses every non-test file and
  rejects any other `store.MessageFilter` literal with `Roles` or `OwnerOnly`,
  so Page, Summary, Read, the decision scope and the export provably start
  from the same value. Mutation checks: restoring the hand-built filter in
  `buildPage` fails with `page.go builds the triaged population by hand`;
  adding `OwnerContent` to the owner fails with `the base filter carries a
  caller's own predicate`.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/triage`; `go test ./internal/triage -count=1`
passes (11.0 s); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet
configs including `triagelive`, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: the structural guard only sees composite literals, so a filter
built field by field into a variable would pass; the behavioural triage suites
(page, summary, read, causal, probe) are the other half of the proof.
`viewSession` still carries `roles` copied from the configuration at prepare
time, exactly as the two twins did. The deployed build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — One paid-call protocol for the two chat adapters

A read-only duplication audit of `internal/layer1`, `internal/triage` and
`internal/engine` found no high-severity item and three medium ones, all in the
engine's two chat adapters: the decider (`engine/decision`) and the generator
(`engine/generate`) each spelled the same paid-call accounting, the same key
resolution and the same reserve/settle protocol. All three are now single-owner.

- **One accounting path.** `engine.PaidCall` (`internal/engine/call.go`) owns
  the sequence every adapter must follow: start the clock, send through
  `PostJSON`, build the base usage, classify a transport failure or a non-200
  with the one rule, apply `AccountedUsage` with the one estimated rule
  (`ErrAfterWrite` for a transport failure, `!Provider.Declined` for a status),
  and report the call once through `Deps.Record` and the adapter's log. A 200
  is left to the adapter, which decodes first and then calls `Report` with the
  token counts and the billed flag. The adapters' own `post`/`record` methods
  (four functions) are deleted; each keeps a three-line `paid()` describing only
  its label, its transport classification and its one extra log attribute.
- **One key refusal.** `Provider.APIKey(secretStore)` returns the record's key
  or the one `ErrNoKey` error with the same message; the decider and the
  generator call it. The embedder keeps its own refusal on purpose: it is
  `embed.ErrNoKey` over `engine.ErrUnavailable`, a different class ("start the
  runtime"), not a duplicate of this one.
- **One reserve/settle protocol.** `engine.Charge[T](ctx, ceiling, call)`
  reserves before the call, settles with the usage the call reports even when
  it failed (a failed call may still be billed), and returns `ErrBudget`
  without running the call when the reservation is refused. The decider's chunk
  loop and the generator both use it.

Regressions: `TestPaidCallAccountsEveryFailureKind` is a table over {transport
failure, failure after the write, 400, 402, 429 with a quota code, 500}
asserting one record per call, status 0 for a transport failure, the estimated
flag from the one rule, the accounted tokens and USD; `TestPaidCallLeavesSuccessToTheAdapter`
pins that a 200 is not reported before the adapter decodes it; `TestChargeReservesAndSettlesOnce`
covers covered, failed and refused calls; `TestProviderAPIKeyIsOneRefusal`
covers present, empty and missing secrets. Mutation checks: forcing
`estimated := false` on the status path fails the 500 case with `want failed
status=500 estimated=true`; settling only on success fails with `settled 0
times, want 1`; returning `ErrInput` instead of `ErrNoKey` fails both key cases.

The audit's remaining mediums are the triage `summarySession`/`pageSession`
twin and `layer1`'s `orderCache`, which re-spells the bounded single-flight
contract `viewcache` already owns; its lows are a profile→question-keys
projection, a precision derivation, two subscribe loops, and the
`triage.folder_roles` reading.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/engine/...`; `go test ./internal/engine/...`
passes (engine, decision, generate, embed); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all
fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: this is a billing-path refactor, so its safety is the engine's
own accounting tests plus the adapters' failure/transport/parity suites, all
green; the log attribute order changed slightly (adapter extras before
`usd`/`duration`), which no test asserts and no contract exposes. The deployed
build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — One read-only transaction policy for multi-statement reads

The store audit's last open item (low #11): `buildCompanyCounterpartsFrom` and
`threadStates` each opened a read-only transaction by hand —
`BeginTx(&sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly: true})` plus a deferred rollback — because
each makes two reads that must observe one database snapshot.

- **One owner.** `inReadTx[T](ctx, db, label, fn)` in `internal/store/store.go`
  opens the read-only transaction, rolls back on every return path and never
  commits, and returns the body's value or error unchanged. The two call sites
  now pass only their label (`company counterparts`, `thread states`) and their
  body; `BeginTx(ReadOnly)` appears once in the package.
- Regression `TestInReadTxRunsTheBodyOnceAndReturnsItsValue` pins the wrapper's
  contract (one body run, value and error returned unchanged), and
  `TestOnlyStoreOwnsTheReadOnlyTransaction` parses every non-test file and
  fails if any file other than `store.go` builds a `sql.TxOptions` with
  `ReadOnly` — the next hand-written read transaction cannot appear silently.
  Mutation-checked by adding such a helper to `threadstates.go`:
  `threadstates.go opens its own read-only transaction; call inReadTx`.
- The wrapped bodies are unchanged apart from indentation, so the snapshot
  behaviour and the existing thread-state and counterpart tests are untouched.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/store`; `go test ./internal/store -count=1`
passes (27.7 s); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet
configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: the driver's handling of `ReadOnly` is not asserted (a
multi-statement read relies on SQLite's own snapshot for correctness); the
wrapper's job is one policy and one shape, which the structural guard pins. The
deployed build predates this change.

## 2026-11-04 — One participant rule for threads, summaries and deadlines

The store audit's low #7: the thread page used `participantAccumulator`, but
`ThreadSummaries` and `DueDeadlines` each re-spelled the per-message rule —
normalize the sender and every recipient, drop empty addresses and the owner's
own identities, once per message — into a local set. A change to that rule (a
new participant field, a different normalization) would reach the thread page
and silently miss the two agenda reads.

- **One predicate, one set.** `internal/store/thread.go` now owns
  `externalAddress(normalized, owner)` and
  `externalAddresses(sender, recipients, owner)` beside the accumulator.
  `participantAccumulator.add` uses the first; `ThreadSummaries` and
  `DueDeadlines` use the second. Duplicate recipients (the same person in To
  and Cc, or in another case) collapse to one address, and an owner address is
  never a participant of either view.
- Regression `TestParticipantProjectionsAgree` seeds one conversation with a
  duplicate, differently-cased Cc and an owner recipient, a second message from
  the colleague, and a second conversation whose only external participant is
  a Cc'd recipient. It asserts that `ThreadMessages`, `ThreadSummaries` and
  `DueDeadlines` all name `client@example.test` + `colleague@example.test`, and
  that the recipient-only conversation names `dana@example.test`.
  Mutation-checked on both paths: giving `ThreadSummaries` no recipients fails
  with `recipient-only summary participants [], want dana@example.test`; giving
  `DueDeadlines` none fails with `deadline participants [client@example.test],
  want [client@example.test colleague@example.test]`.
- The earlier mutation attempt was also a lesson recorded here: with the same
  helper dropped only from `ThreadSummaries`, the original fixture still passed
  because its second message came from the colleague, so the recipient-only
  conversation was added to isolate the recipient rule.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/store`; `go test ./internal/store -count=1`
passes (68.4 s); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet
configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: `ThreadSummaries` still folds the per-conversation set in Go
with its own map, and `DueDeadlines` sorts each message's list; the shared rule
is membership and exclusion, not ordering, which each view owns for its own
contract. The deployed build predates this change.

The store audit's High #1: `companybook.go` and `counterparts.go` each spelled

sampled the same pair, install under the sampled pair, and `safe.Detached`

which the race detector accepts. The book may return its previous value when

## 2026-11-04 — The owner-facing content boundary has one spelling

The store audit's highest-value finding: the combination "visible folders AND

or junk folder" was written by hand at twenty sites across thirteen files. Each
half already had an owner (`ownerContentWhere`, `threadContentRoleWhere`), but

  the only spelling. `conversationWhere` (the digest's private copy) is deleted
  and its three uses renamed; the other seventeen call sites in

  `mailquery`, `thread`, `world` and the digest use the owner.
- **Reordered sites stay equivalent.** `thread.go` and both `world.go` queries
  interleaved a conversation/task predicate between the two halves; they now
  put `ownerFacingWhere(vis)` first and the extra predicates after. SQL `AND`
  is commutative, and the existing
  `TestDueDeadlinesAndThreadSummaries` (which seeds a picked shared store)
  still sees only the owner's deadline and summary.
- **Deliberate partial uses are unchanged and now say so at their sites:**
  attachments (content store kind, no role), identity (content plus
  sent-by-owner), All mail (`messagepage`, no role so drafts stay visible),
  ThreadStates (role only, a shared reply must still move the state), and
  `EachMessage`'s `OwnerContent` filter.

  `TestOwnerFacingBoundaryHasOneSpelling` parses every non-test file in the
  package and fails if any file other than `each.go` names both identifiers in
  code (comments excluded via the AST). Mutation-checked by adding
  `var _ = ownerContentWhere + threadContentRoleWhere` to `counterparts.go`:
  `counterparts.go combines the two halves by hand`.

Evidence: `go vet ./internal/store`; `go test ./internal/store -count=1`
passes (60.6 s, including the shared-store deadline/summary and thread-content
boundary tests); `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet
configs, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`). No query result changed: the
rewrite is textual, and the boundary halves already came from their owners.

Residual risk: the guard is file-scoped, so a future file that names only one
half but means both still passes; the behavioural tests remain the real proof.
The deployed build predates this change.

- **Deleted** `priorityAPI`, `agendaAPI`, `searchAPI`, `askAPI` and
  `resourcesAPI`. The concrete owners (`*priority.Service`,
  `*agenda.Service`, `*search.Searcher`, `*qa.Service`, `*resource.Guard`)
  already satisfy the `api.Services` interfaces exactly, so `servicesFor`
  assigns them directly. The api package still depends only on its interfaces;
  no import cycle appears, and a signature drift is still a compile error at
  the assignment.
- **One contract repaired on the way.** `resourcesAPI{guard: nil}` was a
  non-nil interface, so the status handler's documented "resources absent when
  the API was built without a guard" was false and a call would have panicked.
  The service list now sets `Resources` only when a guard exists.
- **The agenda closer follows.** `readModelCloserList` passed `agendaAPI{w}`
  only for its `Close`; it now appends `w.app.agenda` when the app wired one,
  so an unwired app contributes no closer instead of a nil receiver the join
  would call. `TestEveryCloserToleratesAnUnwiredApp` lost its adapter case and
  gained an assertion that an unwired wire's closer list joins cleanly.
- `apiwire.go`: 1349 → 1297 lines, five types fewer. Every adapter left
  (`companies`, `hub`, `status`, `learning`, `heldRemovals`, `jobs`,
  `mailboxes`, `runs`, `triage`, `settings`, `secrets`, `providers`,
  `sidecar`, `logs`, `layer1`, `messages`, `thread`, `conversations`,
  `commitments`, `brief`) carries at least one method that is not a forward:
  a view mapping, a lazy build, a bound, or a guard. Those cannot be deleted
  without moving real behaviour.

Evidence: `go vet ./cmd/mailsense ./internal/api`; `go test ./cmd/mailsense
./internal/api -count=1` pass; `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks
passed (9 vet configs including Windows, 87 packages, sidecar, `-race
qa+api`).

Residual risk: the four lazy service builders (`companiesService`,
`conversationsService`, `commitmentsService`, `briefService`) share a shape but
each constructs a different service from different dependencies; forcing them
through one generic would add an abstraction without removing knowledge, so
they stay. The deployed build predates this change; it is wiring only, no wire
behaviour changed.

## 2026-11-04 — A pick no longer re-reads the mailbox views to start its sync

The write-snapshot round removed the route's re-list; one scan remained.
`StartPicked` read `MailboxViews` again to map the new selection to sources,
right after `syncer.edit` had returned exactly that snapshot for the response
and the `TopicMailboxes` event. A pick therefore did three scans: before the
change, after it, and once more to start the sync.

- **`StartPicked` takes the snapshot.** `StartPicked(ctx, m, connectors,
  views)` maps sources from the views the caller already read; `nil` means the
  caller has none and the views are read once here (the automatic first pass
  after a restart, which has no selection write to borrow from).
  `startPicked` itself no longer touches the store.
- **The pick passes what it has.** `mailboxesAPI.Pick` hands over the views
  `Syncer.Pick` returned, so a click now does two scans (the before/after pair
  `edit` needs) and no third.
- **The scheduler keeps its own read.** `Scheduler.attempt` now calls
  `StartPicked(ctx, jobs, connectors, nil)` on its first world pass and
  `StartPickedMail` on later ones; both still read once, because neither has a
  snapshot in hand.
- Regression `TestStartPickedUsesTheSnapshotItIsGiven`: the store's selection
  is empty and only the passed snapshot names a picked source; one job starts.
  A re-read would start none. Mutation-checked by making `StartPicked` ignore
  the argument and read the store: `the passed snapshot did not select the
  source: []`.
- The eight syncer test call sites now pass a snapshot (`Pick`'s return, a
  `pickedViews` helper, or explicit `nil` for the scheduler path).

Evidence: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/syncer ./cmd/mailsense` pass;
`scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87
packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`).

Residual risk: `nil` is the "read it yourself" sentinel; a caller with a
legitimately empty non-nil snapshot passes it as such, and the pick path
always has a real slice. `StartPickedMail` and the scheduler's first pass keep
their single read because they have nothing to reuse.

## 2026-11-04 — Two cursors, two owners, one wire shape

The audit's last consistency item was the cursor split: the mail page parses
`before` in the handler, the conversations page leaves it to the service. Read
against the code, the split is correct and is now documented as deliberate.

- **They are different objects.** A mail cursor is a `store.Cursor`: a keyset
  position bound to the role, store, sender and read state, encoded and
  validated by the store (`store.ParseCursor`), and `store.MessageListQuery`
  carries it typed, so the handler parses it. A conversations cursor binds the
  *normalized* query and state plus its row position (`conversations.cursor`),
  facts only that service knows after normalization, so `pageStep` decodes it.
  One owner per cursor type, like every other cache.
- **The wire is one shape.** Both routes answer the same `invalid_cursor`
  payload (code, message, no params). New `TestMalformedCursorsAnswerOneShape`
  drives `not-a-cursor` and the present-but-empty value on both routes and
  asserts the payloads are identical, whether the handler or the owner caught
  it.
- **An empty result still validates.** Reviewing the service flow showed the
  validation already runs inside `pageStep` regardless of row count, which no
  test pinned; the empty-mailbox case in `TestConversationPagePathsAgree` now
  asserts a malformed cursor is `ErrInvalidCursor` with zero conversations.
  Mutation-checked by guarding the decode on `len(rows) > 0`: `an empty mailbox
  accepted a malformed cursor: <nil>`.
- Comments at both parse sites and on `handleConversations` state the two
  owners and the shared wire shape, so the next audit does not reopen it as a
  bug.

Evidence: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/conversations ./cmd/mailsense`
pass; `scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87
packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`). No production behaviour changed.

The route audit flagged six `/api/actions/*` names with no client. The
call-site search before removing them: no Go, JS, TS, shell or spec call
reaches `evidence`, `layer1`, `judge`, `label`, `label_messages` or
`backfill_bodies`; only endpoint tests and `docs/API.md` named them.

- **Removed the alias branches.** `sync`, `index`, `run_evidence`,

- `label_messages` remains a learning blocker id; the UI handles it by opening

- Regression `TestActionAliasesAreGone` drives all six names and asserts the

Evidence: `go test ./internal/api ./cmd/mailsense` pass;
`scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87

Residual risk: `/api/actions/index` is the one remaining action with no
production caller (only tests use it). It is a distinct manual capability, not

## 2026-11-04 — A mailbox write returns the list it already read

`POST /api/mailboxes/{pick,unpick,declare,undeclare}` read `MailboxViews`
three times per click: once by `syncer.edit` to validate the keys, once by
`edit` after the change to publish it, and once more by the route to build its
response. The second and third reads could also disagree with each other, so
the bus event and the response were not guaranteed to be one snapshot.

- **The service returns its own snapshot.** `syncer.edit` now returns the
  post-change views it publishes; `Syncer.Pick/Unpick/Declare/Undeclare`
  return `([]store.MailboxView, error)`, `api.MailboxesAPI` follows, and the
  production adapter passes them through (a successful pick still starts its
  first sync, with the same warning path on failure).
- **The route writes what it got.** `writeMailboxList` is the one response
  shape; the write handlers hand it the service views, and `writeMailboxes`
  (the plain GET) keeps the list read. The third scan is gone and the response
  is exactly the published event.
- Regression: `TestMailboxWriteReturnsTheServiceSnapshot` drives all four
  writes with a distinctive snapshot, asserts the service was reached once,
  that `Mailboxes.List` was **not** called again, and that the body is that
  snapshot. Mutation-checked by restoring `writeMailboxes`: `the write route
  listed the mailboxes 1 more times`.
- Test call sites moved to the two-value signatures (`internal/syncer`
  identity/StartPicked/status tests, `cmd/mailsense/firstrun_test.go`, and the
  `outlooklive` integration test, which the tagged vet config caught only
  after the first green run).

Evidence: `go test ./internal/api ./internal/syncer ./cmd/mailsense` pass and
`scripts/test-fast.sh` reports all fast checks passed (9 vet configs, 87
packages, sidecar, `-race qa+api`). No wire shape changed.

Residual risk: `StartPicked` still reads `MailboxViews` once to map the
selection to sources right after a pick. Passing it the same snapshot would
remove that read too, but it changes a second public method used by the
automatic sync path and its tests, so it is a separate round. The returned
slice is the one published on `TopicMailboxes`; every consumer treats it as
read-only, as the previous event payload already had to.

## 2026-11-04 — Every numeric path id answers one 400

The route audit found one drift: `GET /api/logs/{seq}` answered `404
log_not_found` for a malformed sequence (`abc`, `0`, an overflow), while
messages, attachments, triage, answer history and held-removal folders all
answered `400 invalid_id`. A malformed URL was reading as "the entry rotated
away", which is a different statement and a second message for one failure.

- **One parser.** `pathID(r, name)` is now the only reader of a numeric path
  id: not a positive integer is `400 invalid_id` with a message naming the
  parameter. Messages, message attachments, triage results, answer history,
  held-removal folders and log entries all call it; the three ad-hoc parses
  (inline `ParseInt` for history, `ParseInt` for the folder, `ParseUint` for
  the sequence) are gone, and so are their three distinct messages.
- **A real absence keeps its own answer.** A well-formed id that does not
  exist is still the route's own 404 (`log_not_found` for the log ring,
  `unknown_thread`, `not_found`, …). The change is only about malformed
  values.
- Regression: `TestEveryPathIDRouteRefusesAMalformedID` is table-driven over
  all six routes and five malformed values (`abc`, `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, an
  overflowing integer), asserting `400 invalid_id` everywhere;
  `TestLogEntryKeepsItsOwnNotFound` pins the distinct 404. Mutation-checked by
  restoring the old log branch: `status 404, want 400:
  {"error":{"code":"log_not_found",...}}`.
- `docs/API.md` states the rule in the error-contract paragraph and on the log
  entry row.

Residual risk: strings ids (`/api/jobs/{id}`, `/api/settings/{key}`,
`/api/secrets/{name}`, `/api/providers/{id}`, `/api/companies/{key}`) keep
their own not-found answer by design: they are opaque names, so "malformed"
is not defined for them. The message text of `invalid_id` is now uniform
("<name> must be a positive integer"); clients compose from the code, and no
test asserted the old strings.

## 2026-11-04 — A mailbox selection request is bounded

`POST /api/mailboxes/pick` and `/unpick` checked that a key was not empty and
then looped over whatever the body held: with the 1 MiB body cap that is tens
of thousands of keys, each scanned against the discovered set or the current
selection, on a click route. Both now refuse more than `maxMailboxKeys` (256)
keys with `400 invalid_request`, before the service is called. The screen picks
one store per action, so no legitimate client is near the bound; a profile that
listed more stores than that can still pick them in batches.

Evidence: `TestMailboxSelectionBatchIsBounded` drives 257 keys through both
actions (both refused, service never reached) and 256 through `pick` (accepted,
service called once). It builds its server with a 64 KiB body cap so the batch
bound answers before the body bound, the same way the label-batch contract test
does. Mutation-checked by deleting the check: both actions answer `200` and
`an oversized selection reached the service 2 times`. `docs/API.md` now states
`1…256 keys` on both rows. Other array inputs were already bounded
(`MaxLabelBatch` 100, company profiles 16); this was the last unbounded one
reachable from a client.

Residual risk: the bound is a protocol constant, not a setting; a profile with
more than 256 discovered stores would need batched picks, which the current UI
never attempts. `go vet ./internal/api` and `go test ./internal/api
./cmd/mailsense` pass; the full fast gate is re-run with the next UI round
because a frontend agent was editing the bundle at the time.

## 2026-11-04 — The gate is read once, not three times

`GET /api/gate` asked the learning machine three separate questions:
`PreviewAnswers` (which resolves the gate), `Open` (the gate again) and `Allow`
(the gate a third time). On the open path that is three learned-scope latch
reads, each a store meta read, on a route every screen mount can hit; worse, a
learning event landing between the three could answer from three different
states, so the view could claim a preview from a closed gate beside an open
flag from an open one.

- **One reading, three answers.** `learning.Machine.GateState(ctx)` evaluates
  the rule once and derives `Preview` (the setting on a closed gate), `Open`
  (the real gate) and `Allow` (nil under the preview, the typed lock
  otherwise). `GateState.Err` keeps the underlying failure Open would have
  reported, so a broken latch or status read still fails the caller even while
  the preview hides the lock from `Allow`.
- **The route uses it.** `handleGate` builds its `GateView` from one
  `GateState`; `LearningAPI` lost `Open` and the `Previewer` embedding, which
  no handler used any more.
- **The learning screen reads once too.** `LearningAPI.Status` and
  `hub.Learning.Status` now return the status together with the same
  `GateState`, so `/api/learning` no longer resolves the gate twice (once for
  `Open`, once for the preview rule), and the hub cannot paint a status from
  one state beside a gate from another. The production adapter still reports
  `PreviewAnswers` for `previewGate` and the cmd test.
- Regressions: `TestGateStateIsOneConsistentReading` (the four
  setting × gate combinations, one learned-scope read each),
  `TestGateStateKeepsTheRawFailureUnderThePreview` (the preview never hides a
  failed latch), `TestLearningViewReadsTheGateOnce`, plus the existing
  `TestGateAllowsWithoutReadingTheStatus` (the handler still adds no status
  read of its own). Mutation-checked: implementing `GateState` from `Open` +
  `Allow` fails the first with `the gate rule read the learned scope 2 times,
  want 1`.

Residual risk: `GateState` makes the three answers consistent with one rule
evaluation, not with one store transaction; the latch and status reads it
triggers are the same ones the previous three calls used, so no new read
appeared. `docs/API.md` now states the one-reading contract. The deployed build
predates this change; no wire shape changed.

## 2026-11-04 — The API document matches the wire again

Four documented claims had drifted from the code the route audit read. Each is
now the code's own shape:

- **`GET /api/brief`** was documented as `400 invalid_since`; the handler emits
  `invalid_since_time` with `params.name = "since"` (`routes_brief.go:18`).
  The document now names the code the client must map.
- **`GET /api/status`** was documented as carrying learning status ("same

  (`services.go:330-349`) has no learning field and never had one: that read is

  wrong endpoint.
- **`POST /api/ask`** documented three body fields; the handler also accepts
  `route` (`routes_ask.go:15,28`) with `auto`/`local`/`remote`, defaulting to
  `auto`, and rejects an unknown value with `400 invalid_route`
  (`errors.go:270`). It is now documented with that code, and the view's
  returned `route` is named.
- **`LabelQueue`** was documented as `{"question","strategy","tasks"}`; the
  struct also carries `total` and `has_more` (`labels_queue.go:74-82`), the two
  fields the label screen uses so it does not claim a page is the whole queue.

No behaviour changed. Evidence is the code lines above plus
`go test ./internal/commitments -run TestAPIDocsListEveryCommitmentKind` (the one
test that reads this document) and `scripts/test-fast.sh`, which passed after
the earlier code round and is unaffected by prose.

## 2026-11-04 — Three parameter shapes, one owner each

The route-by-route API audit found three places where one parameter could be
refused in two different shapes. The client composes one localized message per
code, so a second shape is a second message to maintain and a second thing to
get wrong.

- **The pre-gate label read applies the queue's limit bound.**
  `GET /api/messages/{id}?for=label` proved queue membership with
  `queryInt`, so `limit` was unbounded on the one path that runs before the
  learning gate; its twin `GET /api/labels/queue` bounds it 0…200. It now
  calls `boundedQueryInt(r, "limit", 0, 0, layer1.LabelQueueMax)`. The
  binding still answers the gate error on any failure, so the caller learns
  nothing beyond "not readable yet". Regression
  `TestPreGateLabelBindingUsesTheQueueLimitBound`: `limit=abc`, `-1` and
  `201` neither reach the queue owner nor open the message, and `200` still
  does both. Mutation-checked by restoring `queryInt` (the out-of-range read
  returns 200 instead of 423).
- **The agenda horizon answers one way.** `hours` was parsed by `queryFloat`,
  which emitted a bare `invalid_hours` with no params for `abc`/`NaN`/`Inf`,
  while an out-of-range value emitted the ranged shape from `invalidRange`.
  `boundedQueryFloat` now reads it and both paths share one constructor
  (`rangeError`, the string-bound half of `invalidRange`), so every refusal is
  `invalid_hours` with `name`/`min`/`max` and one message. `queryFloat` is
  deleted (one caller). Regression `TestAgendaHoursFailuresAreOneShape` drives
  `abc`, `NaN`, `Inf`, `0`, `-1`, the empty value, `169` and `1000` and
  asserts one identical shape plus that none reached the service; the old
  parser fails it on the params.
- **Both mail boolean filters carry their name.** `counts` refused a bad value
  with no params while `unread` carried `params.name`. They now share
  `invalidBool(name)`, so `invalid_counts` and `invalid_unread` differ only in
  the name they report. Regression
  `TestBooleanFilterErrorsCarryTheirName` (mutation-checked by dropping the
  params).
- `GET /api/ask/history` joined the shared bounds table
  (`TestListQueryBoundsAreOneContract`), so its default/min/max parity with the
  other eleven list routes is now asserted rather than inspected:
  `1…100`, default `20`, one `invalid_limit` shape for malformed and
  out-of-range values.

## 2026-11-04 — One owner for a detached build

- **`safe.Detached` owns "a build that outlives its request".** Three packages
  spelled the same rule by hand: detach from the caller's context
  (`context.WithoutCancel`), bound it by a timeout, cancel it from the
  service's own context (`context.AfterFunc`), and contain a panic. It is now
  one generic helper in `internal/safe` (the package that already owns panic
  containment), and the call sites keep only their own policy:
  - `priority.buildDetached` keeps the resource guard (`admit`) inside the
    same bounded context and its own panic message, and still stops before the
    install, whose rule differs between the cold build and the refresh.
  - `messages.build` passes a nil base: it has no service context to cancel
    through, and its `join.Group` is the shutdown path.
  - `world.refreshList` passes `Background` as the parent (there is no caller
    to detach from; `s.base` is what ends it), which is exactly the previous
    `context.WithTimeout(s.base, …)` plus the panic containment every other
    build already had.
- The one behaviour this adds: a panic inside a company-list refresh now
  keeps the stale list and logs the failure instead of taking the process
  down, matching every other build in the tree.
- Regressions: `TestDetachedBuildOutlivesTheParentContext`,
  `TestDetachedBuildIsBoundedByTheTimeout`,
  `TestDetachedBuildEndsWithTheBaseContext`,
  `TestDetachedBuildTurnsAPanicIntoAnError`. Mutation-checked: replacing
  `WithoutCancel(parent)` with `parent` fails the helper's own test plus
  `TestFirstPageWaiterSurvivesLeaderCancel` and
  `TestFirstPageBuildIsJoinableAfterTheLeaderLeft` in `messages`.

Residual risk: `priority`'s file stayed under its reviewed line budget by
compacting the extracted function (1554 lines vs the 1558 ceiling). The
deployed build predates this refactor; it is tests-plus-internal-plumbing and
no wire behaviour changed.

## 2026-11-04 — The first-page cache stays separate, with the reason pinned

- **`messages`' first-page cache is not a duplicate of `viewcache`.** The audit
  item is closed as "must stay", with a test for each policy rather than an
  assertion. Three behaviours cannot be expressed by the shared cache:
  - **the first build is detached from the caller that started it.** A leader
    walking away must not abort the read for the callers who joined, and a
    caller arriving after the leader left must still join that build. New
    regression `TestFirstPageBuildIsJoinableAfterTheLeaderLeft` (the caller
    arrives only after the cancellation, waits on the shared build, and the
    store is still read once), beside the existing
    `TestFirstPageWaiterSurvivesLeaderCancel`. `viewcache.buildFirst` derives
    from the caller's context, so both would fail there: the build would be
    cancelled and the next caller would pay a second scan or receive the
    cancellation as its answer.
  - **a moved generation is a wait, not a stale serve**
    (`TestFirstPageCacheFollowsMailGeneration`); a `viewcache` entry is served
    stale while the rebuild runs behind it.
  - **each caller gets its own copy**
    (`TestFirstPageCacheReturnsIndependentCopies`); `viewcache` hands every
    caller the same value.
- Mutation-checked: replacing `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` with `ctx` in the
  build fails both detachment tests (`the waiter received the leader's
  cancellation`, `store called 2 times, want the one detached build`). The
  package doc now records the three policies, the tests that pin them, and the
  rule not to fold this into `viewcache` without a second consumer needing the
  same two extra modes.

Residual risk: the detached build still relies on the store honoring its
context for the 2-minute bound; a non-cooperative read is the one residual the
package's `Close` join already documents. No production logic changed, so the
deployed build is unaffected.

## 2026-11-04 — The company list cache stays separate, with the reason pinned

- **`world`'s list cache is not a duplicate of `viewcache`.** The audit item is
  closed as "must stay", with evidence rather than assertion. Two policies
  `List` depends on cannot be expressed by `viewcache`: it selects by exact
  key, while the list entry serves any request at least as narrow as the one
  built (`entry.limit >= limit`, a prefix of the ranking); and its `Keep`
  rejects an install whose generation moved, while `refreshList` deliberately
  installs a completed scan under the generation it sampled and refreshes

  request path; a generation in `Keep` would discard the raced scan.

  viewcache" rule, and two caller-visible tests pin them:
  `TestListServesOnlyASnapshotAtLeastAsWide` and
  `TestListServesTheRacedRebuildAndRefreshesBehind` (mutation-checked against

## 2026-11-03 — One rebuild per stale generation (the conversations flake, fixed)

- **A stale view cache could run two whole rebuilds for one write.** `Get`
  leaves the lock to run `Keep` (it reads a store generation) and re-locks
  afterwards. If a detached rebuild finished and installed in that window, the
  re-lock saw `refreshing` already cleared and started a *second* full rebuild
  for the same generation move. Every service on the cache (hub, agenda,
  commitments, brief, conversations, triage pages) could therefore pay twice
  for one sync. The entry now carries an install stamp: `Get` captures it
  before unlocking, and after re-locking it re-reads the entry instead of
  rebuilding when the stamp (or the entry itself) moved.
  - This is the real cause of the `TestPageRepeatedCallScansNothing` failure
    that appeared twice only while two full gates overlapped ("digest reads 3,
    want the warm read plus one rebuild"). The interleaving is timing
    dependent, which is why it never reproduced alone; it is a product defect,
    not test flakiness.
  - Regressions: `TestOneStaleGenerationStartsOneRebuild` (parks a reader
    inside `Keep`, lets the rebuild install, and asserts the reader serves it
    instead of rebuilding; mutation-proven against the old condition) and
    `TestKeepRaceDoesNotServeAReplacedEntry` (an eviction in the same window
    starts over from a fresh entry). `TestPageRepeatedCallScansNothing` now
    passes 50 consecutive runs.

Residual risk: the install stamp is per entry, so an eviction followed by a
rebuild of the same key is a new entry and rebuilds once, as before. Live still
runs the previous build.

## 2026-11-03 — A lost port race is not a broken build, one commitment shape, one triage prologue

- **A transient port collision no longer blacklists a working GPU build.**
  `sidecar` asked the OS for a free loopback port, closed its probe listener,
  then told the runtime to bind that number; another program can take it in
  between. The runtime then exited without answering and
  `launchReady` treated that as a property of the build: it marked the GPU
  build broken *permanently*, and the supervisor cannot recover a broken
  build. This was not theoretical: it failed `scripts/test-fast.sh` twice in
  `TestGPUBuildWithoutRequirementInstallsAndStarts`. The launch now asks
  `portHeld` (the one new platform probe: a listening socket still exists
  after our child is gone) and, only for that case, retries with a fresh port
  up to `launchAttempts` (3). A build that fails for its own reason leaves its
  port free, so it still fails on the first attempt. Regressions:
  `TestLaunchRetriesALostPortRace` (GPU shape, mutation-proven: with one
  attempt it reproduces the exact "GPU build marked broken ... address
  already in use" failure), `TestLaunchDoesNotRetryAChildThatFailedOnItsOwn`
  and `TestPortHeldDistinguishesAForeignListener`.
- **One commitment shape for both ranked sources.** `commitments` assembled
  decision items and action items with two near-identical 19-field literals.
  `commitmentFromRanked` now owns the shared fields (counterpart resolution
  included) and both callers pass only the kind. The merge proved no field
  was being dropped: the two literals were identical in every source-derived
  field, so this is a strict simplification with identical output.
  Regression: `TestRankedSourcesBuildOneSharedCommitmentShape` (declared
  organization, shared domain, no book, sender-name fallback) with a
  drop-a-field mutation check.
- **One triage prologue.** Three duplicated blocks became one helper each:
  `startScope` (prepare, store check, decision scope, eligible count) for the
  full and pending plans, `loadRouteAnswers` (records, previews, failures, in
  that order and with the same error text) for the routed read and the routed
  page, and `configuredRouteKey` for the route-key guard (the third copy).
  Regressions: `TestRoutedReadAndPageAgreeOnFailureAndCoverage`,
  `TestBothPlansRefuseTheSameUnpickedStore`.

Residual risk: the port retry is bounded at 3 attempts; a machine where three
consecutive ports are taken reports the original start failure. On a platform
other than linux/windows `portHeld` reports "not held", so the retry never
fires there (unchanged behaviour). Live still runs the previous build.

## 2026-11-03 — Backfill index, dead indexes removed, one language predicate

- **The display backfill is an index range read.** `migrations/0037_index_round.sql`
  adds `messages_backfill(source_id, instant DESC, id DESC) WHERE body_html_known = 0

  the candidate predicate and the newest-first order. `instantSortSQL` no
  longer wraps the column in `COALESCE(NULLIF(...))`: `instant` is
  `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` and an empty string is already the smallest value, so
  a plain `DESC` keeps absent instants last while staying a column the index
  can order by. Measured on a 33,842-message snapshot the page read was

  `TestBackfillOrdersAbsentInstantLast`.

  (no consumer, and it could not serve the backfill's `OR` plus ordering),
  `messages_internet_id` (superseded by `messages_survivor`),
  `qa_history_id_desc` (duplicates the primary-key B-tree),
  `contacts_name`, `calendars_store`, `calendar_events_global` and
  `event_attendees_norm` (each read by a different key). Every drop was
  proved by searching the tree for the index name and for a predicate it
  could serve; the migration comment records the proof.

  "which validated language selects the French copy", replacing nine literal
  `language == "fr"` comparisons across `ask.go` and `entity.go`. The
  validator already admits only `LanguageEN`/`LanguageFR`, so the constant
  and the branch can no longer drift apart.
- **Grouped citation markers are split, not lost.** Models often write
  `[1, 2]`; `answerMarker` now accepts a comma or semicolon list and
  `groundAnswer` rewrites it to one marker per index, so each source becomes
  a chip the UI can open instead of literal prose. One invalid index in a
  grouped marker still refuses the whole answer, and a range stays prose
  because the prompts never ask for one. Regressions:
  `TestGroundAnswerSplitsGroupedMarkers` (with a mutation check).
- **A deadline comment no longer names a vendor model.** The per-kind
  deadline table quoted a provider preset in a comment, which
  `internal/engine`'s vendor-secret scan refuses; the justification keeps its
  measured time without the name.

Residual risk: none of these are deployed; live still runs the previous
build and its CPU ceiling stays at 100 until the fixed build deploys. The
index migration rebuilds the backfill index on a 34k-message table (seconds)
and the drops free space that `auto_vacuum=NONE` will not reclaim in place.

## 2026-11-03 — Detached rebuilds joined, failed jobs explained, sync on demand

- **Every detached read-model rebuild is now joined before the store
  closes.** `join.Group` is the one bounded-join owner. `messages.Service`
  gained a `jobs join.Group` (the first-page build is detached from the
  click that started it) and `Close(ctx) bool`; `triage.Triager` gained a
  `Close` joining its page and summary caches. `agenda` had a detached
  cache but **no closer at all**, so it was silently absent from shutdown.
  The one list now lives in `readModelCloserList`, beside the adapters, and
  a missed closer reports a miss so the store stays open. Regressions:
  `TestCloseJoinsTheDetachedFirstPageBuild`,
  `TestReadModelCloserListJoinsEveryOwner`.
- **A failed job names its cause and stays.** `shell.job.failed_with_reason`
  (EN/FR) shows the producer's redacted error, bounded at 200 runes: a
  provider failure can carry a multi-kilobyte URL. `jobLinger` returns no
  expiry for failures, and the strip no longer schedules a
  `setTimeout(Infinity)` that would fire at once. `.job-strip` is bounded
  and scrolls, so a long reason can never squeeze the route out of the
  window. Regressions: `TestFailedJobShowsItsReasonAndStays`, the `live`
  job-strip spec.
- **Sources has the manual "Sync now" the copy promised.** `syncNowButton`
  posts `/api/actions/sync` for the selected source, so a picked mailbox
  whose first sync failed can be retried with `sync.auto` off. EN/FR copy.
- **A connector's actionable cause survives to the screen.**
  `source.Cause(err)` returns a stable code plus the connector's message;
  `UnavailableCause` tags each Outlook precondition
  (`outlook_not_running`, `outlook_session_lost`, `outlook_busy`, …). The
  API sends `params.cause`/`params.reason`, and the UI translates the code
  (`api.source_cause.*`) so French never leaks an English sentence.
  Regressions: `TestCauseReturnsTheConnectorReason`,
  `TestSourceUnavailableKeepsTheActionableCause`.
- **A malformed providers file is fixable from the screen.** The provider
  panel lists every `invalid_provider` problem instead of offering only a
  retry that cannot repair a hand-edited file. Regression:
  `TestProviderLoadShowsTheFileProblems`.
- **Long unbreakable error text cannot break the layout.** The Logs banner
  row is a bounded scroller with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, and the job and
  boot strips are bounded: the giant evidence/download URL in a health
  banner used to grow `#main` from 63 px to 226 px at 1280 px. Regressed by
  the `boot` scroll specs.
- **Fixtures no longer depend on the developer's disk.** The e2e fixture
  server sets `MAILSENSE_RESOURCE_GUARD=false`: the ceilings are host-wide
  readings, and a 98% full development disk made the content routes answer
  `423 resource_limit`, which is not what any UI spec asserts.
- **Per-kind job deadlines** (jobs round): `kindDeadlines` bounds evidence
  and layer1 at 30m, triage at 60m, index at 90m, `labels.judge` at 30m,
  `sidecar.install` at 2h and `messages.html` at 6h, each with the measured
  evidence in a comment; `sync` stays unbounded through `StartEssential`.
  Expiry reuses `runstate` (`Cancelled`), clears `Paused`, releases the
  `Single` slot and publishes once. Regressions: `TestDeadline*`.
- **Verified this round:** `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`,
  `go test ./cmd/mailsense ./internal/messages ./internal/triage
  ./internal/viewcache ./internal/agenda ./internal/jobs ./internal/store
  ./internal/qa ./internal/layer1 ./internal/judge ./internal/ui
  -count=1`, and `scripts/test-ui.sh` (167/167).

## 2026-11-03 — Traceable answers, honest recovery, and bounded workers

- **Q&A answers follow route commits.** `qa.Store` gained
  `RouteGeneration()`, and `answerCacheKey` carries it beside the mail
  generation. A layer-1 re-score rewrites the certified route answers a
  freeform answer cites without touching mail or labels; the cache no
  longer serves the old classification for its TTL. Regression:
  `TestAnswerCacheInvalidatesOnRouteGeneration`.
- **The production judge answer is never a learned fact.**
  `store.labelPrecedenceSQL` now ranks manual, judge, then
  `judge_answer`, and `labelContextSQL` keeps only the reference sources
  in the `ContextDetails` read. A `judge_answer` is audit data written by
  the model about itself; it never becomes a prior shown next to a
  message. Regressions: `TestContextDetailsOmitsProductionAnswer`,
  `TestSQLVocabularyMatchesDomainConstants`.
- **Priority ignores answers from an older revision.** The priority scan
  selects `ra.revision` and `rp.revision` and drops a route or preview
  answer whose revision differs from the message's, instead of ranking
  an edited message on its old classification. The block decoder is
  unchanged otherwise. Regression:
  `TestPriorityIgnoresAnswersFromAnOlderRevision`.
- **Routed triage reads keep failures.** `readRoute` and `buildPage` load
  `triage_failures` for their window, so a message whose last attempt
  failed and has no route row is counted and shown as failed, matching
  the header summary. Regression: `TestRoutedReadKeepsFailure`.
- **Held removals render their real deadline.** `store.HeldFolder`
  carries `applies_at`, computed in `cmd/mailsense` from
  `sync.removal.auto_apply_after` (empty when confirm-only). The Sources
  card stops promising that held messages stay when the default applies
  them after 72 hours; EN/FR copy states the deadline. Regression:
  `TestHeldAppliesAtFollowsTheSyncPolicy`, held wire test.
- **A failed window is never silent.** `runWithShutdownUI` reports the
  WebView2 failure natively and opens the same bootstrap URL in the
  default browser, so a Windows machine without the runtime is not left
  with a headless process. Regression:
  `TestAFailedWindowReportsAndFallsBack`.
- **A corrupt settings file names its recovery.** The startup report
  names `settings.json` and states that the mail database is untouched,
  instead of only "invalid configuration". Regression included in
  `TestRunReportsEveryStartupFailure`.
- **The install-profile worker joins under the app's shutdown bound.**
  `AfterSync` now cancels without blocking and returns a `done` channel;
  `cmd/mailsense` joins it with the one `shutdownJoinTimeout`, and a miss
  marks the run unjoined so the store and lock stay open. Regression:
  `TestStopWorkerReportsAnUnjoinedWorker`, trigger join tests.
- **Verified this round:** `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`,
  `go test ./internal/store ./internal/priority ./internal/triage
  ./internal/qa ./internal/api ./internal/installprofile
  ./internal/sidecar ./internal/index ./internal/threadintel
  ./internal/search ./internal/learning ./internal/syncer
  ./cmd/mailsense ./internal/ui -count=1` all green.

## 2026-11-03 — Bounded queries, correct event instants, and confirmed held removals

- **One query ceiling.** `search.query_max_chars` (default 512, 32–8192)
  is enforced at `search.Search`, the choke point shared by the search box
  and free-form retrieval. A longer query returns HTTP 422
  `query_too_long` with the configured maximum; EN/FR copy says how long
  the search may be. The QA ingress already had its own 500-rune bound, so
  no duplicate cap was added there.
- **One gzip writer pool.** `httpgzip.Compress` reuses its 32 KiB writer
  through a `sync.Pool`; concurrent responses round-trip independently.
- **Index cleanup (migration 0035).** `messages_sender` (the raw address
  index no query reads) is dropped, and `messages_survivor`
  `(source_id, store_id, internet_message_id)` now covers the move-survivor
  join. Every insert no longer maintains an unused index.
- **Calendar event instants use the host zone.** Built-in Outlook dates
  (`AppointmentItem.Start`/`End`) are local wall clock; `Date.LocalInstant`
  interprets them in `time.Local` with the correct per-date DST offset
  before storing UTC. Schema-name dates and mail dates are untouched, and
  recurrence enumeration stays wall-clock. Unit regressions cover UTC-5
  and both 2026 Toronto DST changes.
- **Sync snapshots keep only absent ids.** `batchSink.Snapshot` computes
  the absent candidates while the presence set is in hand, and the run
  retains only those ids plus the stored count. The former per-folder
  presence maps are gone: a 100k-message measurement drops retained
  presence from **15.55 MiB to 0.78 MiB worst case** (about **95 %**), and
  the one-run move hold, mass valve and incomplete-snapshot behavior are
  unchanged.
- **Priority builds retain one record per row, not three maps.** The
  per-message `signalsByID` and `threadSignals` maps are gone; rows carry
  their decoded signals inline and the resolver view exists only for its
  one call. Measured at 20k rows/4k conversations: scan retention
  **16.1 MB → 8.3 MB (−48 %)**, build allocations **55.4 MB → 32.6 MB
  (−41 %)**. Every conversation state is still retained because agenda and
  commitments enumerate the whole map.
- **Triage probes before planning.** `Store.HasPendingDecisions` is one
  `EXISTS ... LIMIT 1` over the same predicate as the candidate loader.
  A no-work sync now loads **0 decision rows** and builds no per-message
  state; the benchmark records **0 decision-rows/op** on 1,000 decided
  messages. The shared predicate is pinned against `decodeAnswers` with
  16 cases, including extra and malformed answers.
- **Search preparation is single-flight per space.** A burst of search-box
  queries waits on one preparation gate instead of spawning one detached
  vector-refresh worker each; a different space stays independent, and a
  context that ends while another prepares degrades normally.
- **Held removals can be confirmed.** The existing
  `Syncer.ConfirmRemovals` now has production callers:
  `GET /api/held-removals` and `POST /api/held-removals/{folder}/confirm`.
  Sources shows a card only when a folder has held removals, names the
  count and path, asks for a destructive confirmation, posts the folder,
  invalidates only mail-derived reads plus the held list, and moves focus
  to the next row. EN/FR copy covers the card, dialog, result and read
  failure.
- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103212103`.** Live boot **9.197 s**, 12/12
  views, migration **0035_message_survivor.sql** applied, resources CPU
  **15.2 %**, RAM **44 %**, disk **75.9 %** against 80/85/90. A 600-char
  search returned **422 `query_too_long`** with `max=512`; a normal search
  returned **20 hits**. `GET /api/held-removals` returned an empty array.
  The post-restart calendar log has **0** `calendar: series unreadable`
  and **0** `calendar: series skipped`.
- **Guards:** fast gate green; full UI suite **153/153**.
- **Open:** the hub was still in its post-restart first sync
  (`running:true`, `stale:true`) at the verification instant. Stored
  calendar events remain shifted until the next calendar sync replaces
  that window. The live held-removal path is wired and tested, but the
  live mailbox currently has no held folder, so the destructive action
  was not exercised against real data. Startup warm sharing, company
  invalidation scans, FTS count scans, layer-1 design-matrix memory and
  the FTS reindex-at-startup path remain.

## 2026-11-03 — Idle learning status stops re-planning the whole index

- **One cached coverage key.** `internal/index` now separates the collecting
  plan (`Run`, `Ensure`) from the coverage-only path (`Coverage`,
  `Stage.Status`). The coverage cache is one entry keyed by the vector space,
  the text version, `Store.MailGeneration()`, the new
  `Store.EmbeddingGeneration()`, the covered folder roles, the picked store
  keys and the quarantine threshold. The key is read before the database
  read, so a write landing during the read is not cached under the old key.
- **Embedding writes own their generation.** `SaveEmbeddings`,
  `ConfirmEmbeddings` and `RecordIndexFailures` bump
  `Store.EmbeddingGeneration()` after commit. Coverage therefore refreshes
  after a save, a confirmation, a quarantine change, a text-version change,
  a role/selection change or a mail write, and is reused when none changed.

## 2026-11-03 — Resource ceilings, coalesced mail generations, and a working recurrence path

- **Resource ceilings are owner settings and one guard.** Five settings under
  `Resources`: `resource.guard` (default on), `resource.cpu.max_percent` (80),
  `resource.ram.max_percent` (85), `resource.disk.max_percent` (90) and
  `resource.sample_interval` (2s). `internal/resource` owns the host readings
  (Linux procfs/statfs, Windows `GetSystemTimes`,
  `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, `GetDiskFreeSpaceEx`) and the hysteresis: work
  pauses above a ceiling and resumes three points below it, so it cannot
  flap. `jobs.Manager` is the one admission and pacing choke point: a start
  above a ceiling is refused with a typed error, and a running job pauses
  between progress reports. Readings are host-wide; 100 disables one
  ceiling. The job record carries `paused` with the resource, percent and
  limit, so the one aggregate strip names the ceiling instead of looking
  hung.
- **The API and UI speak the ceiling.** `GET /api/status` now carries
  `resources` (usage, limits, paused); a refused start is HTTP 503
  `resource_limit` with `{resource, percent, limit}`. EN/FR copy names the
  resource with the right article and says work resumes automatically. The
  settings screen renders the five rows from the schema with localized
  descriptions.
- **Mail writes invalidate derived views once per boundary.** `Store` now
  has `HoldMailWrites`: a folder sync and a detail pass each hold the mail
  generation and bump it once at the end, instead of once per 500-message or
  50-detail batch. Selection, identity, source and world writes are never
  held. A 50k-message initial sync now invalidates the priority, company,
  search and view caches once per folder and once per detail pass.
- **Recurring calendar series are expanded with the real Outlook member.**
  The connector no longer calls the non-existent
  `RecurrencePattern.GetOccurrences`; it reads the pattern once per master,
  computes occurrence dates locally, and calls `GetOccurrence(DateTime)` per
  candidate. Daily, weekly, monthly, monthly-nth, yearly and yearly-nth
  patterns are supported, with end dates, counts, moved/cancelled/deleted
  instances, a 2,000-candidate cap and one bounded warning per skipped
  series. The fake now mirrors the real object model, and a regression test
  fails if `GetOccurrences` returns.
- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103204648`.** Live boot **9.427 s**, 12/12
  views. `resources` reports CPU **18.2 %**, RAM **44 %**, disk **75.9 %**
  against limits 80/85/90; all five settings are served. Setting the disk
  ceiling to 50 % while the volume was 75.9 % used made a sync start return
  **503 `resource_limit`** with
  `{"resource":"disk","percent":"76","limit":"50"}`. Resetting to 90 %
  started `job-2`, which finished; the hub is `synced:true`,
  `running:false`, newest message **2026-11-03T20:01:12Z**. The log after
  the restart has **0** `calendar: series unreadable` lines and **0**
  `0x80020006` codes, against **300** in the pre-deploy window; the world
  sync reads its calendar with 16 events.
- **Guards:** fast gate green; full UI suite **150/150** (the two new
  paused-job and Resources-group specs included).
- **Next:** the index coverage cache round is implemented and green on its
  own (one cached coverage keyed by space, text version, mail and embedding
  generations, roles, stores and quarantine); it still needs the combined
  gate and deploy. The pre-existing `calTime` local-to-UTC bug remains: on a
  non-UTC host, stored event instants are shifted. H2 (sync snapshot
  memory), the triage decision probe and priority row retention are open.

- **One aggregate job bar.** `#job-strip` now renders exactly one

## 2026-11-03 — Folded contact filters and label caches that follow visibility

- **Contact filters now use the canonical comparison form.** Both the
  contact aggregate and the message/time contact filter built `LIKE
  '%term%'` with ASCII `lower()`. They now use `mailsense_fold` and
  `instr()` over the stored normalized address and the folded name, so
  “emile” matches “ÉMILE.DUPONT@EXEMPLE.CA”, while `%` and `_` in a name
  stay literal instead of becoming wildcards. A regression covers accented
  senders, a literal percent sign, a literal underscore, and a lone `%`
  that must not select every row.
- **Label caches now follow the visible population.** `LabelGeneration`
  counts label writes and the changes that can move a label out of view:
  the mailbox selection, scope verdicts, message removals, folder
  activation and folder discovery. Ordinary mail writes still leave it
  alone, so a sync does not rebuild the label view. The accessor applies a
  pending selection before returning, which fixes the race where the first
  label build bumped its own cache key and invalidated the value it had
  just built. `TestVisibilityChangesAdvanceLabelGeneration` pins the
  category; the hub cache-after-close and stale-while-refresh tests pass.

## 2026-11-03 — One invalidation graph, one discovery pass, consolidated store owners

- **The UI now has one invalidation graph.** `INVALIDATION_TOPICS` in
  `internal/ui/js/13-shell.js` declares each topic's read prefixes, stale
  routes and refresh routes. `invalidateTopics` derives cache invalidation,
  route stales, warm-cache clears, All-Mail forgetting and question-catalogue
  resets from that graph. `feedback.label`, `afterLabelWrite`,
  `index.finished`, `sync.finished`, `triage.finished`, `evidence.finished`,
  `layer1.finished`, `sync.mailboxes`, `jobs.update`, `config.changed` and
  `sidecar.state` all go through it; the per-event read lists are gone.
  Labels no longer stale Brief, Companies, Priority, Conversations,
  Commitments, Threads, Triage or Questions. `index.finished` invalidates
  Search (and learning/hub only when `Report.Committed()`), not Mail.
- **Warm caches clear at their choke point.** Invalidating `/api/companies`
  now clears `companyProfileWarm` beside the priority, triage and
  conversation clears in `11-http.js`, so a sync or triage cannot paint a
  profile up to 20 s old. Labels stale the Answers route as well as its HTTP
  entries.
- **Route invalidation matches Mail surfaces.** Cached route entries carry
  their Mail surface, so `search`, `priority`, `triage` and `conversations`
  target the cached tab they actually own.
- **Steady-state sync no longer pays discovery every minute.**
  `sync.discovery.interval` (default 10m, 1m to 6h) bounds a fresh folder
  discovery. The first pass after restart and every manual sync still
  discover; later automatic mail passes reuse the stored active folders.
  A failed stored folder read invalidates the cache so the next pass

  folders and took **0.48s**, with `mailboxes discovered` absent.
