## 2026-11-03 — Ask correctness and voice: prose answers, real message reads, honest provider states, no dash copy

- **The raw JSON answer had one cause.** The Remote route passed the
  model's whole content to `groundAnswer`. A model that answered
  `{"answer":"…","citations":[…]}` was stored and rendered as that JSON.
  `unwrapAnswerEnvelope` is now the one parser for a fresh generation and a
  legacy history row: plain text is unchanged, a JSON envelope is unwrapped
  to `answer`, and JSON without a usable answer is never shown as prose.
  The prompt now forbids JSON, quotes, code fences, em dashes and double
  hyphens, and asks for short sentence-case sentences.
- **Live proof.** Asking “dois-moi plus sur les messages que j'ai reçu
  aujourd'hui” on the remote route returned clean French prose with 5
  citations (29 messages that day). The earlier raw row, id 250, now reads
  back as the same prose through `/api/ask/history/250`.
- **A failed message read can no longer paint a stub.** Only a valid
  `MessageView` decides the detail; triage alone never does. 404 and 410
  show one removed-message state, other failures show an inline retry,
  a 2xx GET with a `null` body is rejected as `invalid_response`, and the
  conversation and Answers panes use the same rule. `sync.finished` now
  invalidates the hub even when a run wrote no mail.
- **Provider availability is key-aware.** `/api/providers` roles gained
  `available` (record exists, kind matches and the key is present). Ask now
  distinguishes available, unconfigured, unavailable and unknown; a failed
  provider read is unknown, never “not configured”. Remote is enabled only
  for available, and the notice explains a missing record or key.
- **Copy is quieter and clearer.** The saved-answer line now reads
  “Ancienne réponse. Votre prochain message démarre une nouvelle
  conversation.” (EN: “Earlier answer…”). It says what the answer is and
  what the next send does. All em dashes and double hyphens left both
  catalogs, sentence case is used, and temporary value placeholders read
  “Non défini” / “Not set”. A catalog test prevents the dash style from
  returning.
- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103192919`** (answer envelope and failed-read
  fixes) and **`0.1.0-dev+20261103193439`** (provider states and copy).
  Live boot **8.78 s**, 12/12 views, `qa.provider` configured and
  available, auto-fetch running. Served assets contain `readAnswerProvider`
  and “Ancienne réponse”; the French catalog has no em dash.
- **Guards:** fast gate green; full UI suite **139/139**; Ask e2e
  **15/15**; focused QA, UI, API and provider tests.
- **Open:** cache invalidation is still a set of ad-hoc read lists; the
  next round consolidates it into one topic graph. Auto-sync still pays a
  full Outlook discovery per run; the discovery-probe round is next.

## 2026-11-03 — Automatic mail fetching: one scheduler, honest sync truth, mail-only steady state

- **The live app was not stale because Outlook was broken.** A manual sync
  completed at 18:57 and fetched 168 details; the newest message moved from
  Oct 29 to **2026-11-03T18:56Z**. The app had no production sync scheduler:
  boot only discovered mailboxes, and `hub.mailbox.synced` came from the
  learning stage, so it kept claiming “synced” while nothing fetched.
- **One automatic-fetch owner.** `internal/syncer/scheduler.go` starts the
  picked sources once after the startup warm, waits for every started run to
  finish, then rests `sync.auto.interval` before the next check. It never
  overlaps a run (the source claim remains the single-flight guard), skips
  while busy, and joins on shutdown. `sync.auto` (default true) and
  `sync.auto.interval` (default 1m, 15s–1h) live in the Sync settings group.
- **First pass full, steady state mail-only.** The first pass after a restart
  also refreshes calendars and address books; later passes call
  `StartPickedMail`, so polling new mail does not re-read the world model.
  Manual syncs and mailbox picks remain full passes.
- **`synced` is run truth.** `syncer.Status` records per-source attempt,
  success, state, error and partial failure. `hub.mailbox` now exposes
  `synced`, `running`, `stale`, `last_attempt`, `last_success`,
  `newest_message` and `sync_error`; a boot with no run is stale, a failed
  run clears synced while keeping the last success, and a run in progress
  keeps the previous success until it fails. The Home rail shows
  “Syncing…”, “Last sync … · Newest …”, and refreshes the hub on every
  `sync.finished`, including a failed run that wrote no mail.
- **Deployed** `0.1.0-dev+20261103190511` (scheduler), `+20261103190951`
  (mail-only steady state), `+20261103191440` (wait-for-completion).
- **Live proof.** The first automatic sync succeeded at 19:08:26 with no
  manual action; the next automatic cycle started at 19:08:54; after the
  next restart the automatic full pass succeeded at 19:13:04. `/api/hub`
  then reported `synced:true`, `stale:false`, `last_success` set, and the
  newest stored message **2026-11-03T19:11:16Z** — mail that arrived while
  the app was running. The mail-only build booted in **9.43 s** (priority
  6.66 s); the wait-for-completion build booted in **12.4 s** on a cold
  priority rebuild (priority 8.2 s), 12/12 views, RSS **366.5 MB** working /
  **399.9 MB** private at 19:15.
- **Guards:** fast gate green; full UI suite **136/136**; focused
  syncer/hub/store tests for status, scheduler stop, mail-only world skip,
  newest-received query and hub sync truth.
- **Open:** each run still pays a full Outlook discovery (~388 COM calls /
  ~25 s for 19 folders) and the first post-restart pass pays the world sync
  (~2m40s). The next efficiency round should add a discovery TTL plus a
  stored-folder change probe, and gate removals to discovery passes; that
  removes the unrelated store/identity/hierarchy work from polling. The
  `hub.mailbox.synced` field is false during the first run after a restart
  until that run succeeds (honest, not a regression).

## 2026-11-03 — Provider failures: a remote 500 stops the run, embedders honor retry overrides

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103175302`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **9.53 s**
  (priority 6.57 s, home 2.86 s, companies 2.55 s, learning 2.32 s,
  triage summary 1.96 s, triage page 1.63 s, semantic 1.20 s,
  conversations 0.70 s, mail 0.37 s, commitments 0.026 s, brief 0.012 s,
  agenda 0.000 s). RSS **770.5 MB** (private 789 MB), 39 threads. Hub
  still reports 1/17 certified; no errors after deploy.
- **Remote 500 fan-out fixed at the classifier.** A remote embed
  provider’s 5xx (and an unreadable response body) is now
  `ErrTransient`; the index stops after one request instead of
  re-embedding the batch one message at a time. A managed runtime’s 500
  stays `ErrServer` (llama-server’s oversize-input signal), so the
  intentional local split remains. `engine.Classify` maps a remote chat
  500 to `ErrTransient`; triage stops once as `provider_transient`
  instead of charging one failure per message.
- **Embedders honor their retry overrides.** The embed adapter now
  installs `httpx.WithPolicy(ctx, a.adjustPolicy)`, so
  `Retry.MaxAttempts`, `Retry.Statuses` and `Retry.QuotaCodes` on an
  embedder record are no longer silently ignored.
- **Failing-before evidence.** Remote-500 test: **6 calls / 4 failures /
  not stopped** before → **1 call / 0 failures / `provider_transient`**
  after. Triage real-500 test: **5 failures / 10 Decide calls** before →
  **1 failure / stopped** after. Embed retry override: a 529-then-200
  server makes 2 calls with `Statuses=[429,529]`; a persistent 503 with
  `MaxAttempts=1` makes 1 call. The existing 500-as-oversize tests moved
  to a managed-runtime record and still pin the local split.
- **Guards:** `go test ./internal/engine/... ./internal/index
  ./internal/triage`, race on embed/index/triage, gofmt/vet clean; full
  gate **133/133** UI.
- **Open:** a managed-runtime 500 still splits locally (intentional); a
  remote input-specific 500 now stalls the run instead of quarantining
  that input; embed quota 429 still needs a quota-aware class; generate
  transport/read failures remain `ErrHTTP` (pre-existing); 501/505/529
  remain `ErrHTTP` for chat.

## 2026-11-03 — Layer 1: route gates are chosen on out-of-fold predictions

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103174225`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **9.01 s**
  (priority 6.21 s, home 2.89 s, companies 2.54 s, learning 2.34 s,
  triage summary 1.88 s, triage page 1.39 s, semantic 1.39 s,
  conversations 0.69 s, mail 0.55 s, commitments 0.029 s, brief 0.015 s,
  agenda 0.000 s). RSS **757.0 MB** (private 777.8 MB), 39 threads.
- **Defect.** The layer-1 solo threshold was chosen on `Holdout.Select`
  (out-of-fold), but `trainedParticipants` supplied the route gate and
  member selection with `tr.predictWith(s.model, id)` — the **final**
  model, which trained on the selection labels. The cascade was then
  tested once on the honest certification part, so selection was
  optimistic.
- **Fix.** Selection items now offer only `s.model.Holdout.Select`
  (out-of-fold); a selection label with no OOF entry offers no layer-1
  offer (no in-sample fallback). Certification items keep the final model,
  and the commit/answering path keeps the stored/final offer. The
  ID→OOF map is built once per question/route build. `route.Build`,
  thresholds, `selective.Certify`, key/SubQ offers, route keys, wire and
  caches are unchanged.
- **Guards.** `TestSelectionOffersUseOutOfFoldPredictions` (plumbing:
  selection OOF, certification final, missing OOF → no layer 1),
  `TestRouteItemsSelectLayer1OnOutOfFoldPredictions` (fails before the
  fix on selection label 4: final 0.99958 vs OOF 0.98966), and
  `TestRouteGatesFollowOutOfFoldNotAnOverconfidentFinalModel` (forced
  final 0.99/correct, OOF 0.6/wrong; the layer-1 member disappears after
  the fix). Full gate **133/133** UI; the existing route certification,
  coverage, leakage, and re-score tests stay green.
- **Measurement limitation, stated honestly.** The fixture/gold harness
  evaluates the dev split, where the final model is already out-of-sample
  and the changed route path is not exercised; it cannot produce a
  before/after for this change. The live routes remain run 101 (1/17
  certified: `suspicious` 0.9817; the other 16 routes 0.804–0.969, all
  answering false) until the next layer-1 commit. **No live precision
  gain is claimed this round.**
- **Open:** coverage may fall (selection labels without OOF no longer
  offer layer 1); calibration is still fitted on the same OOF
  predictions; a kept active model with a partial holdout omits layer 1
  on those rows until retrained.

## 2026-11-03 — Companies cache: compact pair facts and interned contacts

- **What changed.** The counterpart population no longer repeats facts on
  every pair. `counterpartMessage` owns `conversationID` and `instant`;
  `counterpartContact` interns each exact `(address, norm)` pair and
  `Names` interns each exact display name; `counterpartPair` is three
  `int32` indices plus the direction (96 → 16 bytes). Index 0 is the empty
  contact and the empty name, indices are append-only, and `Messages`,
  `Pairs`, `Contacts`, `Names` are preallocated and clipped after the
  build. `companyPairMatches`, `cachedCounterpartRows` and the cached
  `queryCompanies` fold rebuild the same row values from the message and
  the intern tables; the SQL fallback and `sqlCounterpartRows` are
  unchanged. No cache key, single-flight, install-only-if-generation-
  matches, error, `Close`, window or filter semantics changed, and no
  aggregate or resolved org key is cached.
- **Measured** (`BenchmarkCompanyCounterparts`, prepared 33,842-message
  fixture: 33,410 messages / 41,912 pairs / 2,513 contacts / 2,016 names,
  `-benchtime=1x -count=3`): **81.4 → 67.0 MB/op** (−14.4 MB, −17.7%),
  1,422.2k allocs/op unchanged (the one SQL scan still allocates its
  strings), 238–266 → 238–260 ms/op (within noise). Retained struct
  arrays fall 8.8 → 6.1 MB and the ~3 MB of duplicated per-pair
  address/name string bodies disappear; the remaining per-pair cost is
  16 bytes.
- **Verified.** Parity tests unchanged and green:
  `TestCompanyQueryCacheMatchesSQLFilters` (14 plans plus the Text
  fallback) and `TestCompanyProfilesMatchTheOrderedQuery` (all time,
  October, narrow, empty forward window); the one-build-per-generation,
  stale-build and single-flight tests pass. New
  `TestCompanyCounterpartsInternsContactsAndNames` covers exact-triple
  sharing (received and sent), name variants, exact address spellings and
  the empty sentinels; `TestCounterpartPairStaysCompact` pins 16 and 144
  bytes. `go test ./internal/store ./internal/world ./internal/qa
  ./internal/api ./cmd/mailsense -count=1`, `go test -race
  ./internal/store`, gofmt and vet are clean.
- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103170939`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **9.53 s**
  (priority 6.57 s, home 3.08 s, companies 2.74 s, learning 2.46 s,
  triage summary 1.74 s, triage page 1.43 s, semantic 1.43 s,
  conversations 0.77 s, mail 0.33 s, commitments 0.026 s, brief 0.011 s,
  agenda 0.000 s). RSS **765.5 MB** (private 784 MB), 39 threads: the
  compact layout recovered **21.4 MB** from the 786.9 MB first cache
  build while keeping the boot win.
- **Open issue.** `slices.Clip` bounds `cap` but does not reallocate, so
  the grown backing arrays keep their slack (≈0.5 MB on this fixture by
  Go's 1.25× growth; not released). The remaining +72 MB over the
  693.4 MB pre-cache baseline is mostly one-time build garbage retained
  by the runtime's heap goal; a first-build memory release is the next
  resource option, not a correctness issue.

## 2026-11-03 — Companies: one counterpart scan per mail generation

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103165259`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **10.03 s**
  (priority 6.91 s, home 2.93 s, **companies 2.69 s**, learning 2.37 s,
  triage summary 2.00 s, triage page 1.67 s, semantic 1.22 s,
  conversations 0.74 s, mail 0.58 s, commitments 0.025 s, brief 0.018 s,
  agenda 0.000 s). RSS **786.9 MB** (private 805.5 MB), 38 threads.
- **Root cause.** `world.List` and `world.Profiles(3)` each scanned the
  whole counterpart population through `counterpartCTE`. The profile scan
  repeated the list scan plus a `JOIN messages` for subject/sender/
  attachments, then discarded every organization outside the requested
  three.
- **Fix.** `Store.CompanyCounterparts` is one all-time `DirectionBoth`
  fact population per `MailGeneration` + `cfg.Snapshot()`, built with the
  same single-flight, detached 2-minute bounded build as `CompanyBook`,
  and installed only if the key still matches. It stores message identity
  components + DB id, subject/sender/attachments/read state, and one pair
  per message/address/direction. Resolution stays with `CompanyBook`; no
  org keys or aggregates are cached. `Close` releases the population.
- **Shared folds.** `queryCompanies` folds the cached pairs into the same
  `companyAgg`; a plan with `plan.Text != ""` keeps the SQL fallback
  because body text is not cached. `CompanyProfiles` streams the requested
  window from the cache through `cachedCounterpartRows`; the SQL parity
  oracle uses `sqlCounterpartRows`, and both share
  `foldCompanyProfileRows` / `companyProfilesFromRows`. Every current
  profile accumulator (totals, first/last, months, Activity90, people,
  recent, conversation caps, states/summaries, declared contacts/domains/
  spellings) is preserved.
- **Measured.** Store benchmarks: `BenchmarkCompanyProfile` 315–337 ms →
  77–83 ms; `BenchmarkCompanyProfiles` ~455 ms → 198–224 ms; warm
  `BenchmarkCompanyList` 87 ms, cold 287–353 ms (includes the one-time
  build). Live companies warm **4.57 s → 2.69 s**, boot **11.55 s →
  10.03 s**. Parity tests cover four windows (including empty and
  narrow), 14 filter cases plus the restrictive Text fallback, one build
  per generation, stale-build discard, and single-flight.
- **Cost.** RSS rose **693.4 → 786.9 MB** (+93.5 MB) because the cache
  retains all-time pair facts. This is the next target: move per-message
  facts out of pairs and intern repeated address/name strings.
- **Live proof.** Companies list returns Clinique Exemple / `clinique-exemple.test` with
  949 messages; the profile endpoint returns 949 messages, 274 threads,
  72 people, 2 deadlines; the exact Clinique Exemple Ask question still returns
  generated with 5 citations and no clarify; `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` is free;
  no errors after deploy.

## 2026-11-03 — Store maintenance: the triage-key prune no longer holds the write lock

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103155352`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.63 s**
  (priority 6.71 s, companies 4.87 s, home 3.05 s, learning 2.46 s,
  triage summary 1.96 s, triage page 1.46 s, semantic 1.47 s,
  conversations 0.77 s, mail 0.39 s, commitments 0.029 s, brief 0.022 s,
  agenda 0.003 s). RSS **753 MB** (private 771 MB), 38 threads.
- **Live defect reproduced.** `POST /api/ask` with
  “résume moi les 5 dernières demandes de iso santé” returned HTTP 500
  after ~30 s: `store: save qa history: database is locked (5)
  (SQLITE_BUSY)`. The whole process had been unable to write for hours:
  every `record engine usage` retried 30 s × 4 and failed. A separate
  connection's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` failed continuously; `triage_decisions`
  held **69,527** rows.
- **Root cause.** `pruneTriageKeys` used a correlated
  `NOT EXISTS (SELECT … FROM (GROUP BY … ORDER BY … LIMIT ?))`; the
  kept-key set was re-evaluated per outer row, so the maintenance pass
  started at boot became O(n²) and held the write lock. `EXPLAIN QUERY
  PLAN` showed `CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY` + `CO-ROUTINE kept`.
- **Fix.** The prune is now a materialized `LIST SUBQUERY`
  (`(fingerprint, decider) NOT IN (… GROUP BY … ORDER BY MAX(at) DESC,
  fingerprint DESC, decider DESC LIMIT ?)`), deleted in batches of
  **1,000** rows; each batch is its own short transaction and the lock
  is released between batches. Deterministic tie-breaks keep repeated
  passes stable. The maintenance pass itself is bounded to **2 minutes**
  and retries next interval.
- **QA writes go through the one busy policy.** `SaveQA`, `SaveQAPlan`,
  `ClearQA` and `ClearQAPlans` now use `store.BusyPolicy.WithBusyRetry`
  (validation outside; idempotent closures). `inTxOn` gained a deferred
  rollback, so a panic can no longer return a connection with an open
  transaction (the panic test failed before the defer and passes now).
- **Verified live.** After deploy, five consecutive `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
  probes succeeded (before and during the maintenance pass); the exact
  Ask question returned **HTTP 200**, mode `clarify`, and was saved as
  history row 238 with no `save qa history` error. `qa_history` stays
  at its 100-row cap. The question is stored correctly as UTF-8.
- **Open:** the clarify itself is the next defect — it offers five
  “person” candidates at `@clinique-exemple.test` instead of resolving the named
  organization; the remaining Ask path is tracked separately.

## 2026-11-03 — Triage: a provider-wide transient failure stops the run

- **Deployed with `0.1.0-dev+20261103155352`.** `engine.Classify` now

  codes, 400/404/422 and 500 keep their classes); a non-cancelled

  message until the budget. Index already had this behavior; the two
  now share the engine class.

  credits; 401/403 auth; quota; 400/404/422 rejected; 500 `ErrHTTP`),
  triage 429/503/504 and transport stop tests, the existing 402 tests,
  and `decision` transport/cancellation tests. The wire shape is
  unchanged; no UI string maps `stopped_by`.
- **Open:** a plain 500 remains message-scoped (a local runtime uses it
  for over-context input); `ErrRejected` remains per message.

## 2026-11-03 — ThreadStates: resolve one bounded evidence chunk at a time

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103151456`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **10.81 s** —

  4.29 s; home 2.90 s, learning 2.37 s, triage summary 2.12 s, triage
  page 1.13 s, semantic 1.13 s, conversations 0.68 s, mail 0.36 s,
  commitments 0.026 s, brief 0.010 s, agenda 0.001 s. RSS **730 MB**
  (private 746 MB), 39 threads.
- **Bounded evidence.** Phase 2 used to load full `body` + `headers`
  for the newest undecided member of every requested conversation at
  once and hold them until the whole mailbox resolved: 10,352 frontier
  rows live. `ThreadStates` now resolves conversations in chunks of
  `threadStateEvidenceBatch` (500) inside the same read transaction;
  each chunk's `loaded`/evidence maps are local and dropped before the
  next chunk. Phase 1, the frontier rule, `threadVisibility`,
  `EvidenceFrontier`, `Resolve`, ordering, and the public signature are
  unchanged.
- **Measured** on the 394 MB / 33,842-message fixture: evidence peak
  **10,352 → 500 rows** (20.7× lower); whole-mailbox
  `BenchmarkThreadStatesMailbox` **1.288 → 0.996 s/op (−22.7 %)**,
  **1.899 → 1.307 GB/op (−31.2 %)**, **6.04 → 4.46 M allocs/op
  (−26.1 %)**. A peak test proves an injected batch of 7 caps at 7 and a
  parity test at batches 1/5/all returns identical assessments.

  conversations, agenda, commitments and QA; the chunk bound applies to
  all of them.
- **Open:** phase-1 metadata still holds every requested conversation at
  once (~21 MB scale); a chunk can accumulate more than 500 evidence rows
  across multiple frontier rounds (the hard bound is one chunk's
  conversations).

## 2026-11-03 — Priority build: derive each action fact once per message

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103144956`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.04 s**
  (priority 7.30 s, companies 4.64 s, home 3.02 s, learning 2.43 s,
  triage summary 1.93 s, triage page 1.40 s, semantic 1.40 s,
  conversations 0.72 s, mail 0.59 s, commitments 0.032 s, brief 0.013 s,
  agenda 0.001 s). RSS **738 MB** (private 757 MB), 38 threads.
- **One derivation, two consumers.** `rowSignals` now owns the derived
  action facts: `actionSig = actionSignals(sig)`, `bulk =
  action.Bulk(actionSig)`, `wantsReply = replyOwed(sig) && !bulk`; the
  pass-1 thread evidence and pass-2 scoring both read them. Previously
  the build ran `actionSignals` 5×, `action.Bulk` 4–6× and
  `wantsResponse` 2× per row. `action.Classify` also computes `Bulk`
  once and passes it to `primaryFor`/`withDue`.

  passed to scoring (undated and future-clamped behavior preserved), and
  the build reuses one scratch answer map with `clear()` instead of
  allocating a 15-entry map per row. `signals()` builds the subject from
  the values it already extracted; `subject.FromAnswers` stays the
  triage adapter.
- **Benchmark** (same fixture, single core due to host load):
  `BenchmarkPriorityRow` **3,596 → 2,414 ns/op (−32.9 %)**, **4,164 →
  876 B/op (−79.0 %)**, **17 → 13 allocs/op**;
  `BenchmarkScoreRowSignals` **249.7 → 175.7 ns/op (−29.6 %)**.
- **Guards:** a derivation-parity table (`actionSig`/`bulk`/`wantsReply`
  against their owner functions), a `signals().Subject ==
  FromAnswers(...)` table including the Noul `>1` edge, future/invalid
  timestamp cases, and a scratch-map leak guard; the AST role guard now
  parses `signals()` alone.
- **Open:** `action.Classify` still evaluates `Bulk` once internally
  because `Signals` is its public input; `replyOpen` and `replySignal`
  remain deliberately different facts.

## 2026-11-03 — ThreadStates: the phase-1 row carries two decisions, not a recipients JSON blob

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103143250`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **16.58 s** this
  run (priority 9.33 s, companies 7.08 s, home 3.12 s, learning 2.51 s,
  triage summary 2.01 s, triage page 1.50 s, semantic 1.49 s,
  conversations 1.06 s, mail 0.38 s, commitments 0.037 s, brief 0.019 s,
  agenda 0.001 s) — the host was slower on this boot than the previous
  12.75 s run; the change is a store-projection change, not a new
  sequential stage. RSS **735 MB** (private 753 MB), 36 threads.
- **One expression per decision.** `threadStateSelect` decoded a
  correlated `json_group_array` of every recipient for every member row,
  while the resolver reads recipients in exactly one place: “more than
  one To recipient” on the last substantive message. It also probed
  `owner_identities` for every row, although the Go fallback uses the
  probe only for a sent row with no scope verdict. The select now returns
  `ManyTo` as a scalar `COUNT(*) > 1` and wraps the identity probe in
  `CASE WHEN verdict = '' AND role = 'sent' THEN … ELSE 0 END`.
  `threadintel.Message.Recipients` became `ManyTo`; the frontier/evidence
  phase and the resolver ordering are unchanged.
- **A/B benchmark** on the 33,842-message fixture (500 conversations,
  interleaved on the same store): **55.7 → 53.7 ms/op median** (−3.6 %),
  **75.99 → 74.95 MB/op** (−1.4 %), **252,270 → 238,072 allocs/op**
  (−5.6 %). The fixture has a verdict on every row, so the probe-skip is
  measured at its maximum; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` confirms the To count uses
  the recipients primary key.
- **New pins:** a single-To message still resolves `AwaitingOwner`
  (`TestThreadStatesSingleToRecipientStillOwes`), and a sent row with no
  verdict and a matching owner identity still resolves
  `scope.Owner`/`ReasonSentByOwner`
  (`TestThreadStatesSentOwnerFallbackUsesTheOwnerIdentity`), plus the
  existing partial-visibility gap test now sets `ManyTo` explicitly.
- **Open:** the To count still reads each message's recipient rows;
  eliminating that lookup needs a denormalized count column, which this
  round deliberately did not add. The CASE compares the raw verdict while
  Go trims; the only writer stores validated enum values today.

## 2026-11-03 — Feedback analytics: an abstention is never an answer

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103141227`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **14.71 s** this
  run (priority 8.99 s, companies 5.36 s, home 3.26 s, learning 2.63 s,
  summary 2.15 s, semantic 1.61 s, triage page 1.60 s, conversations
  0.79 s, mail 0.62 s, commitments 0.030 s, agenda 0.001 s); the round is
  backend-only, so the slower boot is host variance. RSS **730 MB**
  (private 749 MB), 39 threads. Label queue still serves (32,835 total,
  3 tasks).
- **One predicate everywhere.** The four remaining `!v.Refused` gates —
  calibration pairs, the escalation flagged-share denominator,
  correlation value lookup and impersonation suspects — now use
  `taxonomy.Value.Answered()`. An abstained value (`below_target`,
  `not_certified`, `below_coverage`, `no_answer`) is a deliberate
  non-answer, never a "no", a denominator row, a correlation key or a
  suspicious-domain suspect, regardless of the number it carries.

  and the same value answered moves the suggestion; `flaggedShare` ignores
  an abstained value (0.75 → 0.5) and counts an answered low-confidence
  one; correlations produce no input from abstentions and the expected
  findings when answered; impersonation produces zero suspects for an
  abstained `suspicious=1` and the six answered ones. Every pre-existing
  feedback test stays green; full gate **126/126** UI.
- **Open:** `Teaching` and priors still consume both label sources by
  design; the trainer's `evalOf` precedence is unchanged.

## 2026-11-03 — Sync: a bad folder no longer strands the mail that arrived

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103140524`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.61 s**;
  priority 7.58 s, companies 4.55 s, home 2.92 s, learning 2.39 s, summary
  1.91 s, semantic 1.40 s, triage page 1.41 s, conversations 0.69 s, mail
  0.35 s, commitments 0.030 s, agenda 0.000 s. RSS **727 MB** (private
  746 MB), 39 threads. Label queue still serves (32,835 total, 3 tasks).
- **Partial is not failure for downstream.** A run that fails only at
  some folders now reports `failed` with `partial:true`; the mail from the
  successful folders is complete and already committed. `Report.Advanced()`
  is the one trigger predicate: a completed run, or a partial run, that
  wrote mail, removed mail, rejudged scope or completed details advances;
  an output/unavailable/cancel failure or a no-op does not. Index,
  evidence, triage and install-profile all use it instead of the old
  `Succeeded` check, so one persistent bad folder can no longer leave every
  later message unindexed and untriaged until a perfectly clean run.
- **Status stays honest.** The run remains `failed`, keeps its error and
  folder report, and the UI continues to show the failure. `sync.finished`
  carries `partial:true` for a later warning surface.
- **Evidence.** New syncer table tests (folder error + write, output
  failure, unavailable/cancel, no-op, held-only, scope-only,
  details-only), trigger parity for all four consumers, and the existing
  cursor/removal tests. Full gate **126/126** UI.
- **Open:** the per-folder last-attempt outcome is still event-only, not
  persisted; a partial run is not yet surfaced as a UI warning; a
  non-folder failure that is neither output nor unavailable can set
  `partial` but cannot advance without a change counter.

## 2026-11-03 — Sync: an unexplained absence is held one run before deletion

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103134908`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.60 s**;
  priority 7.70 s, companies 4.60 s, home 3.19 s, learning 2.56 s, summary
  1.78 s, triage page 1.41 s, semantic 1.04 s, conversations 0.71 s, mail
  0.65 s, commitments 0.025 s, agenda 0.000 s. RSS **722 MB** (private
  742 MB), 38 threads. Live `/api/triage?limit=2` returns 34,763 rows with
  **answered=1, abstained=16, missing=0**.
- **The data-loss path closed.** Folders are snapshotted sequentially and
  removals run after all of them. A message that moved from folder A to B
  during the run could be absent from B's earlier snapshot and A's later
  one; no destination row existed, so `RemoveMessages` found no survivor
  and deleted the message and its labels/paid decisions. An absence with a
  nonempty Internet Message-ID and no survivor is now held for one complete
  run (`move_holds`, separate from the mass-removal `held_removals`); the
  next run either reconciles it as a move (label copy) or removes a genuine
  deletion.
- **Mass valve preserved.** The whole absence set goes through the
  existing mass-removal valve first when its threshold triggers, so a

## 2026-11-03 — Paging: derived models reset with their reads, paging survives a cached remount

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103130551`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **16.69 s** this
  run (priority 9.39 s, companies 7.22 s, home 3.13 s, learning 2.52 s,
  summary 1.99 s, triage page 1.40 s, conversations 1.09 s, semantic
  0.95 s, mail 0.37 s, commitments 0.037 s, agenda 0.014 s); the round is
  UI-only, so the slower boot is host variance, not a new boot path. RSS
  **756 MB** (private 778 MB), 36 threads. Label queue still serves
  (32,835 total, 3 tasks).
- **Derived paging models reset at the one invalidation choke point.**
  `invalidateCache` already reset the conversation page cache; it now
  calls `forgetPriorityPages()` and `forgetTriagePage()` under the same
  exact/prefix-covered/covering-prefix rule, including the empty full
  clear. A sync or triage completion can no longer leave appended Important
  or Recent pages carrying a removed/reranked snapshot. The forgets also
  clear the screen token on cached nodes, so a cached mount cannot re-seat
  a model the read dropped.
- **Age-aware Important.** `cachedPriority` rejects a page older than
  `CACHE_TTL.priority` (the `at` `recordPriority` already stored), so an
  expired accumulated list is a cold read, not a painted old ranking.
- **Paging survives a cached mount.** Each paged screen seats its model on
  the rendered node (`pagingToken`); the router re-seats it on the cached
  re-append path. `loadMoreImportant`, `loadMoreAnswers` and
  `loadMoreTriage` now check that token plus connection instead of the
  captured `state.renderSeq`, which every mount increments. A detached old
  closure is ignored; a cached re-append keeps paging. Answers and Triage
  use `withBusy`, so keyboard focus returns after Load more.
- **Offset cursor fixed.** Important’s second Load more used
  `offset + items.length`, double-counting the first page; the page now
  carries the response’s own next offset (`0/50/100` covered).
- **Evidence.** New source contracts in `paging_model_test.go`; six new
  Playwright regressions (stale Important after sync, stale Recent after
  triage, cached-remount paging on Important/Answers/Triage, expired
  cached Important, focus return) with baseline failures reproduced; full
  gate **124/124** UI.
- **Open:** a natural `/api/triage` TTL expiry alone still re-merges the
  first page into the accumulated Recent view; only an invalidation or
  Refresh resets it. Cached node tokens are scanned under the bounded route
  cache. The slower boot measurement above should be re-checked on the next
  deploy.

## 2026-11-03 — Feedback: an abstention is not a prediction, one pair one label

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103124037`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.85 s**;
  priority 8.01 s, companies 4.78 s, home 3.14 s, learning 2.53 s, summary
  2.07 s, triage page 1.46 s, semantic 1.45 s, conversations 0.73 s,
  mail 0.60 s, commitments 0.026 s, agenda 0.007 s. RSS **744 MB**
  (private 761 MB), 39 threads. Label queue still serves (32,835 total,
  3 tasks).
- **Scoring predicate.** Every feedback gate (`weakReply`, the choice,
  noul and score branches of `evalQuestion`) now scores only
  `taxonomy.Value.Answered()`. An abstained value used to keep
  `Number=0`/`Choice=""` and was compared as a real prediction, producing
  fabricated false errors and distorting accuracy, AUC and Brier scores.
- **One reference label per pair.** `Reference` resolves at most one label
  per `(message, question)`: the owner's manual label outranks the judge's
  independent reference label, matching the trainer's evaluation
  precedence. The kept label keeps its pair's first input position, so
  evaluation lists stay deterministic; `SourceCounts` still reports the
  deployment's real label volume before resolution. The judge's own
  production answer remains audit-only.
- **Evidence.** `TestEvaluateSkipsAbstainedAndRefusedValues`,
  `TestWeakReplySkipsAbstainedValues`,
  `TestReferenceResolvesOneLabelPerPair`, `TestReferenceKeepsDistinctPairsAndOrder`;
  full gate **118/118** UI.
- **Open:** `Teaching` and the priors still see both label sources by
  design; `calibrate.go`, `escalation.go`, `correlations.go` and
  `insights.go` still gate on `!v.Refused` and can score abstentions.
  The trainer's `evalOf` precedence must stay in sync with `Reference`.

## 2026-11-03 — Sidecar lifecycle: shutdown is bounded and starts are gated

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103120545`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.58 s**;
  priority 7.54 s, companies 4.65 s, home 2.94 s, learning 2.39 s, summary
  1.93 s, triage page 1.42 s, semantic 1.41 s, conversations 0.72 s,
  mail 0.36 s, commitments 0.021 s, agenda 0.007 s. RSS **713 MB**
  (private 731 MB), 39 threads.
- **One start gate.** `Manager.startWorker` does `wg.Add(1)` and starts the
  supervisor under the same `workerMu`/`stopped` gate `Stop` closes. A
  `Locate` racing shutdown can no longer panic with `sync: WaitGroup
  misuse` or start a supervisor after `Stop` returned. A refused start
  resolves the instance latch with `ErrStopped` in place.
- **Bounded shutdown.** `Stop` is idempotent, cancels under the gate, and
  waits at most `sidecar.stop_timeout + 5 s`; an unjoined supervisor is
  logged and abandoned so store close and the data-directory lock release
  always run.
- **The real hang fixed.** `exec.Cmd.WaitDelay` now bounds `cmd.Wait`'s
  wait for the stdout/stderr copy goroutines; a grandchild that inherited
  those pipes can no longer block `child.stop` forever. `launchReady`
  passes `sidecar.stop_timeout`; the normal restart path still waits for
  the child to die before a second runtime can own its port.
- **Evidence.** `-race` sidecar and cmd suites green;
  `TestStartWorkerIsSerializedWithStop` (20 rounds × 32 racing starts),
  `TestStopIsBoundedWhenAWorkerNeverFinishes`, `TestEnsureAfterStopResolvesErrStopped`,
  `TestLaunchSetsWaitDelay`, and an inherited-pipe process test (baseline
  without `WaitDelay` 5.001 s; with 200 ms 201 ms). Full gate **113/113**
  UI.
- **Open:** a truly unkillable process can outlive the join bound; the app
  logs it and continues, with the Windows job object as the OS backstop.

## 2026-11-03 — Completed background work refreshes the screens it changed

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103115424`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.51 s**;
  priority 7.63 s, companies 4.53 s, home 3.16 s, learning 2.56 s, summary
  1.77 s, triage page 1.38 s, semantic 1.37 s, conversations 0.71 s,
  mail 0.69 s, commitments 0.026 s, agenda 0.007 s. RSS **723 MB**
  (private 740 MB), 39 threads. Label queue still serves (32,835 total,
  3 tasks).

  changed mail: `totals.written > 0`, `removed.deleted + removed.moved > 0`,
  `scope.judged > 0` or `details.completed > 0`. `triage.finished` refreshes
  only when `decided + partial > 0`. Both parse defensively and treat a
  missing counter as zero, so a no-op run cannot rebuild a screen.
- **One reaction helper.** `refreshMailDerived(reads, routes, {forgetMail})`
  drops the reads, optionally forgets the All-Mail local model, marks the

  coalescer. Sync drops the mail list+detail, conversations, companies,
  priority, hub, triage, brief, agenda, commitments, labels, status and
  learning; triage drops its answer-derived set and deliberately leaves
  Mail All and message bodies alone. No direct fetch, no toast.
- **All-Mail owner strengthened.** `forgetAllMail()` now also clears the
  `__allMailModel` snapshots on cached mail nodes, so a cached restore
  cannot re-seat rows the dropped reads no longer support. It is called by
  `sync.finished`, `sync.mailboxes`, `invalidateAllReads` and
  `scheduleLiveResync`; label writes still leave the list model alone.
- **Reconnect completeness.** `scheduleLiveResync` now also drops
  `/api/agenda` and `/api/triage`; a reconnect no longer leaves those
  screens on pre-gap data.
- **Evidence.** `internal/ui/completion_events_test.go` source contracts;
  new `e2e/specs/completion-events.spec.ts` (sync refreshes Mail/Companies/
  Hub and forgets All Mail; zero-change sync and zero-decision triage issue
  no request; triage refreshes Priority/Triage/Conversations but not Mail;
  `config.changed` leaves no stale All-Mail model; reconnect refreshes
  agenda/triage) **6/6**; full gate **113/113** UI.
- **Open:** a completion while the tab is hidden still invalidates; the
  visible refresh runs when the route next refreshes. `sync.progress` and

  route names `priority`/`triage`/`conversations`/`agenda` are surfaces,

## 2026-11-03 — Teach: a prefetched screen paints its task instead of loading forever

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103114356`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.54 s**;
  priority 7.76 s, companies 4.59 s, home 2.91 s, learning 2.38 s, summary
  1.76 s, triage page 1.36 s, semantic 1.35 s, conversations 0.71 s,
  mail 0.54 s, commitments 0.025 s, agenda 0.006 s. RSS **747 MB**
  (private 765 MB), 39 threads. The label queue still serves (32,835
  total, 3 tasks).
- **Root cause.** Navigation prefetch renders a destination while it is
  detached (`prefetchRoute`), then caches the node. `showLabelTask` loaded
  the message and then discarded the result when
  `!workbenchHost.isConnected`, so the cached Teach screen kept its
  “Chargement du message…” / “Chargement du formulaire de réponse…”
  placeholders forever. The live message read itself answers in 4 ms, so
  this was never a server hang; the same discard also hit a fast cached
  read on a route refresh.
- **Fix.** `taskSeq` is the one stale-result guard; a task now paints into
  the node the router is about to cache, connected or not. The document
  key handler and observers stay owned by `activeTaskAttach`, which the
  router re-installs on mount.
- **Evidence.** New Playwright regression hovers the Teach nav (prefetch),
  then opens it and asserts the task subject and answer control with no
  `.loading` left. Mutation check: restoring the old `isConnected` guard
  fails the same test; the fix passes it. `renderLabels`'s toolbar moved
  to `labelsToolbar` so the source-size budget stays at 799 lines rather
  than being raised. Labels suite **6/6**; full gate **107/107** UI.
- **Open:** a prefetched screen still installs no document key handler
  until mount (by design, via `activeTaskAttach`); a task load that fails
  after the owner left reports only when its node is next shown.

- **Lean route decode.** `priorityQuestionSelection` is now
  `map[string]QuestionKey`, so the store knows each selected question's
  type. A score answer decodes its level distribution (the class
  `selective.Decided` reads can differ from `round(Value)`); every other
  answer keeps only `type/refused/value/choice/abstain`. `confidence`,
  `layer`, `rule` and non-score distributions are consumed by typed
  discard decoders that keep the JSON kind (number/string/object) and the
  `DisallowUnknownFields` boundary, without retaining maps, pointers or
  strings. Unselected answers are syntax-checked but no longer copied into
  a retained `json.RawMessage`.
- **Preview is unchanged.** Preview answers still decode the full
  `engine.Answer` because `checkPreviewAnswer` validates confidence and
  complete distributions; only the route path is lean. The `nil` selection
  (full-read fallback) still decodes the full route shape.
- **Measured:** `BenchmarkDecodePriorityRoute` (17 stored answers, 15
  selected, 5 choice + 4 score + 8 noul): **26,374 → 17,005 ns/op**,
  **15,008 → 12,359 B/op**, **133 → 83 allocs/op** (median of 3; the
  strictness pass kept the same 83 allocs). For 33,416 routed rows that is
  ≈1.67 M fewer allocations per build. Live boot priority did not move
  beyond noise, so the remaining cost is elsewhere (thread states, scoring
  and the TTL rebuild), not decode alone.
- **Evidence.** `TestLeanRouteDecodeMatchesTheStoredShape`,
  `…DeclaresEveryRouteAnswerField` (reflection over `route.Answer`),
  `…KeepsTheStrictBoundary` (unknown field, wrong kind for
  confidence/layer/rule/distribution, malformed selected/unselected, null,
  trailing), `…KeepsEveryScoreDistribution`, `TestPreviewDecodeIsUnchanged`,
  and the `signals`/ranking parity table including a score whose
  distribution class differs from `round(Value)`. Focused suites green;
  full gate **100/100** UI.
- **Open:** the third `answersFor` map still exists; preview-on pays the
  full decode by design; the TTL refresh still rebuilds a 7 s ranking every
  ~21 s while generations are unchanged (candidate next backend round).

## 2026-11-03 — Learning status: one build reads each layer-1 fact once

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103102046`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.75 s**;
  priority 8.26 s, triage page 7.10 s, companies 3.35 s, home 3.26 s,
  learning 2.61 s, summary 1.88 s, semantic 1.57 s, conversations 0.81 s,
  mail 0.55 s, commitments 0.019 s, agenda 0.006 s. RSS **776 MB**
  (private 797 MB), 38 threads. `/api/learning` returns `learned` with
  9 stages and the gate open.
- **One build-scoped fact memo.** `learning.Memo[T](ctx, name, build)` shares
  the existing per-build `statusMemo` with the stage memo, keyed by
  `(fact, type, name)`. Inside one `computeStatus` build the first reader
  runs the fact; every other stage gets the same value and error. Outside a
  build it is exactly `build(ctx)`, and nothing survives the build.
- **Layer-1 reads once per build.** `Runner.plan` (5 → **1**),
  `lastRun` (`ListLayer1Runs(1)` + decode 2 → **1**), `lastSucceeded`
  (`ListLayer1Runs(50)` + decode 2 → **1**), `fingerprint`
  (`ListEvidenceRuns`, `EmbeddingSequence`, `DecisionSummary`,
  `store.ListLabels` each 2 → **1**), and `routeCertifications` (2 → **1**,
  keyed by the report's run so a failed newest run cannot share with the
  newest succeeded one). `labelRows` keeps the one `in.Labels` read of a
  status build. A whole status snapshot before/after the change was
  byte-identical.
- **Consistency, not just speed.** All stages of one build now answer from
  one snapshot of each fact; a write mid-build is observed by the next
  build instead of making two stages disagree.
- **Evidence.** `TestMemoAnswersEachFactOnceWithinOneBuild`,
  `TestMemoWithoutABuildIsDirect`, `TestMemoPreservesAFailedFactWithinTheBuild`,
  `TestMemoAnswersConcurrentReadersOnce`,
  `TestStatusBuildReadsEachLayer1FactOnce`, `TestStatusBuildMemoIsPerBuild`,
  `TestCertificationsArePerReport`; the counting seam showed the before
  counts; focused suites green; gofmt/vet clean.
- **Open:** report decode remains 2× when `lastRun` and `lastSucceeded`
  select the same run (separate facts); `LabelNeed` is still computed once
  per stage; non-status `NewPlan`/`in.Labels` call sites stay direct.

## 2026-11-03 — Shared view cache, phase 2: one shape for conversations, world profiles and commitments

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103101220`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.79 s**;
  priority 8.18 s, triage page 7.04 s, home 3.45 s, companies 3.16 s,
  learning 2.77 s, summary 1.88 s, semantic 1.58 s, conversations 0.65 s,
  mail 0.55 s, commitments 0.025 s, agenda 0.011 s. RSS **767 MB**
  (private 785 MB), 38 threads. Live conversations (5 rows, total 10,658,
  `has_more`), companies (3 of 800) and commitments (5 rows) all render.
- **`Keep` now sees the value.** `viewcache.Options.Keep` is
  `func(K, V) bool`, so a cache whose key cannot carry a generation can
  still refuse to install (and treat as stale) a snapshot built for a moved
  generation. Phase-1 call sites ignore `V` and keep generation keys.
- **Conversations pages:** `*viewcache.Cache[pageKey, pageValue]`, where the
  value carries the generation it was built from; `Keep` requires it to
  match the request key and the current mail generation. TTL 15 s, 32
  entries. `pageEntry`, `refreshPage` and `installPageLocked` are deleted.
- **World profiles:** `*viewcache.Cache[string, profileValue]` keyed by the
  existing profile key; `Keep` requires the value's mail and route
  generations to still be current. The batch `Profiles` path routes each
  missing key through the cache behind one shared batch build, so
  concurrent callers of one profile share a build and a five-profile warm
  costs one store batch.
- **Commitments:** a constant-key `*viewcache.Cache[struct{}, snapshot]`;
  the value carries its generations and `Keep` reproduces “serve the stale
  set while one rebuild runs” on a generation move. `rebuild` and
  `refreshing` are gone.
- **Measured cold concurrency (8 callers, one missing key):** conversations
  pages 8 → **1** build, world profile 8 → **1** store read, commitments
  8 → **1** build. `Profiles` with three keys still builds each once.
- **The world list stays custom, deliberately:** one wider snapshot serves
  every narrower limit, which the keyed cache cannot express without a
  second read path, and a search bypasses the cache. Its comment states
  this.
- **Evidence.** `viewcache` tests (including a value-aware keep and a
  fresh-but-stale serve), per-service cold-concurrency and race regressions,
  `clocktest.Barrier` for deterministic barriers; the focused suites are
  green; gofmt/vet clean.
- **Open:** conversations still owns its snapshot cache and refresh path;
  a cold build holds one goroutine per waiting caller; the cache is
  in-memory and per-process.

## 2026-11-03 — Shared view cache, phase 1: one single-flight shape for four read services

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103094906`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.78 s**;
  priority 8.25 s, triage page 7.06 s, home 3.50 s, companies 3.06 s,
  learning 2.77 s, conversations 0.64 s, summary 1.87 s, semantic 1.22 s,
  mail 0.54 s, agenda 0.011 s, commitments 0.023 s. RSS **772 MB**
  (private 789 MB), 39 threads. Hub wire intact (34,768 messages, 1 store,
  5 manual / 32,708 review). Brief topics are empty because only
  `suspicious` is certified, so the topic question abstains; commitments are
  0 by data.
- **One cache, four callers.** New `internal/viewcache` owns the bounded,
  single-flight, stale-while-revalidate shape that triage already had:
  fresh hit; a missing key runs exactly one build (concurrent callers wait);
  a failed first build installs nothing; an expired entry is served at once
  while one detached, timeout-bounded rebuild runs; a failed rebuild keeps
  the snapshot; entries are bounded and a panicking build releases waiters.
  An optional `Keep` gate refuses to install a result built while a write
  moved the generation.
- **Migrated:** triage pages/summaries (TTL 30 s, 16 entries), hub label
  counts, mailbox counts and recent answers (10 s, 2 each, generation
  `Keep`), brief (15 s, 16, generation `Keep`), agenda (15 s, 8, generations
  in the key). The per-service `refreshing`/`ready`/TTL loops, entry types
  and refresh methods are deleted; each service keeps only its key, its
  build and its result slicing.
- **Measured cold concurrency (8 callers, one missing key):** hub label
  counts 8 → **1** store read, brief 8 → **1** (each source), agenda 8 → **1**
  `OwnerSet`, triage already 1. This is the stampede the old hub/brief/agenda
  caches allowed.
- **Deliberate semantic:** hub/brief/agenda keys now carry the store
  generations, so a generation move is a cold rebuild instead of serving the
  previous generation while refreshing. A snapshot is never served for a
  generation it was not built under; the cost is one synchronous build on
  the first request after a write.
- **Evidence.** `internal/viewcache/viewcache_test.go` (single flight,
  failed first build, stale-once refresh, value-aware keep, panic release,
  bound); per-service cold-concurrency regressions (`LabelCounts`,
  commitments/conversations/priority builds, `OwnerSet`); focused suites
  for viewcache/triage/priority/hub/brief/agenda/conversations/world/api/
  cmd green; gofmt/vet clean; full gate **91/91** UI.
- **Open:** conversations, world profiles and commitments still own private
  copies (phase 2); the world list cache stays custom because one wider
  snapshot serves narrower limits; a cold build still holds one goroutine
  per waiting caller; the cache is in-memory and per-process.

## 2026-11-03 — Review queue: the badge and the tasks count one population

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103093607`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.80 s**;
  priority 8.43 s, triage page 7.22 s, home 3.70 s, companies 3.26 s,
  learning 2.79 s, conversations 0.63 s, summary 1.88 s, semantic 1.03 s,
  mail 0.77 s, agenda 0.015 s, commitments 0.026 s. RSS **773 MB**
  (private 793 MB), 39 threads. Labels unchanged: 5 manual / 32,713 judge /
  5,044 needed / 32,708 review.
- **One presence rule, no decoding in the population.** A review task
  exists iff a **judge** label exists for the message+question and no
  **manual** label does; a manual answer of any form means the owner has
  answered. `layer1.reviewCandidate` returns `(suggestion, hasSuggestion,
  offer)` separately: an undecodable judge label is still offered (no
  suggestion), while the old `labelSuggestion` silently skipped it and
  offered tasks for undecodable manual labels — so the queue could disagree
  with the count in both directions.
- **`ReviewCounts` applies the queue's folder roles.** It now reads
  `triage.folder_roles` and passes `rolesSQL`, exactly like `MemberIDs`;
  previously the count ignored the role selection, so a restricted
  configuration could advertise more tasks than the queue held.
- **Suggestion stays optional.** `buildReviewQueue` appends every offered
  candidate and sets `Suggestion`/`SuggestionSource` only when the judge
  value decodes; the wire already had `omitempty`. No wire change.
- **Evidence.** `TestReviewQueueMatchesCountsOnUndecodableValues`
  (four messages; queue `Total`/ids equal `ReviewCounts`),
  `TestReviewQueueOffersAnUndecodableJudgeLabel`,
  `TestReviewQueueSkipsAnyManualAnswer`, and
  `TestReviewCountsFollowsTriageFolderRoles` (inbox-only → 1, inbox+sent
  → 2). The old decode-gated tests failed before the change. `go test
  ./internal/layer1 ./internal/store ./internal/api ./internal/hub`
  green; gofmt/vet clean.
- **Open:** an undecodable manual label suppresses review even though the
  queue cannot decode it; the owner can still correct it from the message's
  own labels. The population is presence-based, so a future profile change
  can surface a task without a suggestion by design.

  ./internal/api` green; the `-race` matrix passed 20 runs; gofmt/vet clean.

  cost); the `saveCatalog` field is a narrow test seam, nil in production.

## 2026-11-03 — Thread visibility uses the one mailbox predicate

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103091253`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.56 s**;
  priority 8.27 s, triage page 7.08 s, home 3.52 s, companies 3.14 s,
  learning 2.77 s, conversations 0.62 s, summary 1.93 s, semantic 1.02 s,
  mail 0.78 s, agenda 0.010 s, commitments 0.025 s. RSS **773 MB**
  (private 792 MB), 39 threads. The full UI gate was re-run after one
  browser-level `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` navigation failure: **89/89**.
- **One predicate, no drift.** `threadVisibility` counted a shared/delegate
  mailbox as visible when any folder was `picked = 1`, while `visibleSQL` —
  the single predicate of every read over the user's mail — requires
  `active = 1 AND picked = 1`. A picked folder the connector no longer
  discovers therefore counted as evidence, so thread state could claim a
  colleague's reply was absent when it was outside the active evidence. The
  `NOT EXISTS` now derives from `visibleSQL` (same `f` alias), one SQL
  statement, no Go filter.
- **Evidence.** `TestThreadVisibilityCountsOnlyActivePickedFolders`:
  picked+active → Complete; picked+inactive → Partial (failed before);
  active+unpicked → Partial; no folder → Partial; two mailboxes with one
  partial → Partial; primary-only → Complete. `go test ./internal/store
  ./internal/threads ./internal/api` green; gofmt/vet clean.
- **Open:** a mailbox with no folders is still Partial (an evidence gap, not
  proof of absence); folder discovery remains the owner of `active`.

## 2026-11-03 — Certification: per-class recall, and the documented point threshold

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103084003`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.51 s**;
  priority 9.03 s, triage page 7.75 s, home 3.95 s, companies 3.32 s,
  learning 3.03 s, conversations 0.75 s, summary 1.74 s, semantic 1.25 s,
  mail 1.01 s, agenda 0.000 s, commitments 0.021 s. RSS **757 MB**
  (private 780 MB), 39 threads. `suspicious` remains the only certified
  question (983/983 answered, 18 errors, precision 0.982, lower bound
  0.964). The live `class_recall` is `null` on every question because the
  stored route report was committed before the field existed; the next
  layer-1 commit under this build populates it. The report is additive, so
  the gate verdict is unchanged.
- **A pooled precision can hide a class the rule never answers.** Every
  certification now carries `class_recall` (one `{class, eligible,
  answered, correct}` per labelled class) and `class_collapsed` (a class
  with at least `classMin = 3` eligible certification labels and no
  answered row). It is **report-only**: `Certified` still follows the
  pooled Wilson bound, so the live `suspicious` certification cannot be
  closed by this round. It is surfaced on the layer-1 report and
  `/api/learning` (`status.stages[].certifications[]`).
- **A route must report the class it abstained on.** The route's fixed
  cascade used to pass only answered rows, so a class below every gate
  vanished from the report and `class_collapsed` could never fire there.
  `Ranked` gains `Abstained` (zero value = answered); `certifyMembers`
  passes every labelled certification item, and `CertifyFixed` counts only
  answered rows for precision while counting every classed row as
  eligible. `N` is now the tested certification population and `Answered`
  the rule's answers.
- **One threshold rule.** `CertifyEligible` chose `Targets(...)[0].ThresholdLB`
  while its own comment, `docs/LAYER1.md` and the route gates all use the
  point estimate. It now uses `.Threshold`; `TestCertifyChoosesThePointThreshold`
  pins a fixture where the two differ (point 0.8, LB 0.9).
- **Live-safe staging.** The class report and the threshold correction ship
  now; rejecting certification on `class_collapsed` is deferred until the
  live composition is reviewed, because only `suspicious` is certified
  (1 of 17) and enforcement could close the gate without evidence.
- **Evidence.** New `TestCertificationReportsClassRecall`,
  `TestCertificationWithoutClassesSkipsTheReport`,
  `TestCertifyChoosesThePointThreshold`,
  `TestCertifyFixedReportsUnansweredClassAsCollapsed`,
  `TestHoldoutCertificationReportsClassRecall`,
  `TestRouteCertificationReportsClassRecall` (including a below-gate class),
  `TestReportSerializesClassCertification`,
  `TestLearningViewSerializesClassCertification`. The route
  `N`/`Answered` tests were updated to the tested-population contract.
- **Open:** a class with fewer than `classMin` certification labels can
  collapse without being flagged; the report does not block yet; the live
  class composition for `suspicious` is still to be read after deploy.

## 2026-11-03 — Label sources: the model no longer learns from its own answers

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103081940`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.79 s**;
  priority 8.38 s, triage page 7.18 s, home 3.60 s, companies 3.08 s,
  learning 2.78 s, conversations 0.63 s, summary 1.93 s, semantic 1.22 s,
  mail 0.55 s, agenda 0.008 s, commitments 0.021 s. RSS **767 MB**
  (private 787 MB), 39 threads — back from the 868 MB per-message-filter
  regression.
- **One policy owner.** `feedback.Teaching` and `feedback.Reference` keep
  the owner's **manual** labels and the judge's **independent reference**
  labels; `feedback.SourceCounts` reports every known source. `judge_answer`
  is the model's own production answer, written for audit, and never becomes
  an example, a prior, or ground truth. Every consumer applies the policy at
  the owner — `SelectExamples`, `SuspiciousPrior`, `Evaluate`, `Calibrate`,
  `CalibrateEscalation` — and no call site compares a source string.
  **Live data drove the boundary:** the deployment holds 5 `manual` and
  32,713 `judge` labels, so excluding `judge` would have erased nearly all
  teaching signal; only `judge_answer` is self-produced.
- **`feedback.Load` deliberately returns every source** so the quality
  report can show the real composition: `Evaluation.Sources` now carries
  `manual`/`judge`/`judge_answer` counts (zero keys included). A deployment
  with no teaching labels now shows that fact instead of silently feeding
  the model its own output.
- **Mixed fixture, before → after.** Examples 3 → **2** (manual + judge);
  suspicious-prior samples 3 → **2**; evaluation count 3 → **2** (accuracy
  0.5) with `Sources{manual:1, judge:1, judge_answer:1}`; calibration labels
  6 → **4** and its suggested threshold moves off the judge-answer
  contamination. The composed prompt contains the manual and judge values,
  never the production answer. Pinned by
  `TestSourcePolicyKeepsIndependentLabels`,
  `TestJudgeAnswerLabelsNeverBecomeExamplesOrPriors`,
  `TestEvaluateCountsIndependentLabels`, `TestCalibrateIgnoresJudgeAnswer`
  and `TestComposerExamplesSkipJudgeAnswers`.
- **The filter runs once, not per message.** The first cut applied
  `Teaching` inside `SelectExamples`/`SuspiciousPrior`; with 32,718 live
  labels and 34k triage rows that copied the whole set per message and the
  deployed build's RSS rose to 868 MB. `core.withLabels` now filters once at
  the load boundary and the per-message selectors take the filtered set; a
  set where every label is kept is returned unchanged (no copy). This is the
  shape that ships.
- **Evidence.** `go test ./internal/feedback ./internal/triage
  ./internal/layer1 ./internal/api ./cmd/mailsense ./internal/judge`
  green; `-tags judgegold` compiles; gofmt/vet clean.
- **Open:** existing `judge_answer` rows stay in the label tables (no
  migration deletes them); they are audit/count-only for feedback. Layer-1's
  configured teacher sources are unchanged. A deployment with no manual and
  no judge labels legitimately produces empty prompts/priors and low
  evaluation counts until more labels exist.

## 2026-11-03 — Network efficiency: one embed per text, a log wake instead of fanout, a bounded logs page

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103080317`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.78 s**;
  priority 8.57 s, triage page **7.27 s**, home 3.63 s, companies 3.11 s,
  conversations 0.61 s, learning 2.80 s, summary 1.72 s, semantic
  **1.03 s**, mail 0.79 s, agenda 0.008 s, commitments 0.020 s. RSS
  **776 MB** (private 795 MB), 38 threads. `/api/logs?limit=3` returns
  three entries and `last_seq`, so the bounded page and wake path are live.
- **One query-vector cache.** `internal/search` now keeps a bounded (64),
  single-flight cache keyed by the search space and the exact folded query
  text (`mail.Fold`, the existing full-text normalization). Concurrent
  identical texts share one embedder call; a failed call installs nothing;
  FIFO eviction re-embeds. The omnibox asks for `semantic=off`, which returns
  the same text results with `semantic.used=false` and an honest notice and
  never resolves or calls the embedder; the explicit Search page keeps
  semantic. Tests pin 0 calls for `semantic=off`, 1 for repeated text, 1 for
  concurrent identical texts, 65+1 across eviction, and no caching of a
  failure. A Playwright spec types 10 paused prefixes and asserts text-only
  reads with zero embedding calls, while the Search page stays semantic.
- **SSE sends a wake, not the log entry.** `tailLogs` now emits one
  coalesced `log.wake` frame per tail read (`{seq,count}`, no attrs or text)
  instead of the full entry JSON to every client. `Last-Event-ID`/`since`,
  rotation, buffer-full and bus-dropped frames are unchanged. The Logs
  screen listens for `log.wake` and coalesces a `/api/logs?since=state.logLast`
  read through the existing loader; other routes ignore the wake.
  `BenchmarkSSELogFanout`, 100 entries: **171,831 B → 456 B** across 8
  clients (21,479 B → 57 B for 1), a ~99.7 % cut.
- **The logs page is bounded independently of retention.** `Ring.ReadLimit`
  binary-searches the cursor and slices at most `limit` entries under the
  ring lock (`newest` for the initial view, forward for `since`); the API
  page maximum is **5000** regardless of `log.ring.size`, default 500, and a
  larger `limit` is `400 invalid_limit`. `BenchmarkLogsSnapshot` at 100k
  entries / 500 rows is 57,344 B and **1 alloc/op**; retention and eviction
  are unchanged.
- **Evidence.** `go test ./internal/search ./internal/api ./internal/logx
  ./internal/ui ./cmd/mailsense` green, `-race` on search/api/logx green;
  `e2e/specs/{search,logs,live}.spec.ts` **7/7**; generated bundle current.
- **Open:** a cold query still embeds once and the cache is per process. A
  log burst still wakes every connected client once per coalesced read; only
  the per-entry fanout is gone. Each mounted Logs client pays one
  `/api/logs` read per wake window. The 5000 page maximum bounds responses,
  not ring memory. Omnibox suggestions are never semantic, so the Search page
  cannot reuse a suggestion vector (both-semantic reuse is covered).

## 2026-11-03 — UI resilience: live language, cached Teach keys, request bounds, visible action failures

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103075236`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **11.57 s**
  (from 12.08 s); priority 8.31 s, triage page 7.34 s, home **3.35 s**,
  companies 3.08 s, conversations 0.60 s, learning 2.59 s, summary 1.89 s,
  semantic 1.39 s, mail 0.36 s, agenda 0.010 s, commitments 0.020 s. RSS
  **765 MB** (private 785 MB), 38 threads. The full UI suite is now
  **81/81** (eight new specs).
- **A live language switch rebuilds the mounted body.** `applyLanguageLive`
  used to invalidate the route cache and call `renderRoute()`, but the route
  identity still matched, so the router took its same-route branch and only
  the chrome changed. The router now has one `force` path that bypasses the
  same-route shortcut; EN→FR on Mail replaces the body in French, pinned by
  `e2e/specs/language.spec.ts` and a source contract.
- **A cached Teach screen keeps its keyboard and observers.** Route-cache
  entries capture one attach hook from the screen node
  (`screen.__routeAttach`); the cached mount invokes it after appending the
  DOM. Teach re-installs its key handler and recreates both observers
  without rebuilding the task; Companies declares its existing row observer
  through the same hook. `1–9`, `Enter`, `G`, `?` work after Back.
- **Every client request is bounded at one owner.** `request()` owns one
  `AbortController` and timer: ordinary reads 30 s (above the measured cold
  triage ~8 s and priority ~9 s), paid/long actions 5 min via an explicit
  option (Ask send, run starts, sync, backfill). Aborts map to
  `ApiError(0, {code:"timeout"})`. A timed-out mutation may have been
  applied, so the UI reports “no response yet” and refreshes the reads
  instead of claiming failure. SSE never enters `request()`.
- **A user action always reports.** `runAction` wraps top-level actions,
  restores the button in `finally`, and reports once; Sources and Logs
  Refresh use it. The full-suite gate reproduced a real race the isolated
  spec missed: the Settings Apply catch used `reportError`, whose
  prefetch-suppression window swallowed the toast while a background read
  was in flight. All three Settings user actions (Apply/Reset, Reload,
  learned toggle) now use `reportActionError`; the one-toast spec passes in
  the full suite. Background reads keep the suppression.
- **Evidence.** `go generate ./internal/ui && go test ./internal/ui` green;
  `e2e/specs/{language,labels,sources,resilience,boot}.spec.ts` **26/26**
  in isolation and the full UI suite **81/81** after the toast fix
  (the previous full run failed the one-toast spec, then passed after the
  root-cause fix). `internal/ui/app.js` is regenerated.
- **Open:** a timed-out read paints the shared error surface with manual
  Retry (no automatic retry). A cached Teach screen restores interaction,
  not fresh data. A timed-out mutation's server outcome is refreshed, not
  cancelled. Mutation-timeout recovery invalidates all reads because the
  transport does not know the exact affected prefixes.

## 2026-11-03 — Hot reads B: the remaining per-batch and per-address sorts

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103073405`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.08 s**;
  home **3.66 s** (from 4.17 s), triage page **7.33 s** (from 7.43 s),
  priority **8.46 s** (from 8.67 s), companies **3.21 s**, conversations
  **0.62 s**, learning 2.81 s, summary 1.93 s, semantic 1.58 s, mail
  0.57 s, agenda 0.009 s, commitments 0.022 s. RSS **775 MB** (private
  796 MB), 39 threads.
- **Thread summaries read the newest member first.** `threadSummariesQuery`
  pins `messages_conversation_instant` and orders
  `conversation_id, instant DESC, id DESC`; the fold takes a
  conversation's subject and instant from its first row, while participants
  stay an order-independent union of every member (the newest row's sender
  included). The old plan was `SEARCH m USING INDEX
  messages_conversation` + `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST 2 TERMS OF ORDER BY`
  over each batch; the new plan is `SEARCH m USING INDEX
  messages_conversation_instant` with no sort. 500 conversations (1,656
  eligible messages) on the 33,842-message fixture: **13.6–14.5 ms →
  10.8–12.8 ms**; the removed sort is the invariant, the wall-clock win is
  secondary. `TestThreadSummariesKeepTheNewestMember` compares the read with
  the old ordered statement on several messages per conversation, equal
  instants on both insertion orders, a later-inserted older message, a
  shared-store member and a draft.
- **Calendar attendees follow the window, not the calendar.**
  `CalendarEvents` passes the event ids it returned to `attendees`, which
  reads `event_attendees INDEXED BY event_attendees_event` through
  `WHERE event_id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))` and orders
  `event_id, kind, address`. The old query joined every visible
  `calendar_events` row. Plan `SCAN a USING INDEX event_attendees_event` +
  primary-key probe of the event → `SEARCH a USING INDEX
  event_attendees_event (event_id=?)`; the only remaining sort is the two
  trailing order terms over the window's attendee rows. Synthetic 2,000
  out-of-window events (6,040 attendee rows) plus a 20-event window:
  **7.6–8.0 ms → 0.36–0.49 ms**; `BenchmarkCalendarEvents`.
  `TestCalendarAttendeesReadOnlyTheWindow` seeds a sentinel attendee on an
  out-of-window event and proves the returned map never contains its event
  id, while the plan is the indexed range.
- **LatestThreadForAddresses splits the counterpart OR.** The received half
  is one `messages_sender_norm` equality per address (newest first, `LIMIT
  1`); the sent half looks the exact addresses up in `recipients_address`
  and reads the matching messages on `messages_instant`, also `LIMIT 1`.
  One `latestThread.newerThan` owner compares `(instant, message id)` and
  picks the newer branch. The old plan scanned folders, all 33,842
  messages, the scope verdict per message, probed recipients for each
  `sent_by_owner` row and sorted the matches. New plans: `SEARCH m USING
  INDEX messages_sender_norm (sender_norm=?)` and `SCAN m USING INDEX
  messages_instant` + `MULTI-INDEX OR` on `recipients_address`; neither
  branch has a temporary sort. Fixture: **59 ms → 0.33–0.40 ms** for a
  375-message counterpart and **4–6.5 ms** for the widest one
  (`BenchmarkLatestThreadForAddresses`); the raw-fallback recipient arm
  keeps the old exact-address semantics for an unnormalized legacy row.
  `TestLatestThreadForAddressesKeepsTheNewestCounterpart` compares every
  case with the old counterpart scan (received, sent, equal instant on both
  insertion orders, unpicked, shared, draft, unthreaded, normalized aliases,
  legacy row, no result).
- **Label counts start from labels.** Both aggregates use a `CROSS JOIN
  messages` barrier so `labels` is the outer loop: `SCAN l USING COVERING
  INDEX sqlite_autoindex_labels_1` comes first and an empty labels table
  ends the read without visiting a message. The old plan scanned both
  folders, the 33,842 messages, the verdict per message and probed labels by
  message id. Fixture with **0 labels**: `LabelCounts` **4.84–4.97 ms →
  0.05–0.09 ms**, `ReviewCounts` **4.72–5.02 ms → 0.05–0.09 ms**
  (`BenchmarkLabelCounts`, `BenchmarkReviewCounts`). `ReviewCounts` keeps
  the exact `source = judge` / no-manual-label predicate and the wire shape.
  `TestLabelCountsMatchTheScopeDrivenAggregate` compares both counts with
  the old statements over every source and the visibility switch;
  `TestLabelCountsStartFromLabels` pins the outer loop and the empty read;
  `TestHubCountsStayEmptyWithoutLabels` pins the hub's zero-label answer.
- **Evidence.** Plans from `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the prepared
  33,842-message store (10,352 conversations, 58,562 recipients, 33,842
  verdicts, 0 labels); the calendar numbers are the synthetic benchmark
  above because the prepared store has no calendar rows. `go test
  ./internal/store ./internal/world ./internal/hub ./internal/api
  -count=1` green; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean on the touched packages.
- **Open.** The calendar read still scans the window's calendar events
  before the attendee range; label counts still scale with the labels table,
  and the shared `labels` primary key means the `GROUP BY` keeps a small
  temporary B-tree (this tree has no `labels_by_source_question` migration,
  and no schema change was made). The received branch on an owner address
  scans that address's whole sender range without a match because every row
  there is `sent_by_owner` (30 ms on the fixture); callers pass a resolved
  counterpart, not the owner.

## 2026-11-03 — Hot reads A: four whole-population reads become index-ordered

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103072114`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **12.11 s** (from
  13.06 s); conversations **0.63 s** (from 2.12 s, −70%), home **4.17 s**
  (from 5.69 s), companies **3.24 s** (from 3.72 s), learning **2.78 s**
  (from 4.30 s), triage page **7.43 s** (from 7.60 s), priority
  **8.67 s** (from 9.23 s), summary 1.91 s, semantic 1.24 s, mail
  0.57 s, agenda 0.009 s, commitments 0.020 s. RSS **774 MB** (private
  795 MB), 38 threads — the digest fold holds more per-conversation
  state, and the company/total caches are bounded.
- **Conversation digest is one stream.** `conversationDigestQuery` now reads
  `messages` once through `messages_conversation_instant`, joins folders and
  scope verdicts, and returns members in conversation/newest-first order.
  `ConversationDigests` folds `COUNT(*)`, sent, unread, `MIN(instant)`, the
  latest member and the latest received sender in Go, then sorts the ~10k
  digests by instant and conversation id. The unthreaded count stays on its
  conversation index, and the digest/coverage wire shape is unchanged.
  Fixture plan: `MATERIALIZE content` + `MATERIALIZE agg` + group/DISTINCT/
  final `TEMP B-TREE`s + `AUTOMATIC` index → `SCAN m USING INDEX
  messages_conversation_instant` with primary-key lookups. Read 421 ms
  single-shot → 170–237 ms repeated (20× in-process 316 → 170 ms).
- **Embedding states follow the instant index.** The leading
  `m.instant = ''` term was redundant: `instant` is `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`
  and `''` already sorts last under `DESC`. Plan `SCAN m USING INDEX
  messages_folder_run` + `TEMP B-TREE` → `SCAN m USING INDEX
  messages_instant`, with no temporary sort. On this two-folder fixture the
  wall clock is flat (112 → 114 ms over 20×); the win is the removed sort and
  deterministic instant order, not a measured speedup here. A mixed
  dated/undated regression test pins `''` last.
- **Company profiles have no sort.** `companyProfileRowsQuery` is the named
  owner of the counterpart-pair statement and has no `ORDER BY`; every
  accumulator is order-independent. The old ordered statement is a test-only

  instants, matching the old ordered output. Row read 197–210 ms → 168–179 ms

- **Route page pins its access path and owns one total.** The page statement
  carries `INDEXED BY route_answers_by_fingerprint`, so message-id order is
  the access path regardless of statistics; the total uses the same from and
  predicate and is cached per mail generation, route generation, fingerprint

  route rows: warm page 0.31–0.54 ms vs 30–52 ms for the old count+page pair;
  the first page still pays the 34–44 ms count. Count equals the page total,

  the JSON digest bytes against the old SQL on dated/undated, sent/received,
  attachment, unread, equal-instant, hidden and unthreaded mail;
  `TestCompanyProfilesMatchTheOrderedQuery` compares full profiles against
  the ordered oracle; plan tests reject `TEMP B-TREE`, `MATERIALIZE`,

  states 99–140 ms (flat plan-only win), full five-profile batch 0.69–1.46 s
  (the pair query alone is 168–192 ms), warm route page 0.31–0.54 ms.
