## 2026-11-03 — Sync cursors commit after removals; a partial store view never deletes

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103070327`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot 13.06 s;
  priority 9.23 s, triage page 7.60 s, home 5.69 s, learning 4.30 s,
  companies 3.72 s, conversations 2.12 s, summary 1.75 s, semantic 1.25 s,
  mail 0.32 s, agenda 0.010 s, commitments 0.023 s. RSS **758 MB**
  (private 780 MB), 39 threads.
- **Cursors are staged, not written per folder.** `syncFolder` now returns
  its next cursor; `syncFolders` stages it only when the folder delivered a
  complete snapshot, and commits every staged cursor of every complete store
  in one transaction through `store.SetCursors` after the removal pass
  succeeds. `SetCursor` is deleted (no remaining caller). A run that fails or
  is cancelled before that pass commits none, so an unchanged connector
  returns the snapshot again on the next run and the removal is retried
  instead of being lost forever.
- **A partial store view cannot classify a move as a delete.** Per store,
  every discovered folder must either deliver a complete snapshot or be
  verified unchanged; a failed folder or an incomplete snapshot makes the
  view partial. That store's removals and all its cursors are skipped (an id
  absent from one folder may have moved into the folder the run could not
  read); other stores proceed. This also covers a folder discovery no longer
  returns: it still carries its store, so a vanished folder with a failed
  sibling keeps its rows until a complete run, while a store whose folders
  are all gone (no partial view) is removed. Pinned by
  `TestVanishedFolderCarriesItsStore` and
  `TestVanishedFolderInAnIncompleteStoreKeepsItsRows`.
- **Evidence.** New deterministic tests: `TestRemovalFailureDoesNotCommitCursor`
  (a SQLite trigger fails the DELETE; the cursor stays `v0` and the message
  survives; the next run removes it and commits `v1`),
  `TestSuccessfulRunCommitsAllCursors`, `TestCursorCommitIsAtomic`,
  `TestMoveIntoAFailedFolderKeepsTheRow` (the row and its label survive, no
  cursor of the store advances, the next complete run reconciles the move),
  `TestIncompleteSnapshotDoesNotAdvanceCursor`,
  `TestOtherStoreStillRemovesWhenOneStoreIsIncomplete`,
  `TestSetCursorsSkipsEmptyAndIsAtomic`. `go test ./internal/syncer
  ./internal/store ./internal/source/... ./cmd/mailsense ./internal/api
  -count=1` green; gofmt/vet clean.
- **Open:** a crash before the cursor transaction loses only staged cursors
  and re-upserts idempotently; after it, safe because removals already ran.
  A connector that never delivers a snapshot keeps its store partial by
  design (removals and cursors wait). `RunFolders` (a partial selection) also
  leaves its store partial, so only full runs advance cursors; its only
  non-test caller is a live Windows search fixture.

## 2026-11-03 — One busy policy for every bounded store write

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103065147`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot 13.14 s;
  priority 9.01 s, triage page 7.70 s, home 5.70 s, learning 4.39 s,
  companies 3.81 s, conversations 2.24 s, summary 1.92 s, semantic 1.04 s,
  mail 0.79 s, agenda 0.010 s, commitments 0.023 s. RSS **753 MB**
  (private 775 MB), 39 threads. `/api/settings` reports the pair under
  **Storage** with defaults 4 attempts / 250 ms.
- **Three retry policies became one.** `internal/store/busy.go` owns
  `BusyPolicy.WithBusyRetry`: run the write, return non-busy errors at once,
  retry only `IsBusy` while attempts remain and the context is alive, wait
  through the store clock, and after the budget return `ErrStoreBusy` naming
  the write and wrapping the busy cause (no SQL text or values). It reads the
  existing `index.store_busy_attempts` / `index.store_busy_delay` pair on
  every call — the keys are not restart-required, so a runtime change applies
  to the next write — keeps their historical prefix, and moves to the
  **Storage** settings group; both descriptions (and the French catalog) now
  state that the pair governs every bounded store retry.
- **Every listed writer uses it.** Sync `UpsertMessages`, index
  `SaveEmbeddings`/`ConfirmEmbeddings`, triage `SaveDecisions`/`SaveFailure`,
  label `PutLabels`/`PutLabel`/`DeleteLabel` (the layer-1 judge writes through
  `PutLabels`), scope `WriteVerdicts`, and `AddUsage`. Reads are untouched;
  `CommitLayer1` keeps its own short lock and is never re-run. The indexer's
  `writeBusy` loop is deleted; `index.ErrStoreBusy` is now the store
  sentinel, so `stopped_by=store_busy`, the report's no-quarantine rule and
  the existing index busy tests are unchanged.
- **Triage keeps the paid answer.** The retry is around the decision write,
  not the provider call. A decision whose write still stays busy is recorded
  through `SaveFailure` and counted failed, never decided; the message is
  picked up by the next run. Usage stays best-effort: a final failure logs
  one warning with provider and model only.
- **Evidence.** New tests: `TestBusyRetryCompletesAfterLockRelease`,
  `TestBusyRetryStopsOnCancel`, `TestBusyRetryDoesNotRetryOtherErrors`,
  `TestBusyRetryReadsTheSettingPerCall`,
  `TestTriageDoesNotLoseADecisionOnBusy` (released inside the budget: one
  decision, no failure; exhausted: failure recorded, message pending),
  `TestSyncFlushRetriesBusy`; the three existing index busy tests still pass.
  `go test ./internal/store ./internal/syncer ./internal/triage
  ./internal/index ./internal/layer1 ./internal/api ./cmd/mailsense
  -count=1` green; `go test ./internal/config ./internal/ui -count=1` green;
  `go vet` clean on the same packages.
- **Open:** a lock held longer than `store.busy_timeout × attempts + delays`
  still fails the write. The layer-1 commit bounds its own lock by staging
  answers, not by this policy. A usage record is still lost (with one
  warning) if its write never succeeds; a durable outbox is not in this
  round.

## 2026-11-03 — Layer-1 commit stages answers off the write lock

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103063944`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh /
  0 incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot 13.66 s;
  priority 9.48 s, triage page 7.97 s, home 6.01 s, learning 4.48 s,
  companies 3.71 s, conversations 2.05 s, summary 1.97 s, semantic
  1.57 s, mail 0.38 s, agenda 0.007 s, commitments 0.020 s. RSS
  **755 MB** (private 778 MB), 38 threads.
- **The lock is now short and bounded.** `CommitLayer1` used to stream the
  whole answer phase (~15 s on a large mailbox) inside one
  `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so sync, triage, Ask history, labels and usage
  waited out `store.busy_timeout` and aborted. The production
  `Layer1Answers` form now takes one dedicated connection, fills a TEMP
  table shaped exactly like `Layer1Answer` from `Answers.Each` in bounded
  128-row batches (no main-database lock), then runs one short
  transaction on the same connection: promote/retire/meta, replay the
  staged rows in `message_id` order through the existing
  `streamLayer1Answers`/`writeAnswerRow` seen and prune logic, and the
  run report. `inTx` now delegates to `inTxOn`, so there is one
  transaction policy, not a fork.
- **Measured, not asserted.**
  `TestLayer1CommitTransactionSpanExcludesAnswers` (200 messages,
  each answer phase delayed 3 ms) reports answer phase **629 ms** and
  commit transaction **21.7 ms** (the writer's earlier run: 5–9 ms
  before prune). `TestLayer1CommitDoesNotHoldTheWriteLockDuringAnswers`
  blocks `Each` after one row with `max_open_conns: 2` and
  `busy_timeout: 1s`: a concurrent `UpsertMessages` and `PutLabel`
  complete while it is blocked, then the commit succeeds with the
  expected decisions, routes and report. Staging failure leaves the main
  database untouched; a short-transaction failure rolls back every
  answer table and the run row.
- **Open:** the legacy separate `Decisions`/`Routes`/`Preview` streams
  still run inside one transaction (only the production one-pass form is
  staged). A very large staged replay still holds the write lock for its
  INSERT…SELECT span (~1.2 s reported at 35k rows); the commit also
  holds one pooled connection for the whole answer phase, which at
  `store.max_open_conns: 1` waits for that connection. `streamLayer1Answers`
  inserts each message into the seen table twice (the outer add plus
  `writeAnswerRow`); collapsing that is a measured follow-up, not a
  correctness change.

## 2026-11-03 — Threat is a judgment, not a subject; automated service mail owns no action

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103062203`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview false (the one rule), summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible /
  34,763 fresh / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot 13.04 s; priority 9.07 s,

  conversations 2.18 s, summary 1.71 s, semantic 1.22 s, mail 0.98 s,
  agenda 0.01 s, commitments 0.02 s. RSS 769 MB (private 794 MB).
- **Two classification defects fixed at the action owner.**
  `security` is a subject category; only `Suspicious == 1` now produces
  `Verify` and the +100 threat score. The category no longer adds 60
  points, forces inclusion, or matches the security filter (spam remains
  a threat class). `Automated` now reads the independent
  `relationship=automated_service` answer as well as the bulk
  categories, and `Bulk` suppresses the veto when `Suspicious == 1`.
  Automated rows are excluded before scoring, so urgency, deadline, CTA,
  reply or decision can no longer force a receipt or service alert into
  Important.

  `filter=all|security` returned 46 rows both before and after, with
  reply/urgent/decision at 0. Inspecting the rows shows the ranking
  currently holds only genuine threat decisions: message 20654 is
  `suspicious=yes` (0.72; its body contains a password) with every other
  question `not_certified`, and its action is `read` because the thread
  was already answered. The 46 rows are not the old category bonus; they
  are the only certified signal under the current route key. The unit
  tests prove the category/automated change on constructed evidence; the
  live dataset has no certified non-suspicious item to show it.
- **Proof.** `TestSecurityCategoryWithoutSuspicionIsNotVerify`,
  `TestAutomatedServiceRelationshipVetoesAction`,
  `TestBulkMailWithUrgentOrDeadlineDoesNotEnterImportant`,
  `TestFilterSecurityIsThreatBased`, the extended automated test, and the
  updated precedence/weight tests; gate 80b fast + 73/73 UI. The new
  priority tests live in `priority_threat_test.go`, keeping
  `priority_test.go` under its reviewed line budget.
- **Open:** the live ranking is threat-only because the route answers
  under the current key are `not_certified` for every other question;
  this is the known layer-1 certification-data gap, not a filter bug.
  Existing cached rankings rebuild on the next priority generation.

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103060037`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh / 0 failed /

  persisted identity a verdict judged (the addresses and subaddress
  separators); `syncer.identityDigest` is gone. `SyncProgress` uses the same

  summing per store in Go, so an owner change no longer reports the store as
  judged and `SyncStage` cannot report Done while scope still owes work.

  `TestSQLVocabularyMatchesDomainConstants`; `go test ./internal/scope
  ./internal/syncer ./internal/store ./internal/messages ./internal/api
  ./cmd/mailsense -count=1` green.
- **Open:** an identity change still re-judges the whole store; this round

## 2026-11-03 — Attachment completeness: a transient item error no longer deletes stored files

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103055212`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh / 0 failed /
  1 unjudged). Boot 14.82 s; priority 10.40 s, triage page **7.59 s**,
  home 5.58 s, learning 4.30 s, companies 4.04 s, conversations 2.49 s,
  summary 1.68 s, semantic 1.20 s, commitments 0.95 s, agenda 0.90 s,
  mail 0.96 s. RSS **766 MB** (private 788 MB).
- **The defect (data loss, reproduced).** `outlook.attachments()` broke
  out of the attachment loop on an item read error or nil and returned the
  prefix with success. `mail.Details` then marked the message complete,
  and the store's authoritative replace deleted the missing rows and
  pruned their content-addressed blobs. A transient COM error permanently
  lost attachment metadata and inline images.
- **The fix at the connector owner.** A failed or nil
  `Attachments.Item` now returns an error naming the index and count; the
  item stays partial and the next pass retries. Only an absent attachment
  collection is an empty list. The store's replace stays authoritative;
  the completeness contract is documented at `mail.Details`,
  `ApplyDetails`, `replaceAttachments`, `docs/OUTLOOK_SYNC.md` and
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Proof.** `TestDetailItemFailureKeepsStoredAttachments` and
  `TestDetailNilItemIsAFailure` run the real connector → syncer → store
  from three stored attachments (the second an inline PNG), then fail the
  second item on the detail pass. Before: 3 rows → 1, inline blob pruned,
  `partial=0`. Now: 3 rows kept, the PNG bytes still resolve, `partial=1`,
  `Failed=1`, pending for the next run. `go test
  ./internal/source/outlook ./internal/mail ./internal/store
  ./internal/syncer` green.
- **Other connectors checked:** only Outlook implements `DetailReader`;
  rfc5322/archive have no transient prefix path.
- **Open:** an individual property-accessor failure still degrades an
  attachment to minimal metadata without bytes (the documented
  absent-property policy); separating transient from absent there needs
  live evidence.

  triage page fell 8.03 → 7.63 s.
- **Proof the projection cannot silently zero a field.**
  `TestThreadsProjectionIncludesEveryReadField` compares a sentinel-filled
  full read with the projected read through `FromMail`;
  `TestThreadsLoadMatchesFullRead` compares the whole analysis on a
  fixture; `TestThreadsLoadSelectsOnlyItsFields` rejects `body_html`, the
  item subqueries and 33 omitted columns. A removed field fails the first
  two.
- **Storage defaults are baseline again.** The SQLite round shipped
  8 MiB cache / 256 MiB mmap; the mmap is per connection, so four maps
  dominated the working set (1,480 MB). The measured sweep (see the
  previous entry) selected **cache 2 MiB / mmap 0**; the shipped defaults
  now match, and the live app runs them. Both settings remain exposed
  for measured tuning.
- **Open:** the threads read still carries recipients (the excerpt/thread
  path needs them); the triage core build remains the largest boot
  component; the conversation digest, company profiles and route page are
  the next hot-read targets.

## 2026-11-03 — SQLite storage tuning: exposed, measured, and defaulted back

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103053125`**: 12/12 views, gate open,
  preview on, summary wire unchanged (34,764 eligible / 34,763 fresh / 0
  incomplete / 0 stale / 0 failed / 1 unjudged). Boot **13.76 s** (from
  14.72 s); priority **9.62 s** (from 10.41 s), triage page 8.03 s,
  companies 3.75 s, learning 3.08 s, home 3.79 s, conversations 2.21 s,
  agenda 0.72 s, mail 0.55 s, semantic 0.69 s.
- **Two settings now exist at the storage owner**: `store.cache_size_mb`
  (per pooled connection) and `store.mmap_size_mb`, both applied in the
  DSN so every pooled connection gets them. Pinned by
  `TestStoragePragmasApplyToEveryConnection` (two connections, both
  pragmas) plus a default-open assertion.
- **The 256 MiB mmap default was rejected on measurement.** With the
  shipped 8 MiB cache + 256 MiB mmap the process reached **1,480 MB**
  working set (private 881 MB) after boot. Live sweeps on the same build:
  mmap 0 / cache 8 = **828 MB**; mmap 32 / cache 8 = 850 MB; mmap 64 /
  cache 8 = 884 MB; cache 2 / mmap 0 = **776 MB**. The mapping is per
  connection, so 4 × 256 MiB maps dominate the working set. The speed
  difference between cache 2 and cache 8 was inside boot noise
  (priority 10.4 s both), so the defaults are **cache 2 MiB, mmap 0** —
  SQLite's own baseline — and both settings stay exposed for measured
  tuning. The live app was reset to those values; the schema defaults
  change ships in the next gated build.
- **Open:** the pre-round 579 MB reading was taken immediately after boot;
  the comparable steady-state baseline (30 s idle) is now **776 MB**.
  The next resource round measures steady state consistently. Cache and
  mmap remain per-connection; a future tuning round must report RSS and
  boot together, never one alone.

## 2026-11-03 — Honest certification, single-scan ranking and single owners

- **Deployed `0.1.0-dev+20261103031035`, `+20261103032037`,
  `+20261103032721`, `+20261103033425`, `+20261103033811`,
  `+20261103034151`, `+20261103035724`, `+20261103040131`,
  `+20261103040731`, `+20261103041102`, `+20261103041416`,
  `+20261103042139`, `+20261103042930`, `+20261103043636`,
  `+20261103044205`, `+20261103045836` and `+20261103050348`**: each booted
  12/12 views with the gate open and preview on. The last boot took 15.1 s
  with Triage Summary (1.7 s), Triage Page (8.8 s) and Home (5.4 s)
  overlapping priority (10.9 s) instead of waiting for it.
- **Triage summary is one aggregate.** `store.RouteCoverage` computes the
  summary population, coverage and freshness in one SQL statement over the
  existing `MessageFilter` predicate: no `MessageRefs` materialisation and
  no per-answer Go decode. `buildSummary` maps it and keeps the wire shape,
  including `failed` (read from `triage_failures` under its own
  fingerprint/decider — route rows and failures use different keys). On the
  33,416-message fixture the read went from 587 ms and ~545 MB allocated to
  417 ms and ~13 KB, with 102 allocations; the live summary reports
  34,764 eligible / 34,763 covered / 0 stale / 0 partial / 0 failed /
  1 unjudged. Pinned by `TestRouteCoverageMatchesTheGoSummary` (computes
  both implementations) and `TestTriageSummaryCountsFailures`. **Honest
  boot result:** `triage_summary` stayed at 10.0 s because the summary
  still calls `prepareRoute` → `buildCore`, which loads the whole causal
  thread analysis, behaviour, priors and history just to count coverage;
  the next round gives the summary a profile-and-identity session that does
  not build the analysis.
- **Certification is one predicate.** `selective.Answering` is the one
  answer gate used by the route, the requirement verdict and the learning
  stage. A certified route whose coverage lower bound misses the minimum
  now abstains as `below_coverage`, distinct from `not_certified`; preview
  replaces only the latter. The displayed class is the class
  `selective.Decide` chose; the prior stays diagnostic.
- **Standardisation belongs to one fit.** The design no longer carries a
  mean/σ computed over every row (which included the certification rows).
  Each fit computes its own standardiser from the examples it trains on,
  and a contract test proves a held-out row cannot move a weight.
- **The label queue survives a label click.** Warm reads no longer build a
  `Plan`, the member population follows `MailGeneration` only, and one
  label-independent candidate order is reused while the current labels
  filter it at read time. A label write cannot re-rank the mailbox.
- **Priority ranks one coherent scan.** The metadata second pass and its
  union fallback are gone: the rows, signals and recorded generations come
  from the same scan, so a snapshot can no longer mix generations. A
  generation change serves the current snapshot and refreshes behind it.
- **Single owners.** The UI cache key has one format (`cacheKey`); a mailbox
  list has one response (`writeMailboxes`); the log SSE frame uses
  `logx.TopicEntry`; `evidence.ReasonSent` aliases `scope.ReasonSentByOwner`;
  `mailquery.AgendaHorizonMax` derives from `agenda.MaxHorizon`; the
  migration’s layer-1 state CHECK is pinned to `store.Layer1*`;
  `docs/API.md` must name every `commitments.Kind`.
- **Roles and the agenda default come from their owners.** `subject` and
  `priority` resolve question names through the profile’s role map, so a
  supported rename/removal reaches both. `agenda.default_hours` is applied
  by the server (`horizon_hours`), the UI’s first read omits `hours`, the
  chips include the configured value, and the setting is honestly
  `restart_required`.
- **UX truth batch.** Settings keep focus after a row rebuild; a partial
  provider-role save invalidates and names the stored roles; the log pause
  glyph follows its label, Clear resets the ring meta and `aria-controls`
  names a row only while it exists; a stale Brief says it is updating and
  Mark seen announces the stored boundary.
- **Certification and counts stay honest.** The short-evaluation training
  branch now fits only the rows outside the certification part, so a
  threshold-free head cannot memorise its own certification labels. A
  score’s level is `selective.Decided`, the same class Mail and Triage
  display. An aggregate count that named an entity returns a retrieval
  notice when the strict resolver fails instead of a mailbox-wide total.
  A non-empty unreadable 2xx body is an `invalid_response`, never a cached
  empty success.
- **Gate 60 UI truth batch.** A settings control keeps its description as

  block of its `sr-only` label, so the hidden label cannot grow the

  owner, and All Mail shows the active sender as a removable chip. The
  stale job-name and sender-chip expectations were reconciled with the
  intended behavior.
- **A panic finalizes its single-flight.** One `internal/safe` recovery
  owner turns a panic into an error, and every latch that used to wait
  forever now clears itself and closes its waiters: the triage view cache,
  the label queue, the messages first-page flight and the company book,
  including their background refreshes. The job panic log carries the type
  and stack, never the panic value, so mail content cannot leak through it.
- **Priority timestamps are the snapshot’s.** `priority.Page` carries the
  build time of the snapshot that produced it; the API no longer stamps a
  fresh request time on a stale-while-revalidate serve.
- **Storage stays bounded.** `store.retain.triage_keys` (default 3) prunes
  old question-spec/decider answer caches during maintenance; the calendar

  `TestCalendarWindowReplaceAndRead`.
- **The label request can open the gate, and buys only what can certify.**
  The static request is no longer capped at 2,000 labels: the shipped

  remains” while it still needed hundreds of answers. One owner,
  `Requirement.LabelNeed`, returns `{Need, Fixable}` from the observed
  certification: the request scales with the measured error rate and
  certified coverage, keeps the static design count as the measure, and is
  unfixable when the observed precision is below the target or the honest
  search (bounded at 1,000,000 labels) cannot reach it. The labels stage
  excludes unfixable questions from progress and blockers, the verdict
  reports `remaining: 0`, and the auto-label loop therefore buys nothing
  for them. Settle reports its own position (`Done: i`) instead of the
  finished total, and `docs/LAYER1.md` and `docs/API.md` state the same
  contract. **Live follow-up:** `+20261103043636` read the layer-1 answer
  certification (urgency 96.3 %, 486 answered) while the questions stage
  read the route certification (85.9 %, 894 answered), so the labels stage
  asked 9,764 for a route that more labels cannot improve. `+20261103044205`
  (deployed) makes both stages read `last.Routes[].Certification` through
  one `routeCertifications` helper; the layer-1 verdict's
  `request_labels`/`remaining` stay training-stage diagnostics. A report
  with no route entry falls back to its verdict and says so. Live: urgency
  and deadline are excluded as unfixable, `has_signature` remains a fixable
  3,115-label request, and the questions stage still reports the 85.9 %
  route precision. Pinned by `TestLabelsStageUsesRouteCertification` and
  `TestQuestionsStageUsesRouteLabelNeed`.
- **Repeated work removed.** A cold company profile installs its route
  generation, so the next read does not rebuild it. `ThreadStates` returns
  the immutable ranking snapshot instead of copying it. Priority parses a
  message’s instant once and reuses it for the rollup and the ordering. The
  USD formatter reuses one `Intl.NumberFormat` per locale and precision.
- **Important pages honestly.** `/api/priority` now carries
  `offset`/`available`/`has_more`; the list pages through the top-200
  ranked snapshot with a server-owned offset. The UI shows “50 of 120”
  (and names the top-200 cap when `total` is larger), appends only unseen
  message ids, keeps keyboard focus on Load more, and refuses to splice a
  different snapshot. Pinned by the Go paging/cap tests and the new
  Playwright spec.
- **Shutdown joins producers before the store closes.** The API admits each
  request through one handler gate, refuses new ones with `503
  shutting_down`, and joins every admitted handler; a handler that outlives
  the deadline is `api.ErrHandlersUnjoined`. `jobs.CancelAll` runs
  immediately after the signal so a handler waiting on a job can return
  during the API join; `jobs.Shutdown` reports `jobs.ErrUnjoined` and
  `priority.Close` reports whether its builds joined. `main` keeps the store
  and the instance lock open when any bounded join fails and exits 1
  (SQLite replays the WAL next start); otherwise it closes normally. Both
  new regressions (a handler and a job that ignore cancellation) failed
  before the patch and pass after it.
- Evidence: gates 54–66 green (fast suite + 73/73 UI). Gate 60’s five UI
  regressions were fixed at their owners and re-verified by gate 60b.
- Open: live Triage stays empty until the next layer-1 pass commits under
  the current `rk1-` key; a genuinely huge honest label request can exceed
  the judge budget (a budget decision, not a silent cap); triage summary still
  scans/decodes every route answer; there is no backup/restore path; the

## 2026-11-03 — Store hardening and the feature layout in the route key

- **Sender pages use the sender index.** `MessageList` hard-pinned every
  page to `messages_instant`, so an exact-sender page scanned and filtered
  the owner population even though migration 0031 shipped
  `messages_sender_norm`/`messages_sender_domain` in keyset order. The page
  now chooses its index from the same `senderFilterOf` that builds the
  predicate; the EXPLAIN test runs the real page join for exact and domain
  senders and requires no temporary sort.
- **Triage key reads have their index.** Migration 0032 adds
  `triage_decisions_by_key(fingerprint, decider, message_id, decided_at)` and
  `triage_failures_by_key(fingerprint, decider)`: the primary key starts with
  message_id, so every per-teacher read, count and prune was a table scan.
- **Calendar window replacement is per calendar.** The range delete matched
  only source+store, so syncing one calendar wiped every sibling calendar's
  events in the same store. It now matches `calendar_id`; a two-calendar
  regression test pins it.
- **A message deleted after the id snapshot no longer rolls back the
  commit.** Decision, route, preview and failure inserts are
  `INSERT … SELECT … WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM messages WHERE id = ?)`,
  evaluated under the commit's write lock: a stale id is skipped atomically
  instead of failing the whole layer-1 transaction on the foreign key.
- **One compact-fold owner and a zone cache.** `mail.CompactFold` replaces
  the two byte-identical private helpers; `clock.Zone` memoizes successful
  loads (Ask and the world/company views resolved the same zone file per
  request).
- **Feature layout is a route-key input.** `evidence.FeaturesDigest` covers
  the merged bins document, the signal schema (versions, settings and pinned
  data) and `evidence.features.hash_buckets`; the route key carries it and
  the two feature settings are in the trigger list. A bins edit in place or
  a bucket change now moves the key and makes the next pass retrain instead
  of silently reusing a model whose layout changed.
- Evidence: `internal/{store,clock,mail,contacts,layer1,triage,priority,brief,commitments,api,hub,search,qa}` and `cmd/mailsense` green; gate 42 covers the integrated tree.
- Open: deploy. Calendar scope/retention and owner-identity parity remain
  separate rounds.

## 2026-11-03 — Performance fixtures and route-derived caches use the real key

- **The benchmark no longer measures an empty routed page.** The fixture
  prepare wrote route rows under the legacy profile fingerprint while the app
  reads `layer1.RouteKey()`. It moved to `internal/perfprepare` (the triage
  package cannot import layer1, which imports triage) and computes the key
  from the same owner; the priority benchmark resolves the key the same way
  instead of a literal. `bench-perf.sh` now asks `/api/triage` once and fails
  when the prepared page has no rows, so a key mismatch is a hard error, not
  a fast empty page.
- **Route-derived caches follow the route generation.** Priority's ranking
  snapshot records the mail and route generations it sampled and compares
  both before reuse; Commitments keys its snapshot on both (its decision
  source is the route); Brief keys on both. A re-score or a new layer-1 pass
  that writes answers under the same configuration no longer serves the
  previous view for the whole TTL. Each cache records the generations it
  sampled and installs only while they still match, so a write during a
  rebuild is never trusted.
- Evidence: `internal/{priority,brief,commitments}` green; the fixture-tagged
  `internal/perfprepare` compiles and vets. Gate 41 covers the integrated
  tree.
- Open: deploy; feature-layout inputs (`evidence.features.file`,
  `hash_buckets`) are not yet route-key inputs.

## 2026-11-03 — One owner for the pre-gate label read

- **The flag alone no longer unlocks a message.** `GET /api/messages/{id}`
  with `for=label` was readable before the gate for any id. The handler now
  asks the label-queue owner (`layer1.Runner.QueueContains`) whether the
  same queue page the label screen holds (question, effective limit, review
  mode) offers that message; otherwise it answers the ordinary
  `423 learning_locked` gate error. The queue is the cached one the screen
  already read, so the check is a scan of that page, not a second build.
- **One query builder in the client.** `messagePath` in `13-shell.js` is the
  owner of the label-read query; the label screen passes `task.question`,
  `queueLimit` and `review`, so it can never request a page it did not load.
  A regression contract pins both sides. `docs/API.md` records the binding.
- **Route-key hardening from the independent verification.** The label-queue
  cache key now includes `plan.RouteKey()` (an evidence-rules edit is a key
  input but is not a file stamp and does not bump the route generation
  until a commit); `Read`/`Result`/`Results`/`Analytics` fail closed without
  a keyer instead of dereferencing nil; `pruneAnswerTable` refuses an empty
  key (an exported prune could otherwise delete every route row); triage
  fixtures commit and read under a distinct `rk1-` test key so a fallback to
  the paid fingerprint fails the suite; `trainer` names its paid SubQ key
  `subqKey`.
- Evidence: `internal/{api,layer1,triage,store,priority,ui}` green; the
  first-run e2e probes (`long content scrolls`, fixture contract) pass 2/2;
  gate 40 covers the integrated tree.
- Open: deploy the route-key build; the first pass under `rk1-` must finish
  before triage shows rows. Benchmark fixtures still write the legacy key
  (`triage/perf_fixture_test.go`, `priority/bench_fixture_test.go`), so perf
  runs can measure empty pages.

## 2026-11-03 — Route key covers every decision input

- **Two keys, two facts.** Paid decisions stay under
  `store.TriageKey{profile fingerprint, decider}`; route and preview rows
  live under `layer1.Plan.RouteKey()` (`rk1-` + 32 hex). The route key
  covers the full profile (not only its questions object), the merged
  teachers and requirements, the decider and its tolerance, the algorithm
  and feature versions, the merged evidence rules, the folder roles and
  every route-affecting setting. The legacy 12-hex fingerprint remains the
  paid-decision, judge and import identity.
- **One owner per piece.** `Profile.Digest()` (taxonomy), `RuleSet.Digest`
  and `RulesDigest(cfg)` (evidence), and `Plan.RouteKey()` (layer1) own the
  components. Triage and priority receive the key through one injected
  `RouteKeyer`/function at startup, because layer1 imports triage's
  finished topic; a routed triager without a keyer fails closed instead of
  falling back to the legacy fingerprint.
- **A key change is a run input.** `Report.RouteKey` is stored, the run
  fingerprint includes the route key, `triggerKeys` is derived from the
  same setting list as the key, and the route stage blocks a report from
  another configuration. Old route rows become unreachable at once and are
  pruned by the next successful commit.
- **Two real bugs found by the split.** The one-pass commit path (the
  production one) never bumped `RouteGeneration`, so a committed route
  kept serving cached pages and label queues for the TTL; fixed with a
  regression test. A nil decisions stream panicked the legacy commit path;
  it now leaves its table untouched, like the route and preview streams.
- Evidence: `internal/{store,layer1,triage,priority,api,hub,search,qa,agenda}`
  and `cmd/mailsense` green; gate 38 below.
- Open: the first pass under the new key must complete before triage shows
  rows; the live count is 0 until then. The route key is computed per page
  and ranking read (a Plan construction); measure it and cache under a
  content digest if it shows up.

## 2026-11-03 — Family-wise certification quantile

- **The target is now a family-wise statement.** `Requirement.FamilyWise`
  (shipped `true`) derives `ZEffective` once at parse time from the profile's
  question count: a two-sided Bonferroni correction,
  `z_eff = Φ⁻¹(1 − (1−Φ(z))/m)`. With 17 questions the shipped `z: 1.96`
  becomes **2.9738**; a document that sets `family_wise: false`, or a
  `Requirement` built directly, keeps its uncorrected z.
- **One effective quantile reaches every bound.** The model holdout, the
  route build, the training reports and the questions-stage blocker all read
  `EffectiveZ()`; `Verdict` carries `z` (effective), `z_base` and
  `family_wise`, so the report can no longer show a bound at one quantile
  while claiming another.
- **The correction changes verdicts, not only labels.** A reproduced
  953/982 certification (lower 0.9579 at z 1.96) falls to 0.9497 at z 2.9738
  and no longer certifies at 0.95 (`TestFamilyWiseBoundMovesCertification`).
  At 0.99 the zero-error need rises from 381 to **876** certification labels;
  the static label request (3,504 before the cap) now hits the existing
  2,000-label cap, which the next label-budget round must resolve honestly.
- **Synthetic fixtures opt out explicitly.** Fixtures that assert
  per-question behavior now write `family_wise: false`; the shipped-document
  and correction tests keep the correction on. `internal/mathx` gained the
  normal CDF/quantile primitive with boundary tests.
- **Evidence.** `go test ./internal/mathx ./internal/selective ./internal/route
  ./internal/triage ./internal/api ./internal/hub` and `./internal/layer1`
  green; full gate 33 below.
- Open: the live Hub count still reflects the last run; a new layer-1 run is
  required before the corrected certificates appear. The report still does
  not distinguish untested from 0 % precision, the coverage bound is still a
  point estimate, and the route key still hashes questions only.

## 2026-11-03 — Mail consistency and certification isolation

- **An HTML detail no longer ships the duplicate plain body.** `MessageView`
  projects `message.body` away when `body_html` is non-empty; a plain
  message keeps its canonical text. `MessageWire.Body` is `omitempty`, and
  the handler applies the one `ProjectBody` policy.
- **Mail reads follow sync and backfill.** `sync.mailboxes` now drops the
  message reads and resets the local All-Mail model; a finished
  `messages.html` job drops only the message-detail reads. The gate read is
  cached for a tab switch and invalidated with the learning reads.
- **Certification labels no longer choose the route.** `route.Build` chooses
  the member set on the selection part (selection coverage at the target,
  then more members on a tie) and certifies that set once on the
  certification part. A key that is wrong only on certification labels can
  no longer be dropped from the cascade; the route stays uncertified and
  abstains. This removes the certification-data selection bias the audit
  reproduced.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (67 specs) green; deployed build `0.1.0-dev+20261103014336` (PID 12204,
  12/12 views, `learned`, Hub 2/17, HTML detail `body_format=html`,
  `body_html` present, `message.body` absent).
- Open: the report still needs family-wise correction (P0-1), a tested/
  coverage-bound distinction (P1-5), and a route key that covers the full
  decision inputs (P0-4). The current 2/17 is from the previous run and will
  move only on the next layer-1 run.

## 2026-11-03 — Payload projections, Logs delta, Ask history detail

- **The Recent list is a projection.** `triage.Page.Results` now carries
  `PageRow` (answered/first_question/first_value/missing/stale/decided_at/
  escalate/failure/preview); the full value map stays on
  `/api/triage/{id}`. A 50-row page no longer ships ~60-70 KB of unread
  answer JSON, and the UI reads the same first value it rendered before.
- **Dead payload removed.** `/api/answers` no longer carries the question
  `type` (the UI resolves it from `/api/questions`), `LabelSummary` no
  longer duplicates the gate blockers, and `/api/triage/summary` no longer
  ships a per-question distribution no screen reads. The answers list also
  stopped paying a `Triage.Questions` read per page.
- **The Ask history rail is a four-field projection.** `History` reads
  `id/question/mode/created_at` via `ListQASummaries`; opening a row is the
  one full read (`GET /api/ask/history/{id}` → `HistoryItem`). The list no
  longer rehydrates citations or decodes twenty answer/plan JSON blobs.
- **Logs remounts read the delta.** `state.logLast` is the cursor; a revisit
  asks `/api/logs?since=…` and only resyncs the full page when the ring
  rotated past it. The old path re-read 500 entries (~22 KB gzip) on every
  mount.
- **Field errors are bound to their control.** `markFieldError` sets
  `role=alert`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` and clears all three;
  Settings, the zone dialog and Labels use it. API conditions have one
  constructor each (`ErrUnknownSetting`, `ErrUseMailboxEndpoint`,
  `ErrUnknownCompany`).
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (67 specs) green; deployed builds `0.1.0-dev+20261103013119`,
  `+20261103013545` and `+20261103014055` (PID 10344, 12/12 views,
  `learned`, Hub 2/17, triage page keys `first_question`/`first_value`,
  history row keys `id/question/mode/created_at`).
- Open: `/api/status` no longer embeds learning (one gate view); the
  certification report still conflates model and route certification, the
  subset scan selects on the certification split, and the 0.95 target is
  not family-wise corrected. `/api/messages/{id}` still ships the duplicate
  plain body for HTML mail; All-Mail and message detail need explicit sync/
  backfill invalidation.

## 2026-11-03 — Thread policy, exact senders, plan bounds, Logs path

- **One open-thread policy and one order.** `threadintel.OpenStates`/`IsOpen`
  and `StateOrder` are read by the store profile, the world overlay and the
  Ask company facts; the display cap is `store.CompanyProfileOpenCap`. The
  same company profile can no longer order its open threads differently
  between the two assembly paths.
- **Sender questions are exact lookups.** `qa.askSender` resolves the named
  person to addresses (`PersonCandidates`), then lists received messages per
  exact address with `ExecuteMailQuery`; a name that only appears in a body
  or a recipient line is never cited as a message from that person. An
  unresolved sender gets `qa_sender_unknown`, not a silent no-match.
- **Plan bounds are published, not copied.** `mailquery.PromptSchema()` is
  generated from the validator's own constants (`MaxCompanyLimit`,
  `MaxAgendaLimit`, `AgendaHorizonMax`, defaults) and the planner prompt
  embeds it; the companies bound (1..100) and agenda/time bounds now agree
  with the prompt instead of failing as generation errors.
- **Logs typing and live traffic are bounded.** The component filter
  coalesces the 1,000-row rebuild instead of running per keystroke; the live
  ring trims in batches instead of sorting 5,000 keys per entry. A label or
  settings write invalidates shared reads and marks dependent screens stale
  instead of dropping all 24 cached screens.
- **Phone layout fixed.** At 360 px the stacked job/boot cards consumed the
  workspace and left the route 65 px tall; each strip is now a bounded
  scroller (`max-height: 20vh`), and the log table's visually-hidden caption
  is contained by its host so it cannot extend the document.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (66 specs) green; deployed build `0.1.0-dev+20261103011334` (PID 27876,
  12/12 views, `learned`, boot 20.5 s, Hub 2/17, triage 34,763 fresh).
- Open: `/api/status` still ships the full learning view; the triage page
  ships each row's full value map; the Important chips still ask for one
  page per chip (fixed in the next batch); Ask evidence has no source
  provenance and no per-conversation cap.

## 2026-11-03 — Honest answering gate, bounded retention, grounded replies

- **Certification and answering now share one predicate.** `route.State.Answering`
  is `Certified && Coverage >= MinCoverage`; the answer gate, threshold,
  route writer, report (`answering`), route stage and Hub count all read it.
  The live layer-1 run regenerated 34,763 route answers under the gate:
  17 routes, 2 answerable, **0** non-answering questions with a given answer.
- **Preview answers follow `learning.test_mode`.** A commit writes the
  threshold-free preview copy only while the test preview is on; turning it
  off clears the table at the next commit and at startup, so the disk does
  not keep a second full answer copy nobody can open.
- **Retention is bounded at its owners.** Older layer-1 run reports lose
  their mailbox-sized label digest arrays (only the newest is read); a clean
  `Close` checkpoints the WAL; an unterminated sidecar output fragment is
  capped at 64 KiB.
- **Home and Ask stop over-reading.** Home asks for the six priority rows it
  renders (Important keeps its 50-row page); Ask reads only
  `/api/settings/qa.provider` instead of the 76 KB settings document; the
  boot strip backs off to two seconds after five seconds; Companies prefetch
  warms the selected row and two neighbours, not every visible row.
- **Grounded answers are strict.** A reply with any citation marker outside
  the numbered evidence is refused (not partially grounded); a fenced JSON
  object that fails the contract is a generation failure, never prose; a
  fenced plain-text answer is still accepted with the fence removed.
- **Small accessibility batch.** A busy control restores focus when it owned
  it; agenda horizons expose `aria-pressed`; the log table has a caption and
  column scopes; the main landmark is named by the route title; two remaining
  decorative-token text uses moved to `--muted`; learned-value busy labels
  are catalog text.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (66 specs) green; deployed build `0.1.0-dev+20261103005658` (PID 28836,
  12/12 views, `learned`, boot 20.5 s); live invariant query returned zero
  violations.
- Open: company open-thread order/policy is duplicated between the store and
  the world overlay; Ask sender questions can cite a body mention; the Logs
  filter rebuilds 1,000 rows per keystroke; label/settings writes still drop
  every cached screen; the triage page ships the full answer map.

## 2026-11-03 — Frontier reads, fingerprinted assets, one action vocabulary

- **Thread states read only the evidence frontier.** The read selected body and
  headers for every conversation member (195.1 MB / 455 ms on the fixture).
  Phase 1 now reads metadata; phase 2 fetches body and headers only for the
  newest undecided member of each conversation, looping until the first
  substantive message. `threadintel.EvidenceFrontier` shares the resolver's
  one substantive rule. An oracle test covers auto-replies, trivial
  acknowledgements, attachments and the stop-at-substantive case. Fixture
  estimate: 63.6 MB (−67.4%), 10,410 evidence rows instead of 33,842.
- **Capitalized acknowledgements no longer close a thread.** `trivial` matched
  “thanks” case-sensitively, so “Thanks” became the last substantive message
  and hid the client request. The comparison folds case; a regression test
  pins it.
- **Company summaries are open-only.** A closed conversation keeps its id and
  state but its summary is never rendered. `CompanyProfileRead.OpenState` lets
  the world overlay skip those reads; the id list is unchanged.
- **Assets are content-fingerprinted.** `index.html` names each asset at its
  current `?v=`; the same map is in one meta tag for the lazily fetched
  catalog. A matching version is served immutable for a year; unversioned or
  stale URLs revalidate. `i18n.js` reads the one map instead of building a
  bare path. Tests cover every reference, the meta map, immutable headers and
  stale-version revalidation.
- **One action vocabulary.** `common.cancel`, `common.dismiss` and
  `common.load_more` replaced ten private keys; French now uses one Brief
  name, one conversation/thread term, one learning action and one “no reply”
  phrase. The settings writes share `invalidateSettingsReads`.
- **One Ask notice owner.** Eight hand-built icon/title/body notices now use
  `askNotice`, built on the shared warning banner.
- **Home never invents a generation date.** A missing `generated_at` omits the
  date instead of rendering the current time as a fact.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (66 specs) green; deployed build `0.1.0-dev+20261103003820` (PID 21876,
  12/12 views, `learned`; boot 20.7 s).
- Open: the route still answers a certified question whose coverage is below
  `min_coverage`; boot still waits for secondary agenda/company/conversation
  views; support/disk retention and API duplicate reads are under audit.

## 2026-11-03 — One row skeleton, one invalidation policy, honest cache restore

- **One mail-row skeleton.** Mail All, Search, Important and the triage list
  rendered the same avatar/sender/time/subject/snippet/reason structure four
  times. `mailRow` in `01-components.js` owns that skeleton; the four callers
  keep only their tag, href, classes, dataset, accessible name and action.
  `rows_test.go` rejects a screen that hand-builds an avatar row and pins the
  shared class contract.
- **Companies resolve priority truth once.** The world overlay already holds
  the authoritative thread assessment of every conversation the priority
  ranking covers, but the store resolved all of them again and the overlay
  discarded most. `CompanyProfileRead.SkipStates` skips exactly the covered
  conversations; summaries and the id list are unchanged. A store test
  proves one skipped state is absent, its summary survives, and every other
  state is intact.
- **Background events no longer discard mounted screens.** Route-cache
  invalidation now has two explicit operations: `invalidateRouteCache` drops
  the DOM when the markup itself is wrong (language, settings, a local write),
  while `staleRouteCache` marks only the data as advanced. A stale entry keeps
  its scroll, focus and open disclosure on the next mount and revalidates in
  place afterwards. `afterLearningDataChanged`, `index.finished`,
  `sync.mailboxes` and a remote `config.changed` use the stale path; the same
  events still drop their API reads.
- **A progress tick is not a gate change.** `scheduleLearningRefresh` compared
  the learning gate (open, state, scope) before and after the refreshed
  status and no longer drops Home, Brief, Mail or Companies when only a stage
  progressed. This was the root cause of the intermittent scroll-cache spec:
  a boot `learning.status` tick discarded the cached Hub 350 ms later.
- **The cache specs own their clock.** The two scroll specs install the
  existing fake EventSource, so a real boot refresh cannot replace the node
  under test. The app refresh stays real; the spec now tests the router's DOM
  cache instead of racing the live bus. Both specs pass 8/8 consecutive runs.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (66 specs) green; deployed build `0.1.0-dev+20261103002750` (PID 22408,
  12/12 views, `learned`).
- Open: the thread-state read still loads body and headers for every member
  (195 MB/455 ms on the fixture); thread summaries are read for conversations
  they are then discarded; assets still revalidate on every launch; the
  certified-question count still needs to be traced to the route's answering
  gate.

## 2026-11-03 — Certification honesty: preview never relabels a certified route

- **The test preview is a gate rule, not a setting.** With

  under its 1,300-line budget.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`

## 2026-11-03 — One owner per fact: sender keys, batch reads, wire contracts, a11y

- **Sender filters read stored keys (migration 0031).** The exact-sender and
  domain predicates compared `lower(trim(sender_address))`, so a sender page
  scanned the whole owner population and sorted it. `messages.sender_norm` and
  `messages.sender_domain` are written by the one message writer and indexed
  with the page order. On the 33,842-message fixture: exact sender
  **37.1 ms → 0.125 ms**, domain **44.9 ms → 0.099 ms**, both with no temp
  sort. Live schema 31 applied; `EXPLAIN` uses `messages_sender_norm`.
- **WAL settings live in the DSN.** A post-Open `PRAGMA` reached one pooled
  connection only. `storagePragmas` now emits `wal_autocheckpoint` and
  `journal_size_limit` into every connection's DSN; `checkpointIfLarge` is the
  one "over the ceiling" owner shared by startup, maintenance and the layer-1
  commit. A busy checkpoint result is an error, not success.
- **Detail reads are batched.** `ApplyDetails` loaded every update with three
  queries (row, recipients, items); 500 updates made 1,500 reads. One query
  per 200 keys now reads exactly the non-detail columns plus the message's
  further folders, and `Complete` supplies the rest. Tests pin one read for
  five keys and that folders survive while attachments are replaced.
- **Profiles are parsed once.** `taxonomy.Load` cost ~531 µs on every request
  that read the question catalogue or built a page. The parsed profile is
  cached by `{config snapshot, resolved file, SHA-256 of the merged bytes}`:
  a same-size/same-mtime edit is still seen, and a setting or file change
  rebuilds. Four tests cover the stale cases and the one-build case.
- **The triage page stops shipping the profile.** The wire carried the whole
  ~16 KB profile on every page while the screen already reads
  `/api/questions`; the page now carries answers only and the screen renders
  from the shared cached catalogue.
- **Wire projections.** `MessageWire` is the viewer contract (no raw headers,
  recipient list or connector ids); `PriorityRow` keeps the rendered fields
  and drops the classifier vector and score; `MessageListRow` drops the
  store/folder labels no list renders.
- **Accessibility.** `appendMain` captures and restores the focused row across
  cached and background repaints (never stealing focus from the search box or
  a dialog); the global search is one combobox with non-tabbable options; the
  log table has one roving tab stop with a real disclosure button; settings
  controls are named by their setting instead of "Value"; `field()` hints are
  `aria-describedby`; loading states and route skeletons announce a status;
  route segments use `aria-current` instead of tab roles without tabpanels;
  text on `--faint` moved to `--muted`.
- **i18n.** One retry wording (`common.try_again`) replaced three private
  keys; the Answers detail uses `detail.loading` with the message number; the
  French catalogue uses Réglages, triage and courriel consistently.
- **Consistency.** `reasonKind` is the one severity of a priority reason
  (deadline was warn in a badge and urgent in a row class); Companies reuses
  the shared thread-state vocabulary; one provider invalidation serves save,
  delete and role writes; Home counts use the shared stat strip; Companies,
  Brief, Labels and Ask empty/error states use the shared helpers.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  (66 specs) green; deployed build `0.1.0-dev+20261103000611` (PID 28408,
  12/12 views, `learned`).
- Open: the certification audit found honesty gaps (preview substitution while
  the gate is open, the coverage-blocked count vs the answering gate, a
  fingerprint that covers only questions, and 2-decimal formatting that makes
  0.985/0.99 look equal); the strict target remains unmet on 15 questions.

## 2026-11-02 — Measured query wins; live caches get one owner

- **The materialized instant is the only mail-time read.** `instantSQL`
  recomputed the sent/received CASE in every query, so SQLite could not use
  `messages_instant`. It is now `m.instant`. On the 33k-message fixture a 2025
  `Since` count went **47.5ms → 23.6ms**, and the newest-50 page went
  **46.4ms → 0.17ms** (index order, no temp sort). The existing
  `TestInstantSQLMatchesMailInstant` still pins the column to `mail.Instant`.
- **Attendee index.** Migration 0030 adds `event_attendees(event_id)`. Live
  schema 30 applied and `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN DELETE ...` changed from `SCAN`
  to `SEARCH ... USING INDEX event_attendees_event`; the audit's synthetic
  20k-attendee/500-event measurement was 105.6ms → 9.7ms.
- **The company book is built once per request generation.** The company list
  built a `CompanyBook` inside `ExecuteMailQuery` and again for coverage. The
  store now caches one book keyed by `MailGeneration` and the immutable
  config snapshot (declared owners and shared domains included), builds
  outside the lock, and shares it read-only. Tests pin one build, a rebuild
  after a mail write, a declared-owner change and a shared-domain change.
- **Ask entity candidates are cached per generation.** `PersonCandidates` is
  one full-mailbox scan (154ms on the fixture). It is cached by mail
  generation, folded terms and limit, with a JSON-encoded key and non-nil
  empty hits. Tests pin identity, a fresh read after a mail write, and
  selection-scoped contacts.
- **Mail counts no longer die on a label click.** `messageListCountsCached`
  keys on `MailGeneration`; a label write leaves the role counts valid, a
  mail write rebuilds them.
- **Every selection change moves the generation.** `applySelection` bumped
  only when a folder row changed, so picking a contact-only store left the
  company book and candidate caches stale. It now bumps on the scope change;
  a regression covers a selection with no folder rows.
- **UI primitives.** `lockedCard` replaces the two hand-built locked panels;
  `errorState` carries caller actions or no retry, removing three bespoke
  error states. The Logs live batch appends instead of rebuilding the table,
  and a null note no longer injects the text "null" into the scroll host (the
  6px shell overflow the boot spec caught). The mail detail skips the second
  paint when the cached message/triage/questions are the same objects; a new
  e2e test counts `srcdoc` assignments (2 before, 1 after). Job progress
  ticks no longer force `/api/learning` or invalidate eight prefixes; start
  and completion still do, and the backfill meter is patched in place.
- **The layer-1 route pass reuses its answers.** The commit's decision map
  feeds the route's offers, removing the populated re-inference and the
  duplicate `predictWith` per certified question.
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and
  `scripts/test-ui.sh` (66 specs) green; deployed build
  `0.1.0-dev+20261102225938`.

## 2026-11-02 — v3 features measured; primitives get one owner

- **The v3 features are neutral, not a regression.** Run 95 (v2) and run 96
  (v3) trained on the same 1,929 evaluation labels. Comparing the two saved
  reports per question: the certification lower bound moved by at most
  `+0.0083` (effort) and `-0.0044` (request_count); OOF accuracy is identical
  to four decimals on every question. The causal history block (`Member`
  recipients, owner-sender prior, recency, thread role) is kept because it
  is causal and did not cost precision; it did not deliver the hoped-for
  relationship/topic gain either.
- **Two precision numbers, not one.** The `/api/learning` blocker `have`
  (e.g. effort 0.776 on 868 answers) is the shipped answers measured against
  the certification labels; the run report's `certification.lower_bound`
  (e.g. effort 0.958 on 982 answers) is the model's own held-out test for
  the rows it chose to answer. They measure different populations and must
  not be compared across runs as if they were one curve. The honest target
  remains unmet: 2 of 17 questions certify at 0.95.
- **One owner per repeated fact (round 2).** UI: `warningBanner` replaces
  nine hand-built banners; `unavailableState` replaces the duplicated
  "message no longer available" panel and search stops reusing the answers
  wording; the empty-state box/icon and the page-head stat cells moved to
  `20-components.css`; the mail rows and agenda rows left the Home and
  responsive modules for the shared layer; the dead responsive duplicates
  were removed. Backend: `startWhenReady` owns the ready-wait/join shell of
  six startup workers, `repeatEvery` owns their ticker loop,
  `jobs.StartClaimed` owns claim/refuse/release, `query[T]` accepts a pool or
  a transaction and five hand-written row loops now use it,
  `mail.Setting*` owns the subject/shared-domain keys,
  `clock.SettingZone` is the only `time.zone`, and `api.invalidRange` owns
  the bounded-integer error shape (limits, offsets, horizons, months).
- **Evidence.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` (82 packages) and
  `scripts/test-ui.sh` (64 specs) green; run 96 answered 34,763/34,763 in
  12m47s and the app reached `learned`.
- Open: the strict 0.95 target is still unmet on 15 questions; the fixture
  OOF benchmark is still embedding and has no measured v2-v3 curves.

## 2026-11-02 — The classifier stops looping; the Local engine tab works

- **The loop.** Triage ran one 100-message batch every five minutes; every
  batch changed the teacher labels, and every change started a five-minute
  training pass, so the app was always "learning" and never caught up. Three
  owners changed: `triage.auto.batch` defaults to 500 and the catch-up worker
  chains the next batch as soon as the previous job ends (a backlog drains at
  the model's pace, not one batch per tick); `triage.Report.Drained()` gates
  the layer-1 trigger, so training waits for the backlog to settle; and
  `layer1.retrain.min_interval` (default 15m) defers a training request to one
  run at the end of the interval instead of restarting it after every batch.
  Live: six 500/500 batches back to back (21:00–21:06), then one layer-1 run.
- **A trigger the pause ate.** The deferred run was scheduled with a timer;
  when it fired during a judge run the pause dropped it, and a judge loop
  that kept the pause busy starved training (live: run 93 at 21:03, none
  after). A paused request now re-arms every 20 s until the pause lifts
  (`TestAPausedTriggerIsRetriedAfterTheJudge`, which fails on the old code).
- **The answer phase counts messages once.** Decisions, route answers and
  previews come from one inference pass, so `store.Layer1Answers` writes
  them in one traversal and the job reports `34,763 / 34,763 messages`
  instead of three phases (104,289 units). The store's three answer tables
  now share one descriptor (`answers_table.go`).
- **Evidence and embeddings finish.** One message the source cannot re-read
  (`m.partial=1`) held both stages at N-1/N forever. The evidence stage
  reports "1 message(s) waiting for details: their signals are partial" and
  is done; the embeddings stage accepts `searchable + partial == eligible`.
  A restart that owes an evidence run now starts it (`Engine.Ensure` +
  `startEvidenceReconcile`), and `Store.Open` closes the runs a killed
  process left "running" (live: 4 closed at the 20:55 start, evidence
  35,084/35,084 in 11 s, both stages done).
- **The saved language is applied at boot.** `52-init.js` destructured the
  language from a positional promise triple; when the learning read moved,
  the slot held `null` and a French setting came back English on every
  fresh load. The read is now named and awaited
  (`e2e/specs/language.spec.ts`, red on the old code).
- **The Local engine tab.** The runtime card was stretched by the settings
  grid (`.settings-list > .section { align-content: start }`), the tab owned
  no settings while General showed them, and the section repeated the tab
  name. The tab now renders the status card plus one "Engine settings" group
  (the schema's own descriptions), the section is named like the tab, and
  the `sidecar.variant` paragraph is a sentence again.
- **One owner per fact (dedup round).** Route answers and previews share one
  table descriptor (reads, streams, prunes); begin/finish run rows share
  `beginRun`/`finishRun`; `pruneNewest` owns the keep-newest clamp (a 0 now
  keeps one row everywhere); meta reads/writes share `readMeta`/`putMeta`;
  progress publishing is `events.PublishProgress`; `config.Change.Has`,
  `learning.WaitFor`, `learning.Unit*`, `jobs`-level settings constants
  (`index.SettingQuarantineAfter`, `triage.SettingLeaseTTL`,
  `store.SettingWALAutocheckpoint`), `api.invalidLimit`/`invalidRequest`.
  UI: one thread-state taxonomy (`answered_by_other` was "ok" in the list and
  "plain" in the card), message flags are rendered once (the detail showed
  every flag twice), `link()` honours `small`/`kind`/`icon` (34 sites asked
  for a small link and got a full-size one), one `errorState`, one
  `percentOf`, and one invalidation owner (`invalidateAllData`).
- **Settled, not looping.** Run 95 trained and answered
  `34,763 / 34,763 messages` in 9m28s (21:29:16 → 21:38:45) and the app
  entered `learned`, not `learning`: layer1 `done 17/17`, questions
  `2/17 certified at the target`, evidence and embeddings done with their
  partial warnings. A restart then started no run: the inputs were
  unchanged, so freshness kept the trained models.
- **Gates.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` 82 packages green, `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  63/63 green three runs in a row (two timing flakes fixed at their cause:
  the boot column test waits for all three bodies, the companies test polls
  the prefetched swap instead of sleeping and accepts a browser clamp when
  the screen gains room). Live build `0.1.0-dev+20261102215456`, WAL 0 MB
  after the clean shutdown, DB 2.74 GB.

## 2026-11-02 — One Home section primitive; one progress model; honest near-misses

- **Home sections are one primitive.** Every Home column — Brief, Next,
  Important mail, and the three locked-state columns — is the same
  `homeSection` builder: a kicker, one title size (19 px display), an
  optional count chip, an optional action, a two-line sub, and a body that
  owns the column's scroll. The first column's title was an 11 px
  uppercase label ("À traiter") while the other two were 18 px headings;
  it is now the same heading as the others. The middle column used to grow
  past the grid and paint under the More disclosure because its wrapper
  had no bounded height; the wrapper is a one-row grid and the body is the
  scroll owner, so a long column never overlaps the disclosure. The More
  blocks reuse the same head markup in a flat variant, and the learning
  block inside Brief is an inset (h3), not a fourth column.
- **One progress model.** `layer1` no longer has a progress type of its
  own: the run callback, the live copy and `layer1.TopicProgress` are
  `jobs.Progress`. The producer owns the unit (`questions` for every
  question phase, `messages` for the answer phase), and
  `layer1.Stage.Status` copies `unit`, `step_done` and `step_total` into
  `learning.Progress` instead of hardcoding `questions`. The job chip
  renders the unit beside the count and the Learning timeline renders the
  step, so the two cannot disagree. Live run 44: the job and the stage
  both reported `answer 47,500 / 104,289 messages` (the stage lags by the
  one-second coalesced refresh), and the run finished
  `104,289 / 104,289` in 5m22s.
- **Multi-token person names are one identity.** "qui est richard harvey"
  used to offer six one-token matches (every Richard and every Harvey) as a
  "which person?" choice. The resolver now learns the name structure from
  the address book itself: a token that appears first in a display name is
  a given name, one that appears last is a surname, and a token in both
  positions (Richard) counts as either. When the query covers both
  positions, a person must match all of its name terms or be at the
  organization the question names. If nobody does, the card says
  **Personne ne porte ce nom complet. Voulez-vous dire…** and offers at
  most four near-misses, rarest name token first. The rule is not a list of
  known questions: a test with a different address book (Marc Bélanger,
  Sophie/Julie Tremblay) proves the shape generalizes. Live: the query
  returns David Harvey, Jean-Guy Harvey, Emmanuelle Gougeon and Olivier
  Richard, in 0.9 s. The exact Simon query still answers **Simon
  Bernier / sberthier@services-exemple.test / Services Exemple / 721 messages** in
  2.1 s.
- **Gates.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` 82 packages green; `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  61/61 specs green, including a new Home test that proves all three
  columns are bounded scrollers with one title size, and the chip/timeline
  unit and step assertions.

## 2026-11-02 — Precise job progress; the first model features measured

- **The problem.** The local classifier reported one line per finished
  question, so a run that spends minutes inside a single question looked
  frozen (`has_signature` for 18 minutes). The learning timeline showed
  "pending" or "training" with no position, and the job chip had no ETA.
- **One progress shape.** `jobs.Progress` now carries `stage` (a catalog
  key), `detail` (the current item: a question name, data not a
  sentence), `step_done`/`step_total` and `eta`. The ETA is measured
  once, by the manager, from each job's own average rate since it
  started; a producer that measures a better one overrides it.
- **What layer 1 reports.** `Plan.Step` reports the design, the targets,
  each question's λ path, its folds, its measurement and certification,
  then the settle and answer phases. A run now moves as
  `design → gather → fit category 1/4 → fold category 1/5 → … → answer`.
- **The timeline reads the live run.** `layer1.Stage.Status` answers from
  the runner's latest `Progress` before it reads the stored report or
  re-fingerprints the store; `RefreshOnProgress` subscribes to
  `layer1.TopicProgress` (one rebuild per second). A live run shows
  `running` even when its inputs are not marked done, because the run is
  the truth.
- **Translated.** Nine new catalog keys (`jobs.stage.*`, `shell.job.step`)
  in English and French. `internal/ui` keeps the en/fr parity test and a
  contract test that every `layer1` stage constant has a label, so a new
  stage cannot ship blank.
- **Live evidence (build `0.1.0-dev+20261102135734`, same behavior as the
  final `…145745`).** A manual run
  reported `fit category 2/4`, `fold category 1/5 … 5/5`, `fit topic
  1/4`, `fold topic 1/5 … 5/5`, with ETAs from 678 s to 1,018 s as the
  rate settled; `/api/learning` returned `layer1 running 1/17 fold topic
  eta 592 s` from the same run, not from the stored report.
- **Model features measured (run 20, build `…131443`).** Lexical, sender
  and metadata cells plus decider stacking: category **0.719** (was
  0.688), reply_needed **0.806** (0.760), urgency **0.662** (0.639),
  deadline **0.779** (0.767), relationship **0.471** (0.445), topic
  **0.490** (0.494). Two questions certify at 0.95: suspicious (LB 0.957)
  and info_sufficiency (LB 0.951). The gate stays closed for the rest;
  no fallback route is used.
- **Gates.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` 82 packages green; `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  59/59 specs green, including a staged job chip and a live layer-1
  timeline.
- **The answer phase is a phase.** After the 17 questions the run used to
  sit at `17 / 17 · 100 %` for minutes. `commit` now walks every message
  three times (decisions, route answers, preview) and reports that work as
  `StageAnswer` with its own denominator and ETA. Run 34 moved
  `1 500 → 7 500 → … → 104 289 / 104 289` and the job finished in **3m55s**.
- **kNN was the lock.** Run 26 with `layer1.knn.enabled` spent **17m51s**
  and held the SQLite writer for ~13 minutes: every answer scanned the
  whole vector set, and the commit answered 34,763 messages. An Ask during
  that window failed at its history write (`database is locked`). The
  setting is off (its default), run 27 took **4m01s**, and the code now
  disables kNN above **2,000 messages** with a warning, because its scan is
  O(population) per answer. `store.busy_timeout` is 30s, above the ~15s
  answer phase.
- **Shared mailboxes are not people.** The exact query
  `donne-moi le courriel pour la création de nouveaux employés de simon
  de services ex` returned three "person" options (Simon Berthier,
  `info@`, `rh@`). The resolver drops a shared mailbox from a "which
  person?" choice whenever a real person is present (`isPersonLike`); the
  query now answers **Simon Berthier, sberthier@services-exemple.test, Services
  Exemple, 721 messages** in 1.3s, computed locally.
- **Open.** The layer-1 commit still deletes and rewrites ~260 MB of
  answers on every run (the answers are stable between runs); shortening
  that write is the next storage improvement.
- **Open.** Strict 0.95 certification is still not met for most questions:

## 2026-10-30 — Inline images repaired at the MIME owner; one global search; the UI split into modules

- **Why images still failed.** After the display backfill, **1,550 of 29,626**
  messages whose HTML contained `cid:` still rendered the
  **“Inline image not available”** placeholder. Two root causes were measured
  in the live store, not guessed: (a) Outlook labels genuine inline pictures
  `application/octet-stream` with a `.bin` name (message 196 carried eight
  such parts), and (b) the shared allow-list did not know the common
  `image/jpg`/`image/pjpeg` and `image/x-png` aliases. Message 196 alone
  explained 8 of the missing parts; the alias rows accounted for 207 more.
- **One owner, three rules.** `mail.InlineImageType` now folds the aliases;
  `InlineImageTypeNeedsBytes` allows a bounded byte read only for a generic
  label, and `InlineImageTypeFromBytes` identifies PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP by their
  magic number. The Outlook connector reads those bytes inside the existing
  `mail.inline_assets.*` budget and stores the sniffed type. No remote fetch,
  no new format and no change to the 4 MiB per-part / 16 MiB per-message
  limits.
- **Repair migration.** `0029_inline_repair_v2.sql` fills the
  `has_inline_refs` flag the first backfill never materialized (18,071 stale
  rows) and resets `inline_assets_checked` only for the **226** messages with
  a part this build can now store. The display backfill `job-1` repaired
  **226/226 in 566 s, 0 skipped**. Live evidence: message 196 has **8/8**
  attachment rows with SHA-256, the API returns `body_inline_images=8` and
  `body_missing_inline=0`, and WebView2 loaded **7/7** `<img>` elements from
  `blob:` URLs (one part is referenced as a background/duplicate) with **0**
  placeholders and **0** horizontal overflow.
- **What remains, honestly.** **1,254** messages still contain a `cid:`

  sender's mail; there are no bytes to store), and about **1,086** inline
  parts remain byte-less because they are deliberately unsupported (SVG,

  placeholder; the budget was not raised, so disk did not grow by the 925 MB
  of oversized photos.
- **One global search.** The shell header now owns the only search box, in

## 2026-10-29 — Live verification: WebView2 DOM, a new Outlook inline message, start-up, Defender and a cold page cache

- **Method.** The five items left open by the display repair were measured on
  the live Windows host, not inferred. WebView2 was inspected through its
  DevTools endpoint (`WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS`), the mailbox
  was read through Outlook COM, and the page cache was measured in Chromium.
  The only mailbox writes in this pass were two clearly labelled synthetic
  probe items, created for the inline-image test and removed again; every
  other Outlook operation was read-only. The probe was necessary because the
  mailbox had received no message with an inline part since the repair (the
  newest stored mail predated it).
- **WebView2 DOM.** A DevTools client (`scripts/relay/probes/webview2-dom.ps1`)
  navigated the real WebView2 window to a repaired message and read the
  sandboxed iframe: two inline images hydrated from `blob:` URLs at
  **300×125** and **3,078×858**, two stylesheets (`mail.css` plus the
  compiled `blob:` sheet), 31 `data-ms` hooks, one layout table **251 px**
  wide, **0** `style` attributes, **0** `<style>` elements, and **0** horizontal
  overflow in both documents. The launch token was absent from the URL and
  the DOM; only `sessionStorage` held it. A 1264×801 PNG capture succeeded;
  it was not downloaded because the message is real mail.
- **New Outlook inline message.** The first attempt used programmatic
  `Send()`; Outlook's Object Model Guard raised a modal
  Refuser/Accepter prompt and the message stayed unsubmitted in the Outbox.
  The prompt was denied and the Outbox item deleted. The successful probe
  saved a labelled draft with a 24×24 PNG (`PR_ATTACH_CONTENT_ID`,
  `PR_ATTACH_MIME_TAG`, `PR_ATTACH_CONTENT_LOCATION`), resolved the owner
  recipient, and moved it into the Inbox. Its first version had an
  unresolved recipient (`address=''`) and scope correctly returned
  `unattributed`; the resolved version returned `owner` /
  `recipient_is_owner` after the 5-minute settle window and a normal sync.
  Live API: `body_format=html`, **1** inline image, **0** missing,
  `body_css` **446** chars, **4** hooks, one layout table, no sender
  `style=` and no `<img>` in the fragment. The asset route returned
  **200 image/png, 157 B**, immutable private cache and sandbox CSP. The
  WebView2 DOM showed the image loaded at **24×24** from `blob:`, 4 hooks,
  table 360 px, no overflow. The probe rows were then removed: Outbox,
  Inbox, Sent, Deleted and Drafts all report **0**, the database has **0**
  probe messages and **0** probe attachments, and the orphan blob was
  pruned.
- **35 s start-up bound.** Two process-cold starts of the deployed build
  were measured through `/api/boot`: with a fresh WebView2 user-data folder
  the descriptor appeared at **1,375 ms**, boot reported **22,648 ms** and
  the wall clock to ready was **23,985 ms**; with the default profile the
  descriptor was **281 ms**, boot **13,639 ms** and wall **13,795 ms**. Both
  reached **12/12** views with **0** failures, below the 35 s bound. The OS
  file cache was warm on both runs; a reboot or a standby-list flush was
  not available to a non-admin session, so a true OS-cache-cold run remains

- **Defender.** Windows 11 Pro build 26100, Defender enabled with real-time
  protection and signatures **1.463.13.0** (1.2 days old).
