## 2026-10-29 — Inline asset vault and MailCanvas renderer; live `0.1.0-dev+20261029191919`

- **Two live defects, one data path.** Microsoft 365 messages arrived with
  `cid:` image references but no stored bytes, and newsletters rendered as a
  flattened document because the sanitizer deleted every sender style, class,
  id and table width. Three read-only agents mapped the chain before any edit;
  each load-bearing claim was then re-read in source. The root causes were
  confirmed end to end: RFC 5322 discarded inline part bytes and `Content-ID`,
  Outlook never enumerated attachments, the store had metadata only, the API
  had no binary route, and `internal/render` deliberately dropped all
  presentation.
- **Inline asset vault.** `mail.Attachment` now carries the MIME identity
  (`ContentID`, `ContentLocation`) and, at ingest only, the decoded bytes.
  RFC 5322 reads `Content-ID`/`Content-Location` and keeps bounded bytes for
  PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP; Outlook reads `Attachments`, `PR_ATTACH_CONTENT_ID`,
  `PR_ATTACH_MIME_TAG`, `PR_ATTACH_SIZE` and `PR_ATTACH_DATA_BIN` without
  writing a file. SVG is refused by one shared `mail.InlineImageType` owner.
  Migration 0026 adds attachment identity and `attachment_blobs`, keyed by
  SHA-256; a repeated signature logo is stored once and a rewrite/removal
  prunes a blob only when its last reference disappears. Migration 0028 adds
  the materialized `has_inline_refs` marker, so the repair query scans integer
  columns instead of every stored HTML body.
- **MailCanvas renderer.** `internal/render` is now a presentation compiler,
  not a CSS stripper. A vetted `<style>` block is rebuilt rule by rule into a
  per-message sheet; a sender `style` attribute becomes a `data-ms` hook
  selected by that sheet. Typography, colour, spacing, borders, widths,
  backgrounds, gradients, tables and `@media` survive. `url()`, `@import`,
  `@font-face`, `@keyframes`, custom properties, `position`, `transform`,
  `expression`, `!important` and unbounded lengths do not. Layout tables are
  marked `data-mail-table="layout"` and no longer inherit data-table padding,
  borders or header fill. Safe table/cell presentation attributes, `class`,
  `id`, `role`, legacy `<font>`/`<big>` and safe raster `data:` images are
  preserved. Remote images stay blocked; a 1×1 remote pixel is suppressed.
- **Authenticated delivery and hydration.** `GET
  /api/messages/{id}/attachments/{position}?v=<sha>` serves one stored image
  under the ordinary bearer API, with an immutable private cache, `nosniff`,
  `Content-Disposition: inline` and a sandbox CSP. The shell fetches it with
  the token, turns it into an ephemeral `blob:` URL and swaps it into the
  iframe; the token never appears in an image URL. The compiled sheet is a
  second `blob:` stylesheet linked after `mail.css`; both frame and parent CSP
  gain `style-src 'self' blob:` but no `unsafe-inline`.
- **Backfill.** The existing owner-triggered job now repairs missing HTML and
  inline bytes, newest first, merges attachment identity instead of deleting
  metadata, and sets `inline_assets_checked` after one successful read so a
  source that cannot satisfy a part is not re-read forever. Batch memory is
  capped at 64 MiB of decoded image bytes in both the detail pass and the
  backfill. RFC 5322 cannot re-read old messages (no `DetailReader`); new RFC
  mail stores its bytes at ingest, and Outlook repairs old mail.
- **Tests.** New RFC 5322 assertions for bytes, `Content-ID`,
  `Content-Location`, the per-part budget and the alteration; Outlook fake
  attachment objects plus inline identity/budget tests; store dedupe,
  identity round-trip, owner boundary, blob pruning and backfill repair tests;
  API binary-route tests (bytes, variant, unavailable, unsupported, invalid
  position, gate); renderer tests for compiled CSS, layout tables, legacy
  fonts, inline resolution, missing/mixed assets, data-image limits, CSS
  injection and bounded attributes; UI source checks; one Playwright iframe
  test asserting sender CSS, table layout, authenticated image hydration,
  missing-image placeholder and no horizontal overflow at 390 px.
- **Gates.** `scripts/test.sh` exhaustive: gofmt, vet (host/Windows/tags),
  taxonomy and every package green (71 tested packages, 81 package lines, 0
  failures). The gate now isolates the port-sensitive sidecar suite exactly
  as the fast gate already did, so its child-process port check no longer
  races unrelated package startup; every package still runs. The boot
  scroll-owner test now waits for its section to mount before appending the
  filler, removing a load-dependent null. `scripts/test-fast.sh` green.
  Playwright **57/57**. The final Windows build is

## 2026-10-29 — Round 55: subject hierarchy and action/waiting truth; live `0.1.0-dev+20261029180917`

- **Scope.** New `internal/subject` (topic → subtopic hierarchy, one answer
  adapter) and `internal/action` (one primary owner action, waiting direction
  and due source). `internal/threadintel` gained directed-signal evidence,
  automated-mail and attachment rules, an owner-last closing state, external
  answer detection and a subject fallback. `internal/priority`,
  `internal/commitments`, `internal/brief`, `internal/triage`,
  `internal/store`, `internal/world`, `internal/qa`, the API views, the UI and
  both catalogs consume the new owners. No schema, migration, setting, boot
  stage or model change; the taxonomy fingerprint stays `9c9956169b0c` and no
  cache is invalidated.
- **Audit method.** Three read-only agents audited the subject pipeline, the
  action/waiting rules and the UI/API wiring against the Round 54 tree. Every
  load-bearing claim was re-read in the source before a change; the false
  positives and false negatives below are the verified subset, each now
  covered by a regression test. The agents also confirmed the parts that were
  already correct (closed catalogue, evidence ordering, abstention handling,
  no page/panel overflow at 390 px, Brief count semantics).
- **Subject hierarchy.** Eleven topics and **49** closed subtopics. The topic
  remains the classifier's single choice; the subtopic is derived from
  `asks_for`, then `decision_needed`, then `category`, then `reply_needed`,
  then the topic default. `subject.FromAnswers` is the one adapter: the
  priority ranking and the triage detail both read the raw route answers with
  the profile's own `Cutoff`, so they cannot disagree about a message and a
  configured threshold moves both. The old detail derivation used blended
  values and a hard-coded 0.5. The audit's misleading mappings were corrected:
  a support call or workaround is troubleshooting (not escalation); a partner
  meeting is `partnership/meeting`; an integration verdict is
  `technical_integration/approval`; meeting preparation no longer claims
  `reschedule`; a press-release review no longer claims a product update; a
  no-ask newsletter is now reachable as `news_updates/newsletter`. The
  hierarchy is exposed on every triage result, priority item, Brief topic,
  thread state, conversation state and company open thread, with nested
  subtopic counts and evidence.
- **Action truth.** `internal/action` owns the precedence: security verify,
  automated bulk read-only, verdict decide, named ask (pay, schedule, send,
  do, decide, reply), generic reply, call to action, informational read. Two
  verified defects are fixed: a thread that needs no reply no longer erases a
  concrete payment/decision ask (`NoAction` used to return `read` before the
  message rules), and a named ask now outranks a generic reply, so “pay and
  confirm” is a payment rather than a reply. The reply filter now claims only
  a live owner reply; the decision filter and the decision commitments read
  the action truth, so a history row or an already-answered thread cannot
  resurface as a decision. Commitments gain `kind=action`, one row per
  conversation (strongest kind wins, evidence and earliest due carried), the
  direction follows the kept kind, and the reply candidate bound rises from
  200 to 2,000 so the Brief counts are honest.
- **Waiting truth at the thread owner.** `is_question` is explicitly
  undirected (“regardless of who must answer them”), so it no longer creates
  an owner reply obligation; `reply_needed` is the directed signal. Automated
  categories never owe a reply however their text is phrased. An owner-last
  closing note/thank-you is `owner_last_closed`, not `awaiting_other`; an
  external answer after the owner's question is `answered_by_other`; a
  message carrying an attachment is substantive whatever its cover note; an
  Outlook OOF template is recognised through `mail.KindOf` (the previous
  string check missed the common `IPM.Note.Rules.OofTemplate` class). A
  shared colleague reply no longer blanks the thread subject. Partial
  visibility stays `unknown` and is excluded from the reply filter rather than
  claiming an obligation.
- **API and UI.** Priority items carry `conversation_id`, the full `signals`
  dimensions (`is_question`, `call_to_action`, `info_sufficiency`, `stance`,
  `relationship`, `subject`) and `action` (`primary`, `waiting`, `due_source`,
  `due_level`, `reasons`). Thread and conversation state carry
  `topic`/`subtopic`; company open threads carry them too. The UI renders a
  localised path (never a raw identifier), an action badge, and a waiting
  badge driven by the action truth rather than the thread enum; Conversation
  rows show the path, Important rows show the path and action, and detail
  opened from Important carries the action badge (All-mail detail does not,
  because the message endpoint has no ranking context). The reason strip may
  wrap to two lines so a phone no longer clips the action.
- **Tests.** New `internal/subject` and `internal/action` suites (catalogue
  closure, every ask → closed path, cutoff/abstention, semantic mappings,
  precedence, terminal states, due sources, owner-action predicate). New
  regressions for: invoice with no reply owed still pays; automated mail with
  a question/CTA never ranks or replies; history decision is not a commitment;
  decision source requires the action truth; merge keeps the kept direction;
  owner attachment with a trivial note closes; automated mail never owes a
  reply; Outlook OOF template is an auto-reply; profile cutoff moves the
  subject; thread subject fallback; UI path/action/badge rendering and no raw
  identifiers; the read-model bounds fit the ranking cache. Existing fixtures
  were updated to carry the action truth.
- **Live defect found and fixed.** The first deployed build
  (`0.1.0-dev+20261029180206`) booted 10/12: `commitments` and `brief`
  failed at warm because the decision source called the API ranking with
  limit 200 while the page bound is 50. The fakes had accepted the larger
  number, so the unit suite could not catch it. The fix adds
  `priority.Decisions` (bounded by the 200-item cache, not the screen page)
  and changes the commitments interface to it; the regression
  `TestReadModelBoundsFitTheRankingCache` asserts the read-model bounds
  against `priority.MaxCached`. The rebuilt `0.1.0-dev+20261029180437`
  booted 12/12. Two further rule refinements (`180709`, `180917`) narrowed
  the undirected-question path after live samples; the final build

## 2026-10-29 — Round 52: human company labels + bounded people evidence; live `0.1.0-dev+20261029160930`

- **Scope.** `internal/store/companyname.go` (local vocabulary segmentation

  extract.go` (signature name/phone/title/company, `BestName`, `PhoneKey`),
  `internal/mail/clean.go` (`EvidenceText`, minimal-quote pre-cut, trailing
  lines), `internal/api/routes_companies.go` + `router.go` (batch profiles),
  `internal/ui/app.js` + `app.css` (visible-row prefetch, warm buffer,
  in-place detail), tests and docs. No schema or migration change;
  `rules_version` stays 3 so the existing 34,938-vector space is reused.
- **Baseline (live `0.1.0-dev+20261029151610`, 34,646 messages).** Top 100
  companies: 98/100 labels equal to their first domain, 0 empty. Six top
  profiles: 198 people, 94 named (47%), 0 phone, 0 role. Diagnostic over the
  six newest received messages of six companies (36 messages): 6/36 detected
  signatures and 6/36 phone evidence. A manual trailing-block probe measured
  36/36 signatures, 22/36 phone, 34/36 name, 3/36 title and 8/36 company.

  vocabulary and observed person names (`climatisation-exemple.test` →
  `Climatisation Exemple`, `messagerie-exemple.test` → `Messagerie Exemple`,
  `fondation-aurore.test` → `Fondation Aurore`). `contacts.BestName`

  `CleanBody`'s global rules and data version stay unchanged.

## 2026-10-29 — Round 48: All-Mail unread boolean filter

- **Scope.** `internal/store/messagepage.go` (query/cursor predicates,
  counts cache), `internal/messages/service.go` (first-page cache bypass),
  `internal/api/routes_messages.go` + `internal/api/request.go` (one strict
  boolean grammar), `internal/ui/app.js`, `internal/ui/i18n.en.js`/`i18n.fr.js`,
  the store/API/messages/UI tests, `e2e/specs/mail.spec.ts`,
  `e2e/fixtures/data.ts`, docs. No schema, setting, migration, boot, warm or
  `is_read` index change.
- **Contract.** `unread=true`/`1` adds `m.is_read = 0` to the page and the
  per-role counts; `false`/`0` and an absent value are one filter-off state,
  never a read-only page. It composes with role, store and sender. The keyset
  cursor carries the read state and is rejected (`400 invalid_cursor`) under
  the other state. A present-but-empty, blank or unknown value is `400
  invalid_unread` with `params.name = "unread"`. The startup warm stays the
  one unfiltered first page; the service cache accepts `Unread=false` as the
  same default and rejects `true`.
- **Red (before production behavior).** Store/API/messages compile-red on the
  missing `Unread` field (`red-store.txt`, `red-api.txt`), the UI static
  contract was red on the 11 missing unread markers (`red-ui.txt`), and the
  updated Mail Playwright test was behaviorally red on the exact Round 47
  tree at the missing Unread chip (`red-mail.txt`: `element(s) not found`).
  After only `MessageListQuery.Unread` was added, `TestNonFirstPageBypassesTheCache`
  was behaviorally red: `store called 1 times for two unread reads, want 2`
  (`red-service.txt`) because `firstPage` still cached the unread page.
- **Change.** `MessageListQuery.Unread` and `Cursor.Unread` (JSON
  `omitempty`); `IsZero` includes `!Unread`; `normalize` rejects a cursor
  issued for the other read state; page and counts predicates add
  `m.is_read = 0` only when true; `NextBefore` carries the flag; the counts
  cache key is `(generation, store, sender, unread)` with the same bound 8
  and generation invalidation. `messages.firstPage` returns false for
  `Unread=true`. The API reuses one `queryBoolValue` for the existing
  `counts` grammar and `unread`, keeping `invalid_counts` unchanged and
  adding `invalid_unread`. The UI adds one `unread` boolean to the model,
  snapshot and restore, parses `route.params.get("unread")` with
  `allMailUnread`, emits only `unread=true`, and splits the filter strip
  into two labeled sibling groups: the eight folder chips keep
  `mail.role_aria` ("Folder filter"), and the Unread toggle sits alone in a
  `mail.filter.state_aria` ("Read state") group with `aria-pressed` and the
  active class. A `.filter-chip-group` flex wrapper keeps the wide row
  unchanged and lets the strip scroll as one nowrap row at narrow width.
  It composes every path (row link, selection, Load more, observer, role
  chips, sender apply/clear), adds the sender → unread → folder empty
  precedence with a clear-only-unread action (`mail.filter.unread_clear`,
  not the chip label), and changes the row dot to
  `row.is_read === false` in every folder. i18n adds
  `mail.filter.state_aria`, `mail.filter.unread`, `mail.filter.unread_clear`,
  `mail.all.empty_unread_title` and `mail.all.empty_unread_body`; the CSS
  adds only `.filter-chip-group`.

## 2026-10-29 — Round 47: All-Mail prefetch/refresh race hardening

- **Scope.** `internal/ui/app.js` (`prefetchRoute`, the All-Mail model,
  `loadMoreAllMail` and `renderAllMail`), `internal/ui/ui_test.go` (source
  contract markers), `e2e/specs/mail.spec.ts` (the progressive probe, fake SSE
  and a deterministic Load more dispatch); docs. No Go production path, API,
  schema, setting, migration, boot or warm change, and no new filter.
- **Gap and red.** A bare `#/mail` idle prefetch could build the default
  All-Mail destination while a filtered All-Mail list was mounted. Its
  `renderAllMail` replaced `state.allMail` and disconnected the single
  `allMailObserver`, so the mounted list's Load more failed its role/sender
  guard and silently no-opped. Separately, a same-filter
  `refreshActiveRouteNow`/`refreshCachedRoute` during an in-flight Load more
  rebuilt the Mail All screen from the stale model while `model.loading` was
  true. The new list painted "Loading more…", the old request's list was
  detached and returned before appending, and its finally repainted only the
  old sentinel; the new list stayed at the old rows with the loading text.
  Red on the unchanged Round 46 tree: the fake-SSE probe invalidated the mail
  route cache with `config.changed` (`keys: ["mail.sync"]`) and hovered and
  focused `[data-nav="mail"]` on a 100-row `other@example.test` list; one
  bare `/api/messages` request fired (`Expected: 0, Received: 1`,
  `round47-red-prefetch.log`). The red run aborts at that assertion, before
  the Load more click; the resulting no-op is the mechanism, not asserted in
  that red run. With Fix A only, the gated-cursor probe held the 100→150 page,
  emitted `dropped`
  (`reason: "buffer_full"`, one 400 ms live resync), confirmed the refresh
  reached the render, released the cursor and stayed at 100 rows instead of
  150 (`Expected: 150, Received: 100`, `round47-red-refresh.log`). The Go
  static contract was red on the missing markers (`round47-go-red.txt`).
- **Change.** `prefetchRoute` returns false after the cache hit and before
  the inflight marker when the target is default Mail All and the current
  route is Any All-Mail; `scheduleRoutePrefetch` already deletes the
  once-only link on false, so a later hover after leaving All retries. The
  guard is inactive on Hub→Mail, so the existing first-click prefetch is
  unchanged. The filtered-All→unfiltered-Mail nav click is cold only when the
  bare `#/mail` route-cache entry is absent, evicted or invalidated (the test
  forces that with `config.changed`); a surviving entry is a warm cache hit.
  Every All-Mail model owner (the initial literal,
  `restoreCachedAllMail` and the filter-change object) gained a transient
  `morePromise`, which `allMailSnapshot` never stores. `loadMoreAllMail`
  creates one settle/pending promise after `model.loading = true`, wraps the

  even on error or paint failure. `renderAllMail`, after the first-page block
  and before its render-sequence check, awaits the in-flight page while the
  current model still owns it, with a defensive break so a broken owner
  cannot spin. There is no retry timer, no new generation token and no second

## 2026-10-29 — Round 46: All-Mail sender filter (exact address / @domain)

- **Scope.** `internal/mail/address.go` (`NormalizeSenderQuery`,
  `MaxSenderQueryRunes`, `ErrInvalidSenderQuery`), `internal/store/lowersql.go`
  (the `mailsense_lower` scalar), `internal/store/search.go` (one
  `senderWhere`, shared), `internal/store/messagepage.go` (`Sender` in the
  query and cursor, page/total/counts predicates, counts-cache key),
  `internal/messages/service.go` (sender pages bypass the first-page cache),
  `internal/api/request.go` (`querySender`), `routes_messages.go`,
  `routes_search.go` (the duplicated validator removed), `internal/ui/app.js`
  (sender field, chip, URL/model/guards, links and empty copy), `app.css`, both
  i18n catalogs, the store/API/service/mail tests, the two extended All-mail
  Playwright tests and `e2e/fixtures/data.ts`; docs. No schema, setting,
  migration, boot or warm change.
- **Gap and red.** The page had no sender filter and the only sender rule was
  inline in search. Store/API/mail/service were compile-red on the unchanged
  tree; with only the new store field in place the service failed
  behaviorally (`store called 1 times for two sender reads, want 2`). The
  before binary ignores `sender` (all arms returned the unfiltered 33,416-row
  page in the measurement).
- **Change.** One validation and one predicate. An exact address is the whole
  normalized address; `@domain` (or `domain`) is a single-domain suffix, never
  a subdomain or a display name. The SQL compares `mailsense_lower`, because
  SQLite's `lower()` is ASCII-only. Page, total and role counts carry the
  filter; the counts cache is keyed by generation, store and sender; the
  cursor carries the normalized sender and rejects another role/store/sender;
  an empty sender adds no predicate. The API returns `400 invalid_sender` for
  blank, a lone `@`, any control character (checked after trimming) or more than 320 runes, and
  search uses the same path (lone `@` is the one deliberate search change). The
  UI keeps the applied sender in the URL and model, adds a field with Enter/
  Apply, an active chip with clear, sender-preserving row links and selection,
  and a sender-specific empty copy; typing is protected by the existing focus
  guard and no SSE event refreshes Mail. A cached All-Mail pane now owns the
  model it was rendered with (`__allMailModel`): Back restores that snapshot
  only when it is loaded and the route's role/sender match, repaints Load more
  and re-arms the observer, while a mismatch discards the entry for a fresh
  render; a stale in-flight page also has to be the current model before it
  can append. The row builder returns the rows it accepted after its one
  dedupe rule, and `loadMoreAllMail` appends exactly those to `model.rows`, so
  the model, the DOM and the snapshot stay one population; a >20 s refresh
  repaints all 150 loaded rows, not the first 100. An inner read error marks
  the mail screen non-cacheable, so Back and Try again issue fresh requests.
  A role/sender change now replaces `state.allMail` with a fresh object,
  including `loading: false`; an old first-page or Load more promise keeps the
  old object, so its identity, role/sender and render-sequence guards drop it
  and it cannot clear or repaint the new filter's sentinel.
- **Measurements.** Five interleaved order-balanced pairs (B,A,A,B,B,A,A,B,B,A)
  at 1-min load 14.47/15.29/16.84/21.16/23.31 before and
  13.91/15.63/16.29/20.72/21.36 after: default page paired median p50 −0.41 ms,
  p95 −0.27 ms (worst pair +0.20/+1.78), gate PASS. Sender after-only: A
  13,779 rows 3.45/4.98 ms (first 54.9, second 4.04), B 297 rows 25.68/32.19
  (first 67.12, second 21.52), rare 2 rows 57.99/72.83 (first 109.98, max
  170.29, second 57.54), domain 16,019 rows 3.46/5.67 (first 67.7, second
  3.67). Counts sum equals total; A/B/domain return 100 rows and a cursor,
  rare 2 rows and none. The declared read-only SQL baseline is a different
  warm-cache measurement; no filter win is claimed and the expression-index
  migration remains the follow-up. Provenance: `measure-one.py` retains only
  each run's `stats.json` aggregates (the raw per-request timings were
  discarded), and these p50/p95 values were recomputed from those per-run
  stats; the SQL baseline is the design's measurement and was not re-run here.
- **Correctness and gates.** 58/58 live checks (exact, domain, counts, cursor
  binding, zero-result page 200/0/0, present-but-empty/blank and malformed
  400s, search preservation, store boundary); domain-not-subdomain and plus-tag
  are unit-tested only, and the empty-parameter 400 has both live and unit
  coverage. The progressive All-Mail Playwright test now also covers the
  cached Back path: filter `digest@example.test` → Sent → Back → 100 rows →
  scroll → 150 rows (`2000–2149`, no duplicates), no empty `sender=` request.
  It also loads 150, opens Sent, waits a real 20.5 s with the SSE stream held
  pending (so learning invalidation cannot clear the route cache), goes Back,
  observes the cached restore plus the background refresh, and requires 150
  rows, no duplicates and the end state. The error test leaves, goes Back and
  retries with a fresh request each time. The same test delays the default
  cursor response 1.5 s, clicks Load more then Inbox, and requires 100 Inbox
  rows with a live Load more control before and after the old response
  resolves; the old cursor page must not append. Focused tests green, `-race`
  store/messages/api green, `scripts/test-fast.sh` **79 packages**, full
  `scripts/test.sh` green, Playwright **42/42** and `scripts/test-ui.sh`
  **42/42** on its final rerun (two earlier runs hit the known boot
  `#token-title` flake; `boot.spec.ts` 8/8 alone), no sidecar flake; the
  focused back/error tests passed 2/2 and the progressive test 3/3 repeated;
  Round 45/44/43/40/37 guards green, no test weakened. Before `361485e2…`
  30,395,847 B, after `fe8e4259…` 30,411,679 B; the Round 45 rebuild was
  verified `695bb459…` first; the final fixes built `05c47d65…` 30,416,199 B
  (byte-identical rebuild; the measured API binary is not final). One-sample
  final default-page sanity pair: 0.54/0.99 vs 1.14/1.49 ms p50/p95, 33,416
  rows and 100-row pages in both (not a new series, no win claimed); source
  store DB/WAL/SHM hashes unchanged.
- **Residual.** Windows/WebView2/COM/Defender, a cold page cache and a real
  mailbox unmeasured; the sender page has no expression index; the prepared
  store has no shared/delegate store, so that boundary is unit-tested only;
  the older ≤100 ms messages→list, 150 ms click and absolute ready bounds stay
  open.
- **Residuals (pre-existing, not introduced by Round 46; queued for Round
  47).** The background `#/mail` prefetch (`prefetchRoute`/
  `scheduleRoutePrefetch`, around `internal/ui/app.js:2046-2071` and `:2698`)
  can call `renderAllMail` while a filtered All-Mail list is active, replacing
  `state.allMail` and disconnecting the active observer; that list's Load more
  then sees a role/sender mismatch and silently no-ops. A same-filter
  `refreshActiveRouteNow` (around `:1827-1857`) during an in-flight Load more
  can paint the refreshed sentinel as "Loading more…"; the old request's
  finally clears the shared model's loading flag but repaints only its
  detached old `more`, so the new sentinel can stay stale until scroll. Both
  predate Round 46 and were found by the final adversarial check, not
  introduced by the sender filter; Round 47 fixes them in the same owner
  before adding another filter, and they are not fixed here.

## 2026-10-29 — Round 43: QA count-synonym cleanup (routing win; D1/D2 person frames closed; French quantité supported)

- **Gap.** Round 39's provider-less count gate recognized only
  how many/how much/number of/nombre de/count/counts/total/combien. A person-,
  company-, date- or pronoun-scoped count phrased with "amount of",
  "quantity of" or bare "number" could still bypass `aggregateCountRequest`,
  parse directly to a category in `parseIntent` and answer the mailbox-wide
  priority total. In the live store both "Amount of deadlines does Bob have?"
  and plain "Amount of deadlines" returned `structured/deadline` with
  `counts.deadline=16704` and five citations.
- **Red first.** `/tmp/mailsense-round43-baseline.txt` is behavioral, not
  compile-red. The five scoped synonym cases returned `structured/deadline`
  or `structured/urgent` with counts and priority reads: "Amount of deadlines
  does Bob have?", "Quantity of deadlines from Atelier Nord?", "Number deadlines
  does An have?", "Amount of deadlines this week?" and "Quantity of urgent
  messages does she have?". "Amount of priority messages" returned
  `structured/priority` with total 7. The plain amount/quantity/bare-number
  and French `Quantité d'échéances` cases were already structured through the
  legacy category path, and the French week control was already freeform.
  The eight original cases, seven unlisted scopes, person frames, priority
  removal, strict `peopleErr`/`listErr` and zero/error/nil-source/broken-
  generator tests stayed green.
- **Change.** One canonical cue owner: `aggregateCountWords` adds
  `amount`/`quantity`/`quantite`, `aggregateCountPhrases` adds
  `amount of`/`quantity of`/`quantite de`, and `aggregateCountRequest` adds
  `aggregateBareNumberRequest` for bare `number` immediately before a
  category or mailbox noun. The new cue tokens are removed by the existing
  `aggregateCountCueTokens` before the residual allowlist, so the Round 39
  fail-closed pre-switch gate applies to them unchanged; no second list or
  setting was added. `aggregateStructuredIntent` still rejects person,
  company, date, content, action, two-category and priority wording.
- **Live finding.** The first after-series binary (before the final entity
  fix) answered plain "Amount of deadlines" as freeform. The strict person
  resolver matched the count cue "amount" by substring against the sender
  "Paramount Software UK Limited" and deferred the question. The final fix
  factors `resolveEntityMentionsChecked` and filters the cue terms before the
  bounded candidate query (`aggregateCountEntityMentions`). A category noun
  in the person-subject position is added back as a term, so a contact
  actually named Deadline, Urgent or Reply still scopes the freeform
  follow-up; a cue term or an object-position category noun is not a person
  term. The
  freeform resolver for a recognized count uses the same filtered mentions
  (D2), so "Amount of deadlines does Bob have?" considers Bob and not
  Paramount. The aborted probe is kept in
  `/tmp/mailsense-round43/after-aborted*` and is not the headline measurement.
- **D1/D2 correctness follow-up.** `aggregateCountPersonSubjects` is the one
  subject owner for `does/did` and `has/have`. A `does/did` subject is now a
  person frame unless it is first/second person or a mailbox noun, so a
  category noun after `does/did` ("does Deadline have", "does Urgent have")
  no longer passes as the category. A cue token or category noun before
  `has/have` is a person frame unless the next token is I/we/you or the
  subject is a mailbox noun ("Amount of deadlines Amount has?" is freeform;

  `EachPriorityItem carried 9 body bytes`. The `PriorityHeads` store tests

  compile-red (`store.PriorityBody` undefined) until the store type landed;
  the behavioral priority red then measured `fullScans=1`, `headCalls=0`,

  no route/preview answers. `store.PriorityBody` and `PriorityHeads(ids)` read
  one 2,000-character head, truncation flag and revision for the cached ids

- **Change.** `aggregateStructuredIntent` (`internal/qa/intent.go`) accepts a
  plain, single-category count only when the residual wording, after the
  count cue and the one category word are removed, is on a small explicit

  or date word stays free-form (fail-closed), as do person, latest, content,
  action and multiple-category wording. The allowlist has no third-person
  pronouns or `an`, and a `does`/`did <subject>` person frame rejects a
  subject that is not I/we/you or a category/mailbox noun, so "does she/he/
  they/An/Bob have" stays free-form while "do I/we/you have" remains a plain
  count. The fixed list is security, decision, deadline, urgent, reply and

  also returns free-form for a count whose wording would otherwise parse
  directly as priority (for example "Combien de messages importants ?"), so

## 2026-10-28 — Listener and window before the warm; boot contract

- **Gap.** `main` built the API only after `warmDerived` and the semantic
  prepare, so the desktop window, the runtime descriptor and every route
  waited for the whole warm (ready **2.833 s** in Round 33). The priority
  cold path had no single-flight: two concurrent first readers both ran
  `buildRanking`, and the second result was discarded. The shell awaited
  `/api/status`, `/api/learning`, the language setting and `/api/jobs`
  before it mounted any route, so `#main` was empty during that window.
  The independent review then found a shutdown defect: first-open
  discovery was not joined and could still be in `Discover`/`SaveMailboxes`
  when `Store.Close` ran; the ready-with-failed boot state was silent in
  the shell; and the priority `Close` comment claimed an absolute join
  although its wait is bounded.
- **Fix.** `srv.Start` now binds loopback and writes `runtime/api.json`
  before the warm; the window opens immediately; the warm (learning beside
  priority, seven dependent views, brief, semantic prepare) runs in one
  cancellable background task and logs `mailsense ready` at the end.
  `startFirstOpenDiscovery` returns a stop that cancels and waits, and
  `main` defers it after `st.Close`, so LIFO joins discovery before the
  store closes; the semantic maintenance worker is joined too. A
  `bootState` owns the eleven ordered stages and backs `GET /api/boot`
  (`warming`/`ready`, per-view `pending`/`running`/`done`/`failed`,
  `done`/`total`/`failed`/`current`); it is authenticated and not
  learning-gated. The priority service gained one cold single-flight beside
  its stale-while-refresh path: concurrent readers join one build detached
  from their request contexts; a failure is shared but not cached;
  idempotent `Close` cancels and waits up to **10 s** (production reads
  honor the context; a non-cooperative build is logged, not hidden). The
  shell mounts the route skeleton and opens the event stream before its
  first awaits, polls the boot strip every 400 ms, hides it at ready only
  when `failed == 0`, keeps a warning strip naming failed views at ready
  with `failed > 0` (Dismiss uses the existing job-strip key), and starts
  the one core prefetch then (or on a 404 from an older server). No fake
  list, count or "no mail" is shown while a read is pending.
- **Result (final4 measured artifact `6ab03e91…`; fresh Round 33 store copies; five
  interleaved pairs; saved host load 39.80/39.18/31.11 before startup,

## 2026-10-28 — One learning status build reads each stage once

- **Gap.** The learning status fan-out asked the embeddings stage three
  times per build: directly, as the layer-1 stage's `after` dependency, and
  through the route's own layer-1 stage. With evidence complete, one build
  planned the 33,842-row index coverage **3 times** (`index.plan` measured
  **116–145 ms** per call). The red test
  `TestComputeStatusAsksEachStageOnce` observed **3** calls of a counting
  fake index stage per build (want 1), and the before-fix live probe
  counted 3 plans before the first `learning status` log line.
- **Fix.** `learning.StatusOf(ctx, stage)` reads through one memo installed
  by `computeStatus` with `withStatusMemo`; the layer-1, route and labels
  stages now read their `after` stages through it. The memo is keyed by
  stage type + id (the machine already enforces unique top-level ids, and a
  nested stage repeats the id of the stage it mirrors), uses one
  `sync.Once` per entry, preserves status and error, and is dropped when
  the build returns. A plain context still calls the stage directly, so
  direct layer-1 callers are unchanged. No cross-build cache, setting,
  schema, API, UI or event change.
- **Result.** Plans inside one learning build **3 → 1** (instrumented
  probe, same source plus a measurement-only `println` in `plan`). On a
  disposable copy with evidence complete, learning **666 → 313 ms**
  (median of 3+3, −53%). On the Round 32 resource store (evidence pending,
  so the layer-1 path never reached the index) learning **361 → 308 ms**.
  Ready **2935 → 2833 ms** (median of 9+9; target ≤2.75 s missed by
  0.083 s), priority **1630 → 1653 ms** (noise; target ≤1.60 s missed),
  CPU **4.60 → 4.62 s** (target ≤4.50 s missed), peak RSS **564 → 550 MB**
  (no regression; both above the audit's 539 MB), FDs **16**, goroutines
  **69**, threads **8** unchanged. The 600-read pass was unchanged within
  noise (p50 status 0.965, hub 1.028, priority 1.529, messages 25.823,
  search 8.969, companies 1.062 ms; network 15,307,255 B), as were 60 s
  idle CPU (**+0.00 s**), DB (**381,194,240 B**) and WAL (**4,429,032 B**).
  Learning ≤200 ms was missed: **313 ms** is the median of three runs; one
  instrumented run split **56 ms** sync + **119 ms** evidence +
  **146 ms** embeddings, which does not sum to the median.
- **Regression coverage.** `TestStatusOfMemoizesWithinOneBuild`,
  `TestStatusOfPreservesAFailedStageWithinTheBuild`,
  `TestStatusOfKeepsStagesApart`, `TestStatusOfHandlesANonComparableStage`
  and `TestComputeStatusAsksEachStageOnce` (real layer-1/route/labels
  constructors wrapping a counting index stage); the gate, latch,
  final-invalidation, embeddings-stage and warm/startup tests stay green.
- **Residual.** A coverage-only `index.Stage.Status` path (no materialized
  work slice) would have to beat the 116–145 ms plan to move learning under

  it is recorded, not implemented. Windows/Defender, WebView2, a live

  multi-hour goroutine/FD/disk soak were not measured (goroutines 69 and
  FDs 16 are two ready-time samples, not a leak test over time).

## 2026-10-28 — Split FTS text and coverage versions

- **Gap.** Round 30 bumped one `ftsVersion` to `4-indic-substring`, so
  every open of a pre-v4 store rewrote both indexes. The word index content
  did not change; only `substring_extra` coverage changed. A 33,842-message
  store paid **17.90–18.35 s** and **+35.4 MB** DB (96.96% of it free pages)
  plus **33.6 MB** WAL to add **one** trigram row.
- **Fix.** `fts_text_version` (`3-nfkc-casefold`) names the folded form both
  indexes hold and rewrites both when stale; `fts_coverage_version`
  (`4-indic-substring`) names which messages have a trigram row and runs a
  trigram-only pass when stale. `fts_version` stays as the downgrade mirror
  and the fallback for a store without the split keys: legacy
  `4-indic-substring` adopts text 3 / coverage 4 with no index work, legacy
  `3-nfkc-casefold` selects the trigram-only pass, and a missing, older or
  unknown value rebuilds both. `reindexTri` reads the existing trigram
  rowids once, scans message ids in `sync.batch_size` batches with the same
  fields as the full pass, inserts only the missing rows (through the shared
  `foldedFTSFields`/`insertTri` helper), marks the needed ids seen and
  deletes the remaining stale rows at the end; it never prepares a
  word-index statement. The word rebuild keeps the pre-split
  `full-text indexes rebuilt` log line and `messages` attribute for
  operator docs and parsers. The coverage version is written only after the last
  insert and delete; a canceled or interrupted pass leaves it old and the
  next open retries without duplicating rows. No migration, setting, table,
  index or column was added; `writeFTS` remains the incremental write
  path and the coverage pass shares its fold/insert helper.
- **Result.** On three fresh disposable copies of the legacy-3 prepared
  store, the tri-only cold open measured **0.753–1.536 s** (the first read
  of the 384 MB file was the slow sample; exact `reindexTri` pass
  **0.686–0.728 s**: scan **0.656–0.696 s**, one insert **0.1 ms**), versus
  **17.880–18.043 s** for the full control. The word index stayed
  byte-identical (`47,386,624 B`, rowid checksum `71119cb292231a62`),
  trigram rows went **93 → 94**, trigram bytes **1,605,632 → 1,613,824**,
  page count **93,795 → 93,797**, DB file **unchanged at completion** and
  **+8,192 B** after checkpoint, WAL **53,592 B**. The full control
  reproduced Round 30: **17.880–18.043 s**, DB **+35,401,728 B** (page
  count 102,438, freelist 8,380 = 34,324,480 B), WAL **33,648,072 B**,
  word **+1,048,576 B**, trigram **+28,672 B**.
  App ready on fresh legacy-3 copies was **3.439 s**, **3.639 s** and
  **3.946 s** (full control **20.324 s**), warm **2.832–3.239 s**. A Round 30 store adopted
  the split keys in **255.9–397.5 ms** with no row or byte change; a complete
  coverage scanned 33,842 messages in **0.693–0.707 s** with 0 inserts and 0 DB
  growth; the 10,040-message Hindi store scanned in **0.160–0.168 s** with 0
  inserts. A text-version bump on an already-reindexed store still costs a
  full rewrite: **19.966 s**, **+794,624 B** DB and **42,238,272 B** WAL
  (it reuses the existing free pages).
- **Evidence.** `/tmp/mailsense-round31-baseline.txt` (14 red test
  functions: legacy 3 still full-reindexed, no split keys seeded),
  `/tmp/mailsense-round31-after.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round31-measure-before.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round31-measure-after.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round31-fast.log`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round31-playwright.log`. Windows, Defender, a live
  mailbox and WebView2 were not measured.

## 2026-10-28 — Indic substring routing

- **Gap.** The ten matra-based Indic scripts of the locale data
  (Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Oriya, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada,
  Malayalam, Sinhala) use spaces, so they were not in the substring
  coverage. `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2` treats their dependent vowel
  signs as separators: कि, की, कु and कू all word-index to क, कमल and कमला
  to कमल. On a synthetic 10-script × 4-term fixture every query returned
  **4/4** documents in word mode; the prepared 33,842-message store has
  only one Devanagari message (हैलो) and none of the probe terms.
- **Fix.** `substring_extra` in `internal/mail/scripts.json` now holds the
  10 scripts (Hangul stays); `Spaceless` is still false for them, so word
  counts and triage facts are unchanged. The data was edited as the
  documented hand-kept key and `scripts/update-unicode-data.sh` regenerated
  the shipped file and recorded its new SHA-256 in `unicode-pin.json`;
  `TestShippedDataMatchesItsPins` and `TestUnicodePinMatchesGo` pass.
  `ftsVersion` is `4-indic-substring`: an existing store rewrites both
  indexes once at open and the trigram index gets a row for every message
  of those scripts. No new table, index, column, setting or tokenchars
  change; `writeFTS` remains the only writer.

  the correct id in scan mode (2-rune terms); कमला is substring and कमल
  matches both कमल and कमला (the documented substring residual). Prepared
  store: the eight probe terms are 0 hits before and after (negative
  control), while हैलो is found by substring and है by scan. The one-time
  reindex measured **17.97 s** and **18.35 s** (two cold opens; audit
  **17.95 s**; exact `reindexFTS` on an already-open store **19.95 s**).
  DB **384,184,320 → 419,586,048 B** (**+35,401,728 B, +9.21%**), WAL
  **33,648,072 B** at completion and absent after close, freelist
  **8,380 pages = 34,324,480 B** (**96.96%** of the growth; the app never

  index **1,605,632 → 1,634,304 B** (+28,672), combined group
  **48,992,256 → 50,069,504 B** (+1,077,248 = 1,048,576 + 28,672),
  trigram rows **93 → 94**. Warm open

  messages and **49.128 ms** at 10,040 (p95 5.201 / 52.778 ms); the
  prepared mailbox has only 94 trigram rows, so its scan is structurally

- **Downstream data digest.** `mail.DataDigest` includes `scripts.json`, so

  The prepared copy has **0 embeddings** (no runtime here), so that recheck

## 2026-10-28 — Search snippet anchoring

- **Gap.** A full-text hit's snippet was cut at the first *substring*
  occurrence of a query word, and `terms` dropped every one-rune term, so
  `a` and `x` returned the unrelated body beginning; `com` could anchor
  inside `communication`; a hit that matched only the subject, sender or
  recipients still showed a body beginning. On a disposable copy of the
  prepared 33,842-message store with the real pre-fix binary (top 20, 8
  samples, `/tmp/mailsense-round29-measure-before.txt`), `a` and `x`
  were **0/20 matched excerpts** (the old `terms` dropped one-rune words,
  so every snippet was the cleaned preview; 1 and 2 previews happened to
  coincide with a body-start cut), `com` was **11/20** (3 inside a longer
  word); nine field-only hits showed a body beginning and **0** were
  empty. The audit's Python model (a/x 0/20, com 11 whole/9 inside) is a
  different measurement; the real build's 3 inside-only com snippets are
  the number recorded here.
- **Fix.** `hydrate` receives the store's `text.Terms` instead of
  re-deriving words from `q.Text`, and prepares one mode-aware
  `snippetPlan` per page. Word mode matches whole FTS-like tokens
  (letters, numbers, private-use; marks, underscores and punctuation
  separate) and requires adjacent tokens for `mailer-daemon`, `com_value`
  or a quoted phrase; one-rune word terms stay. Substring/scan mode keeps
  substring matching and drops a one-rune scan term when a longer term
  exists. A full-text hit whose body has no match returns an empty
  snippet; a semantic-only hit keeps the cleaned preview. The excerpt is
  plain text under `search.snippet_chars` (n + two ellipses), with no
  highlight markup, subject/sender synthesis, new setting, schema,
  migration or store query.
- **Result.** After the fix, on the same store and commands: `a` **20/20**,
  `x` **20/20**, `com` **19/20 anchored + 1 field-only empty**, and **0**
  snippets with the term only inside a longer word; the nine field-only
  hits are empty (`noreply` 5, `phising` 1, `mailer-daemon` 2, `com` 1 via
  a recipient domain), while `postmaster` stays 20/20. Non-empty excerpts
  span **100–259 B** (full 240-rune windows **243–259 B**; near-end
  **100–177 B**); whole-page snippet bytes for a/x/com are
  **5,051 / 4,693 / 4,756**. Top-20 JSON is **14,767 / 14,496 / 14,503 B**

## 2026-10-28 — FTS quoted phrases and empty-query safety

- **Gap.** The UI promises "words or a phrase", but `planQuery` stripped
  every ASCII `"` and ANDed the words, so `"bonjour merci"` over-returned;
  a fullwidth quote or NUL reached FTS5 as a syntax error, a zero-width
  space was already removed by `mail.Fold` and surfaced as the untyped
  `store: empty search`, and all five forms became a 500 at the API.
  On a disposable copy of the prepared 33,842-message store (count cap
  raised to 1,000,000 for exact counts; default 10,000 caps), before the
  fix `"bonjour merci"` returned **14,900** and `"merci bonjour"`
  **14,900**, while the true phrases were **180** and **6**
  (`"bonjour-merci"` / `"merci-bonjour"` controls, the hyphen splitting
  into an adjacent phrase); `"compte rendu"` returned **343** against the
  true **168** (`"compte-rendu"`); unquoted controls stayed 14,900 / 343.
  `＂`, NUL and `a＂b` failed with `SQL logic error: unterminated string`,
  `"` and ZWSP with the untyped `store: empty search`, and the API turned
  all five forms into 500s.
- **Fix.** One parser at the FTS owner: `parseQuery` folds the whole query
  once with `mail.Fold` (fullwidth `＂` becomes `"`, default ignorables
  gone), maps control characters (NUL included) to spaces, parses ASCII
  quote spans as one FTS phrase and bare words as ANDed terms, runs an
  unclosed quote to the end, and returns the new typed
  `store.ErrEmptySearch` when nothing is left. `planQuery` still routes the
  whole query to the trigram index when any term needs substring search and
  still scans short terms; bare words and phrases become quoted FTS terms,
  while short scan terms are bound `instr` conditions, so operators and
  syntax stay text. `internal/search` maps
  `ErrEmptySearch` to `ErrEmptyQuery` (400 `empty_query`) without exposing
  the store text. No schema, index, `fts_version` or reindex change: the
  fix works on existing stores.
- **Result.** After the fix the same store returns the true phrases:
  `"bonjour merci"` **180**, `"merci bonjour"` **6**,
  `"compte rendu"` **168**; unquoted controls unchanged at **14,900** and
  **343**. Medians: phrase **7.44 ms** vs AND
  **39.75 ms** for bonjour/merci (~5.3×), and **1.26 ms** vs **1.92 ms**
  for compte rendu. `＂`, NUL, `"` and ZWSP are now typed empty searches;
  `a＂b` is a valid two-word query (1,974 hits on that corpus); the API
  answers 400 `empty_query` for the four empty forms and 200 for `a＂b`
  and `"bonjour merci"` — **zero 500s**. The audit's 2.4 ms / 21.0 ms are
  a different machine's numbers; the counts reproduce exactly.
- **Evidence.** `/tmp/mailsense-round28-baseline.txt` (3 top-level red:
  the Latin phrase test, the folded-quote test and the API test with 5 of
  6 subtests red; the CJK phrase test already held and is the guard),
  `/tmp/mailsense-round28-measure-before.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round28-after.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round28-measure-after.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round28b-fast.log`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round28b-playwright.log`.
- **Gates.** See `docs/BENCHMARK_LEDGER.md` Round 28 for the tails.
- **Open issues / residual.** A recall query that mixes a MATCH term and a
  short scan term still ANDs the scan term: FTS5 rejects `MATCH` inside an
  `OR` (the SQL error is "unable to use function MATCH in the requested
  context"). The all-scan recall form now ORs its scans
  (`TestSearchAnyScanTermsAreOred`); the mixed form is recorded, not
  expanded in this round. Snippet anchoring was completed in Round 29;
  Indic script routing remains a candidate for the next store-FTS round.

## 2026-10-28 — Unavailable-index reconcile backoff

- **Gap.** An unavailable embedder made the 2-minute reconcile repeat the
  full work every tick: `Ensure` planned the 33,842-message coverage, the
  run planned it again, and `finish` planned a third time before writing a
  failed `index_runs` row (plus learning `Stage.Status` plans). In a 130 s
  live window on a disposable copy of the prepared audit store, the
  pre-change binary wrote **2 rows** for the run set (the initial run and
  the 120 s tick; **1 row and 1 failed embedding call fall inside the
  window**), and used **2.39 / 2.41 / 2.36 CPU-s** over three samples
  (1.84 / 1.85 / 1.82 % of one core, `/proc/<pid>/stat` utime+stime,
  GOMAXPROCS=4). A 370 s sample added **3 runs / 3 rows** across three
  ticks after the first finish (4 rows total), 3 failed calls, 5.37 CPU-s.
- **Fix.** A new process-local wait, `index.retry_unavailable` (duration,
  default 15m, bounds 2m…1h, "Semantic index"), is armed after an
  unavailable run that committed no vector (`StoppedBy=unavailable` and
  `!Report.Committed()`). While it is active, `Ensure` returns the stopped
  run's starting coverage and does not plan, start a run or call the
  provider. The wait belongs to a `retryKey` of the vector space, text
  version, `Store.MailGeneration()`, the folder-role scope and
  `index.quarantine_after`; any change of those inputs ends it, as do an
  effective settings change (`config.changed`), a healthy
  `engine.provider` status for the configured embedder and a
  `sidecar.state` that reaches `ready` (the command wires the last two; the
  index package never imports the sidecar). A committed unavailable run, a
  transient stop, `store_busy`, cancellation and every-batch-failed do not
  arm it: they may have written vectors or failure records and must
  re-plan. The finishing unavailable no-vector run reuses its starting
  coverage instead of the third plan, so its report cannot fold its own
  recorded failures into a coverage change it never wrote.
- **Blocker.** The latest unavailable row is untouched and unpruned
  (Round 26 keep=1 still works), so `Stage.Status` keeps reporting
  `blocked`/`no_embedder` with the exact error while the reconcile is
  quiet. Nothing is hidden and no pending mail is dropped.
- **Evidence.** Baseline before the implementation:
  `/tmp/mailsense-round27-baseline.txt` (9 test functions red; the first
  backoff test fails with "Ensure started 1 run(s) during the wait" at
  tick 0) and `/tmp/mailsense-round27-live-baseline.txt` (before samples
  above). After: `/tmp/mailsense-round27-after.txt` (all red tests green,
  existing index tests unchanged) and `/tmp/mailsense-round27-live-after.txt`:
  130 s after the first finish wrote **0 new rows** for the run set (**1 row
  for the run set, the initial run; 0 written inside the window**), made **0 failed embedding calls** and used
  **1.02 / 0.95 / 0.97 CPU-s** (0.78 / 0.73 / 0.75 % of one core) over three samples; the
  2-minute tick logged the cached coverage and started nothing. A 370 s
  sample stayed at **1 row for the run set, 0 new runs**, 0 calls, 1.07
  CPU-s (before: 3 new runs/3 rows, 3 calls, 5.37 CPU-s). Live plan counts
  are not
  instrumented (no plan-level log line): the deterministic test proves the
  absence of a plan with a quarantine-count probe whose direct
  `index_failures` write changes a fresh plan but not the cached coverage.
- **Gates.** Targeted tests, `-race`, `scripts/test-fast.sh` and Playwright
  were run after the final edit; see `docs/BENCHMARK_LEDGER.md` Round 27
  for the tails.
- **Open issues.** None for this round. A manual run and a sync still run
  during the wait (a sync that brings mail changes the mail generation and
  therefore the key); they are deliberate probes, not automatic reconcile
  ticks.

## 2026-10-28 — Index run history retention

- **Gap.** `index_runs` had no prune. The reconciler plans every 2 minutes
  (`indexReconcileInterval`) and a stuck or unavailable embedder selects the
  same pending mail on every pass, so a failed run could be written every
  2 minutes forever (720/day in principle). The synthetic fixture in the
  store test models a failed run with a 1,904 B report, a 299 B error and
  58 B of metadata: 2,261 B of columns. The prepared audit store's 7
  failed rows separately measure 2,326 B each by the same column-length
  sum (1,904 B report + 299 B error + 123 B metadata). At 2,261–2,326 B
  per row that is about 1.6–1.7 MB/day at the 2-minute cadence (inferred,
  not a 24-hour measurement).
- **Fix.** `index.runs.keep` (int, default 100, 1…1,000,000, "Semantic
  index") owns retention. `Store.PruneIndexRuns` keeps the newest N rows
  and returns `RowsAffected`, clamping `keep` to at least 1. The indexer
  calls it with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` after `FinishIndexRun`
  succeeds, using the same finish-path owner as the evidence engine; a
  prune failure is a warning and never fails the run. `BeginIndexRun`,
  `ListIndexRuns` and startup do not prune. The latest run is always kept,
  so `Stage.lastRunUnavailable` still reports the stage blocker with a
  `keep` of 1. Retention deletes rows only: SQLite reuses the pages and the
  database file may not shrink; there is no `VACUUM`. The setting is
  advanced tuning and stays out of `SETTINGS_SIMPLE_GROUPS`; the French
  catalog carries its description.
- **Evidence.** Before any production change
  (`/tmp/mailsense-round26-baseline.txt`): five real runs with
  `index.runs.keep=2` left **5** rows and the setting was still unknown;
  two `stopped_by=unavailable` runs with `keep=1` left **2** rows; the
  synthetic 105-row fixture totals **237,405 B** of
  `length(started_at)+…+length(error)` before any prune (2,261.0 B/row;
  synthetic SQLite data, not the real mailbox). The store owner test did
  not compile (`PruneIndexRuns` undefined). After
  (`/tmp/mailsense-round26-after.txt`): five runs → **2** rows with the
  newest report intact; two unavailable runs → **1** row with
  `Stage.Status` still blocked (`no_embedder`) on the latest error; the
  keep table passed for keeps 0/1/2/5/10 (0 clamps to 1) and under the
  cap; 105 synthetic rows → **100** rows (the newest 100 ids), payload
  **237,405 → 226,100 B** (5 × 2,261 B pruned). The default is 100, the French key exists and the
  simple view does not list the setting. The full-store database-file size
  after retention was not measured; freed pages are reused without a
  `VACUUM`, so the file may stay the same.
- **Gates.** `go test ./internal/index ./internal/store ./internal/config
  ./internal/ui ./cmd/mailsense -count=1`, `-race` index/store,
  `scripts/test-fast.sh` and Playwright were run after the final edit; see
  `docs/BENCHMARK_LEDGER.md` Round 26 for the tails.
- **Open issues.** None for this round. Round 27 is the reconcile-backoff
  follow-up: retention bounds the rows, but a stuck embedder still pays a
  run (and its planning) every 2 minutes.

## 2026-10-28 — Windows Vulkan preflight

- **Gap.** On Windows the catalog published one managed `vulkan` build and
  the install path downloaded the model and the runtime archive before any
  start: **342,039,075 B** (309,855,456 B model + 32,183,619 B archive). A
  machine without a usable Vulkan device could pay all of it and then
  fail, or silently use the CPU backend DLLs the archive is audit-reported
  to ship. The b11617 zip itself is audit-reported to contain no
  `vulkan-1.dll`; the artifact was not available here to re-check.
- **Fix.** A variant may declare `requires`; the Windows build declares
  `"requires": "vulkan"`. One `Manager.require` runs before an install job
  exists, before `layout.verify`, before the install progress total and
  before `StateProbing`, and never in `New`. On Windows it creates a
  Vulkan instance and enumerates a physical device through
  `golang.org/x/sys/windows` (System32-only loader, no cgo); on other
  platforms the probe fails explicitly with `ErrVulkanProbe`. Missing
  driver/device is `ErrNoVulkan` (permanent for the supervisor, 422
  `vulkan_unavailable`); a failed check is `ErrVulkanProbe` (retryable,
  never cached, 503 `vulkan_probe_failed`). A confirmed device is cached
  until the existing `Reprobe` action; a missing device is re-probed on
  each status read, the card's Refresh invalidates the cached
  `/api/sidecar` status before re-reading (so it sees a newly installed
  driver within the 15 s TTL), and a probe failure is retried. `auto` with
  no cpu build returns the
  typed error with zero installs and zero starts; a named build returns it
  before the canary, `markBroken` and any fallback. `BuildInfo.Unavailable`
  (`vulkan`/`probe_failed`) drives the runtime card, which hides the
  install/repair action, the first-use copy and the engine size and keeps
  Refresh. No CPU fallback, second build, setting or variant picker.
  Unknown `requires` values are rejected by `parseCatalog` for the embedded
  catalog and overlays.
- **Evidence.** Baseline before any production change
  (`/tmp/mailsense-round25-baseline.txt`): the synthetic control (GPU
  variant with no `requires`) made 1 model request, 1 archive request,
  served 10,744,219 B (16,384 B fake model + 10,727,835 B fake test-binary
  archive), created 1 install job, started the runtime and moved
  installing → starting → canary → ready; the real catalog total is asserted as
  342,039,075 B and is not the synthetic number. After
  (`/tmp/mailsense-round25-after.txt`): no device (auto and vulkan) made
  **0** model/archive requests, **0 B**, **0** install jobs, **0** starts,
  only `failed` (`Unavailable="vulkan"`, `Installed=false`); a failing
  probe was 0 B/0 jobs with `Unavailable="probe_failed"`; a present device
  still installed (1/1, 10,776,987 B, 1 job, started; the fake archive grew
  because it is the test binary). Probe calls on a no-device machine:
  start + 2×`Builds` = 3 (a negative result is not cached, so Refresh
  re-probes), `Reprobe` + `Builds` = 4; a present device is cached (start +
  `Builds` = 1); the error path was not cached (3 calls over
  Install/Builds/Install). API codes 422/503 covered by
  `TestSidecarInstallVulkanErrorCodes` and
  `TestSidecarStatusReportsUnavailableBuild`. Gates:
  `go test ./internal/sidecar ./internal/api ./internal/ui
  ./internal/config -count=1` green; `-race` sidecar/api green;
  `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` green with no output (compile check only);
  `scripts/test-fast.sh` green (78 packages); Playwright 31/31, including
  `e2e/specs/runtime.spec.ts` (the Refresh click observes the second
  `/api/sidecar` read).
- **Open.** The live Windows probe and the real 0-byte Windows install are
  blocked on a Windows host; `TestVulkanLiveProbe` is opt-in via
  `MAILSENSE_VULKAN_LIVE=1` and `MAILSENSE_VULKAN_EXPECT=present|none`.
  The archive's DLL contents remain audit-reported. The synthetic control
  byte count varies with the test binary, so only its call/job/start counts
  are stable. A confirmed-device result is cached, and the existing
  `Reprobe` action forgets it when a driver is removed or changed; a
  missing device is never cached, so a newly installed driver is picked up
  by Refresh.

## 2026-10-28 — Q&A answer language: notice-only

- **Gap.** A grounded written answer could come back in another language
  than the requested `en`/`fr` and the Ask card showed it exactly like a
  matching answer. A naive language check over the whole answer also
  false-rejected French answers that quote an English mail sentence.
- **Fix.** One shared post-grounding check,
  `finalizeGeneratedAnswer` (`internal/qa/language.go`), now runs at the
  planner JSON answer, the grounded prose fallback and the entity summary.
  It strips quoted reply text with `mail.CleanBody`, judges only answers
  with at least `qa.answer_language.min_letters` letters (default 30), and
  sets the new `answer_language` notice on a confident mismatch. The check
  is notice-only: it never retries, rewrites, translates or falls back to
  retrieval, and never overwrites an existing notice. The answer, mode,
  citations, counts, provider and model are unchanged. A noticed answer is
  saved to history but excluded from the in-memory answer cache, so a
  re-ask calls the provider again. The UI shows the answer, citations and
  provider/model footer beside an `answer_language` warning with no retry
  button, and `askAutoView` still accepts the generated view.
- **Evidence.** Fixed synthetic corpus (24 host answers, 12 quoted-mail, 14
  wrong-language, 3 short/ambiguous). Pre-fix baseline: host accepted
  24/24, quoted-mail false rejects 0/12 and short unjudged 3/3 — all
  vacuous — with wrong-language notices **0/14**; raw detector strict
  agreement **20/24** and raw quoted-mail false rejects **4/12 (33.3%)**;
  quote-stripped **24/24**. The audit's earlier 19/24 and 5/12 (41.7%) did
  not reproduce on this corpus. After the fix: host accepted **24/24**,
  quoted-mail false rejects **0/12**, wrong-language notices **14/14**
  (en↔fr/de/es), short unjudged **3/3**; generator calls after a repeated
  ask: matching **1**, wrong-language **2**, wrong-language summary **2**.
  Logs `/tmp/mailsense-round24-baseline.txt`,
  `/tmp/mailsense-round24-after.txt`, `/tmp/mailsense-round24-calls.txt`.
  Gates: targeted packages, `-race` qa/api, `scripts/test-fast.sh` (78
  packages) and Playwright 30/30 green.
- **Open.** The corpus is fixed synthetic data, not the audit's original
  corpus, so the raw 20/24 is corpus-specific. Detection is statistical: a
  genuinely bilingual answer may be noticed, but the notice preserves the
  answer. No live provider call was made; the tests inject the fake
  generator.

## 2026-10-27 — A warm index that cannot miss a question; repaired legacy text

- **Gap.** A fresh “que veut commander le ciusss” returned
  `qa_index_warming` on a mailbox whose semantic index was complete
  (34,938/34,938). The log proved it was not history replay:
  `semantic index did not finish within the semantic budget (150ms)` at
  22:43:38, followed by four `qa retrieval degraded` warnings over the next
  22 seconds. Four independent defects combined:
  1. the 150 ms interactive timer bounded the **whole** semantic leg —
     vector refresh, coverage count and the owner-filter scan — not just the
     query embedding;
  2. the timer **cancelled** the worker, discarding that preparation, so each
     retry repeated the same cold work;
  3. `OwnerOnly` filters bypassed the id-set cache and re-listed 34,938 rows
     on every question;
  4. QA labelled *any* degraded semantic leg “the index is preparing”, and
     persisted it, so the card replayed forever.
- **Fix.**
  - `search.Query.Wait` (used only by Q&A) completes the semantic leg with no
    interactive timer. The caller’s context is the only bound
    (`qa.retrieval_timeout`, 30 s).
  - A waiting search merges the vectors an index catch-up writes and waits for
    coverage before ranking; `search.Deps.Ensure` wires
    `index.Indexer.Ensure`, so a message that arrived moments ago is indexed
    before the answer.
  - The interactive search box keeps its 150 ms race, but its abandoned worker
    now **finishes** the vector/coverage/filter preparation for the next
    query instead of being cancelled.
  - Filter id sets are cached per filter and mail generation (bounded at 8),
    including the owner scope.
  - Startup calls `Searcher.Prepare` before the port is announced: the vector
    copy, coverage and both filter sets are loaded warm. It does not start the
    local model, so readiness stays fast; the background warm-up embeds the
    first query after readiness.
  - `qa_index_warming` now means a genuinely incomplete index after the wait.
    A warm index that misses its bound reports `qa_retrieval_timeout`
    (“the local search ran out of time”), never “warming”.
  - Transient retrieval notices are not saved to history. Migration 0022
    deletes the old `qa_index_warming` rows (they had no answer, provider or
    citation); the legacy `qa_unavailable` remap now produces
    `qa_retrieval_timeout`.
- **Accents / old conversations.** The live `qa_history` contained three rows
  stored as `C383C2A9` (`RÃ©sume`) while the surrounding text was correct —
  valid UTF-8 mojibake produced by a legacy writer or an ANSI-read PowerShell
  request. `internal/textx.Repair` now repairs unambiguous
  UTF-8-read-as-Windows-1252 sequences at the one question boundary, and a
  one-time counted store repair fixes saved questions and answers
  (`saved answer text repaired rows=5 sequences=11`). The API rejects a body
  that is not valid UTF-8 with `invalid_encoding` instead of letting
  `encoding/json` substitute U+FFFD. Ordinary accented text ("café") is never
  touched.
- **Verification.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` green (including `-race` on qa/api)
  and the exhaustive `scripts/test.sh` green. New tests cover the waiting
  search outlasting 150 ms, the abandoned worker finishing its preparation,
  the warm-index timeout not being “warming”, the mojibake repair (unit, QA
  boundary, store backfill), invalid UTF-8 rejection, and the accent
  round-trip through `/api/ask`.
  Windows build `0.1.0-dev+20261027233201` is live: migration 0022 applied,
  the store repaired 5 rows / 11 sequences, `semantic index prepared`
  reported 34,938 vectors and 34,938 eligible 11 ms **before**
  `mailsense ready`, a fresh “que veut commander le ciusss” returned a
  generated answer with 3 citations in 3.1 s and no notice, and an accented
  “Résume le dernier échange avec messagerie-exemple.test” round-tripped as `c3a9` with a
  generated answer in 2.5 s. `/api/ask/history` reports 0 warming rows (the 5
  legacy timeout rows are retained, not deleted). No `qa retrieval degraded`
  line was written after the deploy.
- **Open.** A retrieval that genuinely exceeds `qa.retrieval_timeout` still
  shows the timeout card; it is no longer mislabelled as warming and no longer
  replays from history.

## 2026-10-27 — First-run time zone confirmation

- **Gap.** The machine stage stayed blocked on `time_zone_unconfirmed`
  until the owner opened the Learning dialog and retyped a zone WebView2
  already knows. The zone was the last manual machine fact before label
  work.
- **Fix.** `autoConfirmZone` runs after the first `/api/learning` load and
  before the event stream opens. When the machine stage carries
  `time_zone_unconfirmed`, it reads
  `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, posts it to
  `POST /api/learning/zone`, reloads learning and status, and shows one
  information toast. The manual `confirm_time_zone` dialog remains the
  fallback for an invalid/refused zone or a failed call; the function
  never blocks boot.
- **Verification.** `scripts/test-ui.sh` 24/24, including
  `timezone.spec.ts` (a mocked machine blocker must produce the POST with a
  non-empty IANA zone); `scripts/test-fast.sh` and the exhaustive
  `scripts/test.sh` are green. Windows build
  `0.1.0-dev+20261027223950` is live: `time.zone=America/Toronto` is
  present, the machine stage reports no blockers, and the remaining gate
  blockers are the label requirement. The live zone was already confirmed
  from an earlier run, so the browser test, not the live host, is the
  direct evidence for the new auto-confirm path. This build also carries
  the final All Mail row cleanup (no redundant per-row store badge).

## 2026-10-27 — One global job strip and gap repair

- **Gap.** `/api/jobs` was read only by Learning and Sources, and
  `jobs.update` was handled as a refresh trigger with its payload ignored.
  A running sync, index, evidence or backfill job was invisible outside
  those screens. A reconnected or overflowed stream repaired only the log
  ring; every other live read could stay stale.
- **Job model.** `state.jobs` is the one shell job model. The
  `jobs.update` payload is a complete `jobs.Info`, so `upsertJob` merges it
  without a fetch; `loadJobs` seeds it from `/api/jobs` before the stream
  opens. The strip between the topbar and `#main` reconciles chips by job
  id and patches the progress bar and counts in place, so a cancel button
  is never replaced under the pointer. A running job can be cancelled from
  the strip; a failure lingers ten seconds with a dismiss action; a
  finished job lingers four.
- **Gap repair.** The first transport `error` marks a gap; the next `open`
  schedules one 400 ms resync that forces status, learning and jobs,
  invalidates the live reads and route nodes, and refreshes the active
  screen through the existing focus guard. A synthetic `dropped` frame
  does the same because missed events are not replayed. The initial job
  snapshot is read before `connectEvents`, so boot cannot race the first
  event.
- **Language and accessibility.** The strip re-renders on a language
  change; `state.succeeded` was missing from both catalogs and is now
  present. A hidden `role="status"` region announces start/finish/failure
  only, never every percentage.
- **Log noise.** The sidecar health client now logs a successful probe at
  debug (`httpx.WithQuietSuccess`); its failures still log at warn. At the
  default info level the five-second probe no longer pushes useful entries
  out of the 2,000-entry ring. `TestQuietSuccessLogsAtDebug` covers the
  level.
- **Verification.** `scripts/test-ui.sh` 22/22, including the new
  `live.spec.ts`: a running job appears, patches 1,234 → 20,000 in place,
  finishes and leaves; a reconnect issues a fresh `/api/jobs` read.
  `scripts/test-fast.sh` green; `go test ./internal/httpx ./internal/sidecar`
  green. Windows build `0.1.0-dev+20261027222704` is live: the served shell
  contains `#job-strip` and `#job-live`, the assets contain `upsertJob`,
  `paintJobStrip` and `scheduleLiveResync`, and the healthy five-second
  probe no longer logs at info.

## 2026-10-27 — Exact entity summaries and a reasoning-safe Q&A cap

- **Live failures.** `Summarize the last exchange with
  nadia@famille-exemple.test` asked a company/person clarification even
  though the address names one person. `Summarize the last exchange with
  messagerie-exemple.test` returned `retrieval` with `qa_generation_failed`. The
  ambiguous `... with Nadia` already produced six one-click candidates.
- **Entity precedence.** `selectEntityCandidates` now prefers an explicit
  address (a person), then a bare domain (a company), before the generic
  person word and the evidence comparison; a company word still wins when
  the owner says "client". `entityMention` already keeps an address out of
  the domain list, so an addressed person cannot become a domain company.
  `TestSelectEntityCandidatesPrefersExplicitIdentity` covers the live
  address, the live domain, a same-name different-domain choice and the
  company word; `TestEntityMentionKeepsAnAddressOutOfDomains` covers the
  parser boundary.
- **Generation root cause (two owners).** The Q&A source replaced the
  provider's output cap with `qa.max_answer_tokens=350`. The configured
  DeepSeek record reasons at `low` effort: the response spent 350 tokens on
  `reasoning_content`, hit `finish_reason=length` and returned a null
  `content`. Separately, the record's `response_format=json_object` (the
  planner's strict contract) was applied to the summary prompt, which asks
  for prose. A summary could therefore fail even with enough tokens.
- **Fix.** `engine.Provider.AnswerOutputTokens` adds the effort's reasoning
  allowance (low 4096) to the answer budget, clamped to the record's
  declared output reserve; `qa.NewSource` applies it, so the budget
  reservation and `max_tokens` cover reasoning plus answer. A new
  `engine.GenerateOptions{Prose: true}` lets one call omit the record's
  JSON mode; the summary uses it, while the planner and judge keep JSON.
  The planner's contract-failure retry, which masked the truncation, is
  removed; a contract failure now reports `qa_generation_failed` once with
  the retrieved sources.
- **Privacy hardening.** `http.log.body_max_bytes` now defaults to 0
  (body logging off). At the old 4096 default, enabling debug wrote the
  whole summary prompt, including mail bodies and the owner's addresses,
  to the log; secret redaction does not remove owner content. The live
  setting is 0 and `log.level` is back to `info`.
- **Verification.** `scripts/test-fast.sh` green, including the new
  `source_test.go` wiring test (reasoning cap 4446 and JSON mode kept) and
  the prose adapter test; `scripts/test-ui.sh` 20/20. Windows build
  `0.1.0-dev+20261027221353` is live. `nadia@famille-exemple.test` returns
  `generated` with five DNS-thread citations; `messagerie-exemple.test` returns
  `generated` with three PHP-vulnerability citations; `Nadia` still
  clarifies. The first search after startup took 166.9 ms with semantic
  used and coverage 34,938/34,938; no `qa_generation_failed` in the new
  history.
- **Open.** A settings reload can rebuild the embedder on the next query
  (173 ms end-to-end, still semantic). The first search after a restart
  remains a manual check. A full `/api/live` snapshot and per-screen
  patchers remain; this slice covers the one job model, the global strip
  and gap repair.
