## 2026-10-25 — Route completed (calibration stage) and the cascade finding

The certified route is built, wired and measured. The app's answer for a
question is now the route: layer-0 key → layer 1 → stored SubQ, each layer
only above its own certified gate, else an abstention that escalates.

- **Finding (fixed):** the first implementation cut all layers with one
  global score (`band + confidence`). Layer 1 offers on nearly every
  message, so SubQ's gate was measured on almost no rows, SubQ was never
  a member, and the route measured exactly like layer 1 alone: 25.54 %
  vs 25.56 % dev-curve coverage at 0.99, with zero SubQ answers. The
  documented chain is a cascade, not one cut. `internal/route` now
  chooses each layer's gate on **all** of that layer's labelled selection
  offers, and the first member at or above its gate answers; a higher
  member below its gate falls through. The cascade's decisions are
  certified with the new `selective.CertifyFixed`, which chooses nothing
  on the certification labels (no scan, no cut), so a route's
  `Certification.Threshold` is 0 and every consumer reads `Certified`.
- **Dev measurement (`v8-route-cascade`, dev split only, test split
  sealed, 240 items per question, 481 gold messages excluded):** mean
  accuracy layer 1 0.7811, SubQ 0.8270 (unchanged). Route dev-curve
  coverage at 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99 / 1.00: **0.8483 / 0.8023 / 0.6982 /
  0.5518** (layer 1: 0.4255 / 0.3145 / 0.2556 / 0.2096; SubQ: 0.6321 /
  0.5135 / 0.4500 / 0.3846). At 0.99 SubQ gives 914 of the 2,085
  point-operating-point answers.
- **Honest certification is unchanged: 0/17 questions at 0.99.** The
  certification part holds 117 labels per question; 381 error-free
  answers are needed (189 at 0.98). At 0.95 only `suspicious` certifies
  (240 answers, 1 error, Wilson lower bound 0.996). The route's point
  operating point at 0.99 is 2,085 answers / 37 errors (0.9823) — an
  estimate, never what the app answers. **Labels are now the only
  binding constraint.**
- **Storage:** migration 0012 `route_answers` (message, fingerprint,
  revision, answers JSON, run id, decided at; PK message+fingerprint).
  One row per message and profile, every question present (abstentions
  included so the app escalates), written in the same transaction as the
  layer-1 answers, promotions and report (`Layer1Commit.Routes`); a
  failed or cancelled commit writes no routes and keeps the old ones.
- **Stages:** `calibration` (`layer1.RouteStage`) is wired; it waits for
  evidence/embeddings/layer 1, blocks `route_not_routed` with
  `run_layer1` when the last pass has no route for a question or
  `Routed != Answered`, and is done otherwise. `questions` now certifies
  the route (five plain-language blocker cases, `label_messages` with
  the remaining count, `run_judge`, `review_requirements`).
- **Read path:** `triage.UseRoute` is wired in `cmd`. `Read` serves
  `route_answers` only under the profile fingerprint (`View.Routed`),
  never mixing the paid cache; `Stale` follows the row's message
  revision; an abstained answer reaches `Result` with the question and no
  value, so `Uncertain`/`Escalate` fire. `Plan`/`Run` still use the paid
  key. `Priors.blend` and the search triage filter ignore abstentions.
- **Rescore:** a label-only change rebuilds the offers from stored data
  (stored layer-1 answers, stored SubQ, rules re-measured on the
  selection labels), re-certifies and re-answers in the same transaction;
  a no-op rescore is byte-identical to the run
  (`TestRescoreReproducesTheRouteAnswers`).

Gate: `scripts/test.sh` green with `-race` (764 test functions plus the
fuzz target); `scripts/build.sh all` green (exe 16,832,512 bytes).

Open: the certification labels are conversation-clustered, so the Wilson
bound assumes more independence than the data has (design risk, not
addressed); the layer-0 key branch is unmeasured on dev (no rule key
fires there), covered by unit tests only; the labels stage and the judge
are still `NotBuilt`, so the gate cannot open.

## 2026-10-25 — Route foundation (calibration stage, part 1)

The certified answer route now exists as a pure, tested module. It is not
wired into the app yet, so the `calibration` stage stays `NotBuilt` and the
gate cannot open; this entry records the foundation only.

- `internal/selective`:
  - `Certification.Eligible` and `CertifyEligible(sel, cert, eligible,
    target, z)`: coverage is answered certification messages over every
    eligible one, so a stack that answers 3 of 100 labels cannot report
    coverage 1.0. `Certify` is the same call with `len(cert)`; its
    behaviour and every existing test are unchanged. `Eligible` is raised
    to `len(cert)` when a caller passes less (coverage can never exceed 1).
  - `Given(q, probs, cutoff)`: the one answer shape (choice/value/
    confidence/probabilities), extracted from `Answer`; `Answer` is now
    the threshold check plus `Given`.
  - `NoThreshold` moved from 2.0 to 4.0. A route score is
    `band + confidence` (bands 2/1/0 for key/layer 1/SubQ, maximum 3), so a
    real cut at exactly 2.0 was indistinguishable from "no threshold".
    Regression test: `TestStackScoreAtTwoIsARealCut` (before: threshold
    2.0, 20/20 rows, zero answered; after: answered). A stored threshold
    of 2.0 still abstains (above every confidence) and the model's
    `Certified` flag is a separate field, so no persisted state is
    misread as certified.
- `internal/route` (new, pure: only `engine` and `selective`; no I/O,
  clock, store or config): `Layer`, `Offer`, `Item`, `Member`, `State`,
  `Answer`, `Build`, `Decide`, `Threshold`.
  - Bands key 2 → layer 1 1 → SubQ 0 (algorithm constants). Each layer's
    gate is chosen on the labelled selection items whose highest-priority
    offer is that layer's; the stack's one threshold is chosen on the
    same selection rows and tested exactly once
    (`CertifyEligible`) on the disjoint certification items, with the
    denominator counting every eligible certification label.
  - An uncertified route answers nothing (`not_certified`); no member
    offering is `no_answer`; below the cut is `below_target` with no
    usable value; a lower layer never falls through.
  - Deterministic: ascending ids, a total order (band, then confidence),
    no map iteration.

Tests added (12 route, 4 selective), including: the route chooses nothing
on the certification part (flipping every certification label leaves
`Threshold` and `Members` bitwise identical); a non-member never answers;
abstentions carry no value in all question types; determinism under
shuffled offers; coverage cannot hide unanswered labels; the counted
answers are exactly the answered ones; adding a lower band never lowers
selection coverage; malformed items and offers are refused.

Consequence of the SubQ 1.1 switch (same day): the layer-1 runner test had
the live decider key hard-coded (`subq/subq-snap-preview`) while the plan
now derives `subq/subq-snap-1.1` from the catalog, so
`TestRunTrainsPromotesAndAnswers` and
`TestTargetIDsShowEveryMessageThatTrained` failed deterministically on the
current tree. Fixed at the owner: the test takes `plan.DeciderKey`, so it
follows the catalog instead of duplicating the model id; three stale test
literals of the live key were updated to 1.1. The legacy teacher key
(`legacy:subq-snap-preview`) keeps its provenance.

Gate: `scripts/test.sh` green with `-race` (gofmt, the relay selftest,
`bash -n`, vet host + windows + every tag, the full suite: 737 test
functions plus the fuzz target, 722 test and fuzz functions before);

## 2026-10-25 — SubQ Snap 1.1 is the decision model

The preset moved from `subq-snap-preview` ($0.05/M input, 16 questions
per request) to `subq-snap-1.1` ($0.04/M input, 1–128 questions, same
`systemone` wire contract). The project key now lists both ids, so the
2026-10-12 restriction no longer applies.

Evidence (live, project key, 2026-10-25):
- `GET /v1/models` → `subq-snap-1.1`, `subq-snap-preview`.
- `POST /v1/systemone` with 17, 64 and 128 tiny noul questions → 200,
  every answer present, `usage.output_tokens` 0. The documented cap is
  128, so the 17-question profile now goes out in ONE call, not two.
- `scripts/triage-live.sh 6 2` through the app's adapter: probe
  `model=subq-snap-1.1`; 6 messages = 6 calls, 19,704 input tokens,
  $0.00079 (planned $0.00114); p50 247 ms, p95 292 ms; repeat agreement
  2 messages = 34/34 answers identical, max |Δ| 0.0000.

Consequences: SubQ input tokens per message roughly halve (the state is
sent once instead of twice) and the price per token drops 20 %. The
preset's `max_questions` is 128; `context_tokens` stays 384K and
`reserve_tokens_per_byte` 1 (the budget ceiling is unchanged). Cached
answers under `subq/subq-snap-preview` stay valid for what they are and
are not mixed into the new key: a re-decision is a user action, per the
paid-answer policy. The legacy teacher key `legacy:subq-snap-preview`
keeps its name (it names the data's true provenance).

Docs updated: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (engine table),
`docs/DECISION_PROVIDERS.md` (preset table, response sample, live
verification), `NOTES.md` (the dated key restriction). Tests updated:
`internal/engine/catalog_test.go` (model, `max_questions`). Gate:
`go test ./internal/engine/...` green; live probe green.

Open: `triage.budget.max_usd` still defaults to $1.00, which at one call
per message covers ~1,000 messages per run; a full-mailbox re-decision is
still a separate, explicit budget decision.

Plan: the layer-1 design (heads on EmbeddingGemma vectors + layer-0
features, teachers as data, grouped cross-fitting, calibration, the
learning stage); `docs/LAYER1.md` is the reference once built.

Step 1 — the gold TEST split is sealed (`internal/goldset`,
`scripts/gold-seal.sh`), before any layer-1 code read gold:
- `goldset.Seal` moved every line and value naming one of the 241 test
  messages, from EVERY file of the gold directory (labels, inputs, the
  judges' batches, labels, notes, adjudication files and the
  disagreement list), into `sealed/` (mode 000): 31 files, 1,872 lines or
  values sealed, 2,913 kept; 3 files named no test message (strata,
  taxonomy, wording notes). Verified by id counts only (per file: kept +
  sealed = before; 241 test lines in each full file); a second run seals
  nothing. Nothing of a test line was printed or read beyond its id.
- `goldset.Open` reads the train and dev labels only and refuses a
  directory that is not sealed or still names a test message outside
  `sealed/` [corrected in review round L1: it then checked
  gold-labels.jsonl only; it now runs the seal planner over every file]; `goldset.OpenTest` needs `GOLD_UNSEAL=<frozen model digest>`
  (not a `MAILSENSE_*` name: the config refuses unknown ones), writes the
  ledger entry before reading, and refuses a second unsealing.
- The evidence fixture and live measurements read gold through goldset
  (the one loader; its private `goldLabels` decoding is gone).
- Disclosure (from the planning round): the planning agent printed 4
  lines of `gold-labels.jsonl` and `splits.json`; two of those lines were
  test items and part of one test input was seen. Nothing from them was
  used. Leftover judge working files in the session scratchpad (outside
  the gold directory, not written by this round) still name test ids —
  listed for the lead, not read.

Step 2 — embeddings (`scripts/layer1-fixture.sh embed`, in the
background): real EmbeddingGemma vectors through the pinned Linux
sidecar into the private vector cache (`fixturetest.VectorCache`,
`~/.cache/mailsense-layer1/vectors`, mode 700, one append-only file per
space keyed by the exact input; a cut record from an interrupted write is
dropped on open). The experiment sample (600 gold + 8,000 drawn by legacy
category, seeded) in the document, classification and clustering
prompts (the EmbeddingGemma model card's `task: classification | query:`
and `task: clustering | query:` prompts, verified on ai.google.dev and
the Hugging Face card; subject and cleaned body as the query text — the
prompts have no title slot), then the whole fixture (document vectors).
Measured: 5.4–5.9 messages/s on a quiet box, 2.6–4 while the box was
shared (load average 12–30, other users' jobs).

Step 3 — built (code, tests; numbers below as they come):
- `internal/optim` (L-BFGS + Armijo, deterministic, cancellable,
  non-finite refused; quadratic, Rosenbrock, non-convex, cancel,
  curvature-skip tests).
- `internal/layer1`: heads (multinomial, logistic, cumulative logit with
  ordered cut points; finite-difference gradient checks of every head and
  of the whole sharded objective with folded standardisation), targets,
  teachers and requirements as data (all-errors validation, per-question
  overrides), grouped folds, metrics (selective accuracy, coverage at
  target with Wilson, AURC, ECE, κ), calibration/kNN pooling, causal kNN,
  the pass (`Plan`, `Train` over `Inputs`), the runner (promotion,
  answers under decider `layer1`, `AfterRuns`), the `layer1` and
  `questions` stages wired in `cmd/mailsense` (calibration/routing and
  labels stay not built).
- `vector.Set` (moved out of `search`: search and kNN share it),
  `config.Overlay` (the one "shipped data + user file" reader; evidence
  uses it), `evidence.FeatureLayout.Indices` (sparse cells; `Vector` is
  built from it), `evidence.Rule.Parsed`, store migration 0011
  (`layer1_models`, `layer1_runs`), `store.SaveDecisions` /
  `ReplaceDecisions` / `DecisionSummary`, `archive.ImportLegacyAnswers`.
- Settings (group "Layer 1", defaults): `layer1.after_runs` true,
  `workers` 0, `shard_rows` 512, `teachers.file`, `requirements.file`,
  `features.embedding` true, `features.evidence` true,
  `embedding.dimensions` 0, `l2.grid_log10` [-4,-3,-2,-1],
  `heads.score` multinomial (added in round v4), `l2.default_log10` -3,
  `lbfgs.memory` 10, `lbfgs.max_iterations` 300, `lbfgs.tolerance` 1e-4
  (1e-6 until round v2), `cv.folds` 5, `cv.min_eval_labels` 30,
  `knn.enabled` false, `knn.k` 20, `knn.temperature` 0.05,
  `knn.prior_strength` 1, `calibration.method` temperature,
  `retrain.min_new_labels` 20, `promote.max_nll_regression` 0.01.
  Actions added: `label_messages`, `run_judge`, `choose_teacher`,
  `review_requirements`, `run_layer1`.
- Cost finding: the first design cross-fitted every λ of the grid (4 λ ×
  (1 + 5 folds) = 24 fits per question): far too slow on 9–34k rows. Now
  the λ path runs on every target but the evaluation labels (each λ
  scores the evaluation labels out of sample: one fit per λ), then one
  cross-fitting at the chosen λ (10 fits per question; a cold start
  cross-fits every λ, over a few hundred rows). One objective evaluation
  (9,000 rows × 768+584 columns, 7 classes) 22–50 ms on the shared box.
- Guard finding (first harness run, `e1-document`): the harness guard
  failed the run — 393 excluded gold dev/test messages had a target. The
  wrapper filtered labels and decisions but not the layer-0 rule firings
  (the measured `suspicious` rules fire on most mail). Fixed in the
  wrapper (`harnessInputs.Rules` drops the excluded messages' firings);
  the guard now runs on every harness pass (`Trained.TargetIDs`, unit
  test `TestTargetIDsShowEveryMessageThatTrained`).
- Round 0 (`e1-document`, the experiment sample: 8,119 teacher messages
  with document vectors, 119 judge labels, 240 dev; method v1): mean dev
  accuracy **layer 1 0.763 vs legacy SubQ 0.827**; train 760 s for 17
  questions on the shared box; models 542 KB. Finding from it: the
  out-of-fold accuracy on the judge labels was far above dev (topic 0.71
  vs 0.58, stance 0.80 vs 0.68, request_count 0.70 vs 0.55) and λ sat on
  the grid's low edge — the held-out evaluation messages kept their own
  SubQ answer as a training target (the "fallback"), so the head
  repeated the teacher on exactly the messages it was scored on. Fixed
  (method v2): a held-out message has no target of any source in the
  fits that score it (the fallback is gone). Rounds before v2 are not
  compared with later ones.

Interruption (18:00): the session's process exited during the τ runs of
round E3 (`v3-sample-e3-knn-t02` was mid-run; its partial log removed;
nothing else half-written: the vector cache is complete — document
33,842 messages / 32,993 distinct inputs, classification and clustering
8,600 each —, reports and the ledger end on whole lines). The test gate
then failed once on a pre-existing flaky test
(`outlook.TestStateAndActionsDoNotWaitForAnOperation`: the test released
the blocked call before `Close` had marked the connector closed, so the
operation could finish first; 1 failure in 5 under load). Fixed in the
test (the call is released only once `Close` has begun), 30/30 green.

Lead directive (after the interruption): "1.0 accuracy" = every answer
given on its own is right; below the target the system abstains and
escalates (layer-0 key → layer 1 → SubQ → Gemma → the user). From now on
the primary objective is the coverage at ≥ 0.99 precision (mean over the
questions); mean accuracy is secondary. Every round reports, per
question and for the stack of layer-0 keys + layer 1, the coverage at
precision 0.95/0.98/0.99/1.00 on dev (point estimate and Wilson lower
bound), the same for legacy SubQ (its own probabilities as confidence),
and the errors at the 0.99 operating point by gold agreement (single,
double-agreed, adjudicated). `target_accuracy` defaults to 0.99; infer
marks an answer below its question's operating threshold as abstained.
Built for it: `layer1/selective.go` (`Rank`, `Targets`: coverage at
precision targets, point and Wilson, cut only between different
confidences; `Answered`), `Metrics.Points` and `Metrics.Threshold`,
`Model.Threshold` (certified out of fold at the question's target;
`NoThreshold` = abstain on everything), `engine.Answer.Abstain`
(`below_target`; values kept), `AnswerOf(q, probs, cutoff, threshold)`,
requirements `target_accuracy` 0.99, `report_targets` [0.95, 0.98, 0.99,
1.0], `request_labels` null = the labels that can certify the target
(381 at 0.99), `goldset.Agreement` (ids only, from the judges' second
batches and disagreement list), the harness's selective report
(`fixture_select_test.go`) and the paired bootstrap of the stack's
coverage at 0.99 next to the accuracy's. Earlier per-item run files
(v1–v3) hold correctness only and cannot be baselines of v4+.

**Stop rule met**: the last three rounds on the whole fixture (kNN
+0.44, T 2 −0.07, the score head +0.83) each improved the mean dev
accuracy by less than 1 pt (as did every round on the sample since v2),
and the primary metric (coverage at 0.99) moved within its noise in each.
The improvement loop stops; the final configuration (v5, the defaults
now shipped) is measured below.

- The ceiling (labeller agreement, WORDING-ISSUES.md; all labellers were
  Claude agents) bounds both: layer 1 reaches 88 % of it on average,
  SubQ 93 %.
- Requirement (target 0.99, coverage ≥ 0.5, Wilson-certified): **no

  point estimate, layer 1 alone reaches ≥ 0.99 on at least half of dev
  for suspicious (1.00, mostly the layer-0 keys), decision_needed (0.73),
  has_signature (0.66) and relationship (0.59); SubQ alone for
  suspicious, decision_needed, has_signature, sentiment, info_sufficiency,
  relationship, reply_needed, call_to_action and urgency. In the app
  every layer-1 answer abstains until ≥ 381 error-free evaluation labels
  per question certify a threshold (honest; the gate stays closed).
  [Corrected in review round L1: that understated it — the gate needs
  381 error-free certification labels on ≥ min_coverage of the
  certification part, 1,524 evaluation labels with the defaults.]
- At the 0.99 operating point (out-of-fold threshold) the 41 errors: 20
  on single-labelled gold (867 answered, 2.3 %), 17 on agreed items (428,
  4.0 %), 4 on adjudicated ones (5 answered).
- Costs: train 227–400 s for 17 questions on 33,581 rows (the box was
  shared: load 12–30); models 748 KB; answering one message with 17 heads
  58 µs (`BenchmarkInfer`); kNN would cost 6 ms per scan
  (`BenchmarkKNN`, 34,000 vectors).
- Cold start (no SubQ teacher; 119 judge labels and the measured rules):
  mean accuracy 0.673, coverage at 0.99 0.113; decision_needed cannot be
  trained (its 119 judge labels are all "no": `layer1_single_class`);

Gate: `scripts/test.sh` green (696 test and fuzz functions, 638 before; RACE off on this box: gofmt, the script
self-test, every vet tag incl. `embedlocal` of layer1, taxonomy check,
`go test ./...`); `scripts/build.sh` green (exe 16,650,240 bytes,
+472,704 for layer 1, optim, goldset).

Open issues and decisions for the lead:
- **Certification needs labels**: at target 0.99 no question can be
  certified with fewer than 381 error-free evaluation labels; the gold
  train split has 119 per question. Decide the judge's label budget per
  question (requirements `request_labels`), or a lower target for some
  questions (an override reflecting the wording's agreement ceiling,
  e.g. effort .83, topic .84).
- Layer 1 alone is a student of SubQ: −4.5 pt mean accuracy, about half
  of SubQ's coverage at 0.99. Its value is answering new mail for free
  where it is certified (suspicious, decision_needed, has_signature,
  relationship) and ranking what to escalate; the routing between layer
  1, SubQ and Gemma (the "calibration" stage) is not built.
- Classification/clustering prompts were measured on the sample only
  (v5: +0.61 and −0.81 pt, neither ≥ 1 pt with CI > 0): no second vector
  space, no migration 0012.
- kNN not adopted (no gain with the whole mailbox; 6 ms per scan): the
  shared-neighbour optimisation stays queued.
- The planning-round disclosure and the leftover judge files in the
  session scratchpad naming test ids (not read) remain for the lead.
- All labels and the dev split are French/English (agnosticism not
  validated on other languages; per-language rows above show English
  ahead of French for most questions, n = 38).
- The test split is untouched (sealed; `goldset.OpenTest` once, on the
  lead's call, with `GOLD_UNSEAL` = the frozen model's digest).

  Wilson-certified coverage is 0 at 0.99 and 1.00 for both (240 items

- Questions where layer 1 alone reaches ≥ 0.99 on a large dev share:
  suspicious 1.00 (119 dev items answered by the layer-0 keys), has_signature
  0.71, decision_needed 0.56; SubQ alone: suspicious 0.98, decision_needed
  0.86, has_signature 0.78, sentiment 0.69, info_sufficiency 0.61,
  relationship 0.60, reply_needed 0.55, call_to_action 0.51, urgency 0.50.
- The out-of-fold thresholds (119 judge labels) do not transfer at 0.99:

  answers, 57 wrong). The certified thresholds answer nothing (they need
  ≥ 381 error-free labels), which is what the app does now (it abstains).
- The 57 errors at that operating point: 32 on single-labelled gold (883
  answered, 3.6 %), 23 on items two labellers agreed on (422, 5.5 %), 2 on
  adjudicated ones (5, 40 %): the errors are mostly on clear items, not on
  ambiguous ones.
- Queued experiment "quoted tail by parent match" measured first
  (`threads.TestFixtureQuotedTails`): 30 fixture messages, 0 dev messages
  would change; matching trailing lines against the parent in general
  would cut the sender's own signature in 51 % of replies. Deprioritised

## 2026-10-15 — Review of the Outlook crash-safety round (review 3) and the lead's decisions

A read-only review of the crash-safety round found 11 numbered findings
and 10 lower ones. Each was reproduced by a committed test that failed on
the code before this round (run on the old behaviour; "new API" = the
test needs an API that did not exist, the reviewer's repro stands).
Nothing was run on the Windows machine.

| # | Finding | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 2026-10-15 — Outlook safety after two crashes; lead decisions on the layer-0 round

Incident: OUTLOOK.EXE crashed twice on the target (Application log event
1000, `ntdll.dll`, `0xc0000374` heap corruption) during back-to-back
reruns of `scripts/evidence-live.sh`. The investigation found no memory
bug in the connector's COM code; the most likely cause is our unthrottled
load (≈1,250 calls/s on Outlook's UI thread, with Google Workspace Sync,
Teams and Lync add-ins loaded), made worse by the reconnect logic and the
harness. Nothing was run on the Windows machine in this round.

Part A — Outlook safety (`docs/OUTLOOK_SYNC.md`, "Load and crash safety"):

| # | Change | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Pace at the one call choke point (`guard.invoke`, `pace.go`): share of wall time inside Outlook and calls per second, a slower pair while the user is active (`GetLastInputInfo`, 32-bit tick wrap handled; unreadable ⇒ active), `Stats.Pace`. The detail pass's `sync.details.pause` (20 ms per 50 items: paced nothing) removed | `TestPaceNextKeepsShareAndRate`, `TestPaceHoldsTheBusyShare` (0.5/0.25/0.1 within 5 %), `TestPaceHoldsTheCallRate`, `TestPaceSlowsDownWhileTheUserIsActive`, `TestPaceIsReducedAfterALoss`, `TestPaceWaitEndsWithTheContext`, `TestIdleSinceWraps`, `TestDetailsPassCompletesNewestFirstInBatches` (no sleep of its own) |
| A2 | Breaker in `Connector.op` (`breaker.go`): cooldown × growth per loss (capped), then Outlook's process up ≥ min uptime (Toolhelp + `GetProcessTimes`, never Outlook itself), pace × resume factor per loss in the window, stop after K losses until `Connector.Resume`; states disclosed (`Breaker`, `Health.Breaker`, topic `outlook.breaker`, actions `resume_source`/`start_source`). Lost-connection set researched (Microsoft Learn COM/RPC codes): + `RPC_E_CONNECTION_TERMINATED`, `RPC_E_SERVER_DIED(_DNE)`, `RPC_S_CALL_FAILED_DNE`, `CO_E_SERVER_STOPPING`, `RPC_E_SERVERFAULT` (Outlook raised an exception: stop calling it too); busy + `RPC_E_SERVERCALL_REJECTED`, `RPC_S_SERVER_TOO_BUSY`. Attach only: `Launch`/`Logon` removed, `StartOutlook` (shell `outlook.exe`, its window) is the user's action | `TestBreakerCooldownUptimeAndStop` (5 → 10 min, warming until 15 min uptime, factor 0.5 → 0.25, stopped at 3, no COM call while open, events), `TestBreakerWindowForgetsOldLosses`, `TestBreakerAfterCooldownNeedsARunningOutlook`, `TestCooldownGrowthIsCapped`, `TestBackgroundWorkNeverStartsOutlook`, `TestStartOutlookMisuse`, `TestErrorClassification` (every code) |
| A3 | `source.ErrUnavailable` (`source.Unavailable`): `ErrSessionLost`, `ErrNotRunning` and the breaker's refusals wrap it; `syncFolders` and the detail pass end the run on it (no next folder, no details, no removals) | `TestUnavailableSourceEndsTheRun` (a plain folder error still lets the others sync), `TestUnavailableSourceStopsTheDetailPass`, `source.TestUnavailableMatchesThroughWrapping` |
| A4 | Mail received less than `sync.details.settle_after` ago waits for a later run (one predicate of the pending queries, `store.pendingSQL`); `sync.details.max_per_run` caps a run's detail reads (`DetailReport.Capped`) | `TestDetailsPassDefersUnsettledMessages`, `TestDetailsPassIsCappedPerRun`, `store.TestPendingDetailsNewestFirstAndApply` |
| A5 | Harness: `scripts/relay/outlook-guard.sh` before (Outlook running and up ≥ `OUTLOOK_MIN_UPTIME`, 900 s) and after every live run (same PID and start time, no event 1000/1001 naming OUTLOOK.EXE since the start, else `OUTLOOK CRASHED`, exit 3; a failed check is a warning and a failure); never reruns; `outlook-live.sh` captures `_test.go:` lines; both scripts default to a short verification run (`LIVE_DETAILS=1000`, `LIVE_RATE=100`: `livetest.Limit` → `-live.details`, `-live.rate`) | `selftest.sh` (probe parsing, CRLF, none running, unsafe instant refused); `go vet` of both live tags |

`outlook.pace.calls_per_second` 200, `outlook.pace.active.busy_share`
0.05, `outlook.pace.active.calls_per_second` 20, `outlook.pace.idle_after`

`outlook.breaker.cooldown_max` 2h, `outlook.breaker.min_uptime` 15m,
`outlook.breaker.window` 24h, `outlook.breaker.max_losses` 3,
`outlook.breaker.resume_factor` 0.5, `sync.details.max_per_run` 0 (no
cap), `sync.details.settle_after` 5m; constraints active ≤ away pace,
cooldown ≤ cooldown_max. Zero, negative and out-of-range values are
refused by the schema (`TestPaceAndBreakerSettingsRejectMisuse`).

still naming them is refused as an unknown setting; nothing shipped).
At the defaults a detail read runs at ≤ 20 items/s (user away), ≤ 2 while
the user works: the target's primary store (34.6k items) ≈30 min instead
of 3.4 min (reasoned from the measured costs, not measured).

Part B — the lead's decisions:

1. **Triage reads the causal view only.** `triage.causal_threads` and the
   filed-view history (`threads.Analysis.History`, MyReplies-based) are
   removed; `KnownHistory` is the one history (`TestFilingNeverChangesAnotherState`
   replaces the on/off test; `TestFixtureCausalThreadsImpact` removed:
   it measured a switch that no longer exists — 41 of 33,581 fixture
   states changed). `TestStateIsPinned` keeps `22af6e01a787c139` (its
   composer has an empty history). `threads.folder_roles` is still read
   by the install-profile learners (shared domains, reply prefixes), so
   it stays, its description narrowed to them (decision below).
2. **Year-less numeric dates.** A year-less all-numeric form is a
   resolved date only if no pattern of the language (any region) writes
   numeric dates in the other day/month order (`locale.disputeOrders`,
   from the data; year-first ISO patterns claim no order; patterns whose
   literals name the fields, "M月d日", are not all-numeric); otherwise
   `ambiguous_order`. Disputed in 10 shipped languages (ak, en, es, fr,
   ha, kn, qu, so, ti, zh-Hant). Fixture: messages with a resolved full
   date 3,157 → 3,104, with an unresolved one 46 → 124
   (`date_next_days` `ambiguous_order` 33 → 86); rules: `deadline_any`
   17/55 → 17/54, `deadline_none` 209/259 → 210/260. Tests:
   `locale.TestYearlessNumericDatesNeedAgreeingRegions` (failed first),
   `TestDatesInEveryShape` (fr "03/11" is now disputed: fr_CA writes
   MM-dd).
3. **`deadline_same_day`.** The masked structure of its 38 train+dev
   hits (letters and digits masked, no text kept): 28 were an attribution
   line ("<date>, <name> <address> … :") before a quote that Outlook's
   plain-text Body indents with a TAB (its rendering of a quoted HTML
   block — Gmail, Apple Mail), not with ">", often with the attribution
   indented too; `mail.CleanBody` only knew ">" quotes. Research (talon,
   email_reply_parser and forks, quotequail, Carvalho & Cohen 2004): every
   library's attribution detection is a keyword list per language except
   talon's structural splitters ("a date and an address on a line ending
   in a colon"). Fix at the lowest choke point, `mail.CleanBody`: an
   attribution line — at most `intro_max_runes`, ending in a colon (full
   width too), naming an address, holding a digit — followed by a quoted
   or tab-indented line is a reply boundary (`clean.json` `rules_version`
   2, so every view of the cleaned text is recomputed). Over the whole
   fixture it cuts 1,577 more messages (1,526 before a tab-indented line,
   51 before ">"), none left without text of its own. Re-measured
   (train 119 + dev 240 via the shared gold loader; the test split never
   read): `deadline_same_day` 2/38 → **0/10** — the rest are dates in the
   mail's own content (notifications, receipts) — so the rule is
   **dropped**. Tests: `mail.TestCleanBodyCutsAttributionsBeforeIndentedQuotes`
   (fr, en, ja full-width colon, ar, es; five look-alikes kept) and
   `evidence.TestTheQuotedAttributionIsNoDateOfTheMessage`, both failed
   first.

- coverage: messages with a resolved full date 3,157 → **1,842**, with an

- rules (train + dev): the same **2 keys** (`not_susp_known_pass` 179/179,

  `deadline_any` 17/55 → **13/24** (precision 0.31 → 0.54),

## 2026-10-15 — Review round layer 0 (evidence engine: bugs + rules reviews)

Every finding of both reviews, confirmed and plausible, was reproduced
with a test committed here ("failed first" = it failed on the code
before this round, run on a copy of it; "new" = a new API, the reviewer's
repro on the old code stands). No plausible finding failed to reproduce.

| # | Finding | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 / R3 | The owner's later filing (Deleted Items, Junk) changed the causal history of other messages | the **causal view** in `threads` (`CausalRoles`: owner-scope mail of every folder but drafts, wherever it is filed now), read by evidence; `threads.folder_roles` is no input of evidence any more | `TestOwnerFilingNeverChangesCausalHistory` (failed first: 6 signals of a2 changed) |
| B2 / R2 | A later message bridging two conversations changed earlier messages' thread values and reply pairing | `threads.Analyze` grows conversations in time order (union-find with member snapshots): `Analysis.EarlierMembers`, replies paired at their own instant (`KnownReplies`, `KnownHistory`); `Threads`/`MyReplies` stay the final, retrospective view | `TestALaterBridgeNeverChangesEarlierThreads` (failed first), `threads.TestConversationsGrowInTimeOrder` (new) |
| B3 / R1 | Message-only values reused after a new verdict, owner or organisation | a per-message **context digest** (verdict, reason, the store's owner, the source's capabilities, the owners' organisations) stored with the revision (migration 0009); reuse needs both; the verdict's reason joins `store.EvidenceInputs` | `TestARejudgedMessageIsComputedAgain` (failed first: stage done, computed 0) |
| B4 / R1 | New source capabilities never picked up | capabilities in the context digest and in the inputs fingerprint; `UpsertSource` moves the store generation when they change | `TestANewCapabilityIsPickedUp` (failed first) |
| B5 | Partial messages (details pending) got complete-looking zeros | `Signal.Summary`; every other signal is unavailable `details_pending` while `Partial`; the stage waits ("waits for the details of N messages") | `TestPendingDetailsAreNotValues` (failed first: zeros, stage done) |
| B6 | A header block cut mid-line read as complete | `mail.ParseCutHeaders` drops the last logical line of a cut block (evidence `Input.Header`); the RFC 5322 connector reads labels and Status from the whole header block | `TestTheCutLineOfAHeaderBlockIsNotRead`, `rfc5322.TestLabelsAreReadFromTheWholeHeaderBlock` (both failed first) |
| B7 / R5 | A trigger during a run was lost | `jobs.Single` (one run of a kind at a time; a run wanted meanwhile follows it, requests coalesce), used by the evidence and the index triggers | `jobs.TestSingleNeverLosesARequest`, `TestSingleUnderConcurrency`, `evidence.TestATriggerDuringARunIsNotLost`, `index.TestASyncDuringARunIsNotLost` (new) |

Triage and the causal view (lead decision 1). The triage cache re-asks
whenever a state's hash differs from the stored decision's
(`Plan.Invalidated` → decided again, billed), so moving triage to the
causal view would re-bill every changed state. Measured on the fixture
(`triage.TestFixtureCausalThreadsImpact`): **41 of 33,581 states (0.12 %)
change** — all from reply pairing, since the export holds no deleted or
junk mail; the live mailbox (Deleted Items, Junk) would change more.
Triage is unchanged by default: the causal view is implemented once in
`threads` and available as `triage.causal_threads` (off). **Decision
needed:** flip the default and how to keep paid answers (a one-time
re-keying of stored decisions to their new state hash when only the view
changed, or accept the re-decision cost the plan shows).

## 2026-10-15 — Review round L0 (bugs + rules reviews)

Rule chosen for the gate after an unpick (priority 1): a non-empty
STRICT SUBSET of the last fully learned selection stays learned (open);
any store added to the selection closes the gate until the new selection
is learned as a whole; the latch is replaced by each newly learned
selection. Unpicking takes the store's mail out of search, vectors,
scope, triage and the learners at once (it is kept for a re-pick).

"Failed first" = the regression test, run on the unfixed code (the
reviewer's copy), failed; "(here)" = observed failing in this tree with
the old rule restored; "new" = the test exercises a new action or API.

| # | Finding | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| perf | FTS insert followed by the next UPSERT → statement journal → FTS5 one-message segments + merges (26 % CPU) | `store/writer.go`: every statement prepared once per transaction, full-text entries written after the batch's other writes (repoA ported); headers parsed once (`mail.ParseHeaders`); Fold 3.3× faster (ASCII and lone precomposed characters skip the normalizer; an immutable BMP table replaces the mutable cache) | fixture counts unchanged; `mail.BenchmarkFold` 58 → 195 MB/s |
| 1 | Offline/partly read picked store erased identity and verdicts; wrong error | `source.Mailbox.IdentityComplete`; Outlook records every failed identity read (`ownerRead`; an absent property is no failure); the syncer saves a reported identity only from a complete read of an online store (`Report.Waiting`, `IdentityKept`), `ErrMailboxUnreadable` instead of `ErrNothingPicked` | `syncer.TestAnOfflineOrPartlyReadStoreKeepsItsIdentityAndVerdicts` (failed first: identities [], verdicts {"":5}, ErrNothingPicked), `outlook.TestAnIdentityReadInPartKeepsTheRecordedOne` (new) |

Found during this round:
- The new CleanBody panicked on a quoted line ending in ":" inside the
  bottom quote (the fixture run caught it). `mail.TestCleanBodyQuotedIntroInsideTheQuote` (failed first (here)).
- The auto choice was stamped before its probes ran (seen in the live
  report). Stamped after; asserted in `TestAutoPicksAFasterGPUAndRemembersIt`.
- Linux can refuse to open an executable for writing for a moment after
  its process exits (`ETXTBSY`): a test artifact; the tamper test replaces
  the file by rename.
- The tuning test was timing-sensitive under `-race` (1 vs 4 ms per input):
  the fake's speed gap is now 1 vs 26 ms (3 green `-race` runs in a row).

Median/percentile: `mathx.Median` (average of the two middles) is the one
median, also in the causal history's bucket median; `mathx.Rank`
(half-even, legacy's p90 exactly) the one rank, `Percentile` uses it
(2a's half-up picked the next value when q·(n−1) ends in .5; the test
was changed). The urgency prior is legacy's again: median at 0.1 minute,
`≤` each bound (`rules.json` `resolution_minutes`). On the fixture
(`threads.TestFixtureMedians`, 16,237 sender standings): the history's
median bucket equals a brute-force median for all of them; against 2a's
rule **778 urgency priors** (dormant: weight 0) and **1,001 speed bands**
change — so those triage states change and are decided again on the
next run (the plan's `invalidated` shows it).

Rules review, by section:
- §1: os.Root unpack; job handle once; one key per manager (redaction
  list no longer grows); failing GPU builds persisted (auto); one verify
  per launch with a stamp cache; removals/renames through fsx
  (`fsx.Remove`, `Promote`, `WriteJSON`) — reads stay `os.Open`/`ReadFile`
  (sharing violations hit deletes and renames, not shared reads);
  `Content-Range` start checked (`TestARangeAnswerFromElsewhereRestartsThePart`).
- §2: per-slot context declared once in the runtime catalog
  (`slots`, `slot_context`, `{context}`); `sidecar.variant` a string
  checked against the catalog at start; `VariantCPU`/`VariantAuto` and
  placeholder constants; `{host}`; allowlist instead of the `LLAMA_`
  prefix; `embed.dimensions` 0 = native; model URL pinned to commit

### Findings (new)

1. Example provider bills this account by energy: the reported charge was 17% of
   the list token price on real states (summed over 230 calls), so
   the plan (list price) overestimates its cost ≈6×; the guard stays safe.
2. Clef-flash answers in one call but is ≈3× slower per call; per message
   SubQ's two calls are still faster (588 vs 946 ms p50).
3. Clef-flash is not bit-deterministic (mean |Δ| ≤ 0.006, one score level
   flip in 510 answers); SubQ repeated identically again (510/510).
4. Both rank the weak reply label alike (AUC ≈ 0.70); Clef-flash is better
   calibrated (Brier 0.278 vs 0.313); both under-call replies (recall
   0.39 / 0.32 at the 0.5 cutoff). Weak labels are noisy: gold labels decide.
5. The two models disagree most on the multi-option and timing questions
   (category, relationship, deadline, urgency): the gold judge is needed
   before switching.

### Open

- Gold labels pending (independent judge); then `bench-deciders.sh score`.
- No language detector: no French/English split.

Leftovers of review 2a:

| # | Item | Outcome | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | Budget guard overshoot by in-flight calls | Per-call reservation: the adapter reserves each call's ceiling (`reserve_tokens_per_byte` × request bytes, provider data) with the run's `engine.Reserver` before sending it and settles the usage after; no serialization. A call billed past its ceiling is counted (`Report.Overruns`) | `TestBudgetNeverOvershootsWithParallelWorkers` (4 workers in flight: $0.40 ≤ $0.50; with the old rule, reservation = estimate, it spent $0.80), `TestCallsBilledPastTheirCeilingAreCounted`, `decision.TestEveryCallIsReservedBeforeItIsSent`; `TestBudgetStopsMidRun` now stops at $0.40 (was $0.80) |
| b | Urgency-prior bounds `<` vs legacy `≤` | Kept `<` (one bucket rule with the speed bands), justified by evidence: replaying both rules causally over the fixture (legacy matcher, 16,278 inbox messages with a sender prior), the bound change alters **0** priors (no median falls in the 0.05-minute window legacy rounding creates); the median-low of an even sample (legacy: mean of the two middles) alters **811 (5.0 %)**, a second deviation the reviews had not listed. Both are dormant by default (`prior_blend.urgency` = 0) | `TestUrgencyPriorBoundsAreExclusive` (pins 119.99 → 3.25, 120 → 2.5, …) |

Bugs found by measuring (each with a regression test):
1. **Inputs over the server's context.** A characters-per-token budget
   cannot bound tokens: 2,560 characters of one fixture mail made 2,089
   tokens, over the 2,048-token slot (HTTP 500). Inputs are now capped at
   `context_tokens − reserved_tokens` UTF-8 bytes (a byte-fallback
   tokenizer never makes more tokens than bytes).
   `embed.TestInputNeverExceedsTheServerContextInBytes` (failed first).
2. **One bad input kept its batch out, every run.** The 7 neighbours of
   that mail were never indexed. A failed batch is now embedded message by
   message. `index.TestOneBadInputNeverKeepsItsBatchOut` (failed first).
3. **Same-second rewrites were invisible.** `messages.updated_at` has
   one-second precision, so a read-flag change in the second of indexing
   was never re-checked. Every write now increments `messages.revision`.
   `index.TestOnlyChangedTextIsEmbeddedAgain` (failed first on updated_at).
4. **Live test:** the job-object helper was started through the relative
   `os.Args[0]`, which `os/exec` refuses (`ErrDot`), and the test passed
   anyway. It uses `os.Executable()` and fails on a failed check.

## 2026-10-14 — Review round 2a (bugs + rules reviews)

Design (bugs 1, 4, 5 fixed once, at the composer): a triage state is
CAUSAL. Standings, reply examples and label examples come only from data
dated strictly before the message's own instant (`mail.Instant`: sent_on
for sent items), bucketed, excluding the message; the arrival fact is UTC.
`threads.History` answers standings at any instant from per-correspondent
timelines with per-bucket prefix counts (O(log n) a query). The pinned
snapshot and its hysteresis are gone. Priors are causal too.

"Failed first" = the reviewer's repro (ported as the named test) failed on
the unfixed code.

| # | Finding | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | One label changed 39/40 (19/60) states | Labels inform only later mail of the same sender/domain (`Label.Before`); subject overlap only orders within that group | `TestALabelNeverChangesExistingStates`, `feedback.TestSelectExamplesIsCausalAndLocal` (failed first) |
| 2 | Concurrent runs billed twice | In-process `TryLock` + store lease (`leases`, `triage.lease_ttl`, renewed per message); `Start`/`Run` → `ErrTriageBusy` before any job | `TestOneRunAtATime` (failed first: 12 calls), `store.TestLeasesAndGeneration` |
| 3 | Chunk-2 failure discarded paid chunk 1 | `Decide` returns earlier chunks' answers; triage stores partial answers and asks only the missing questions (`Plan.Partial`, `Result.Missing`) | `decision.TestFailedLaterChunkKeepsEarlierAnswers`, `TestPartialAnswersAreKeptAndCompleted` (failed first) |
| 4 | State and reply prior saw the message's own outcome | Causal composer and priors | `TestARepliesNeverChangeExistingStates` (failed first), `TestReadBlendsPriorsAndFlagsLowConfidence` (prior 1.0, was 0.8 with itself counted) |
| 5 | Volume band and time.zone changed states | Causal standings; arrival in UTC; `Plan.Invalidated` counts cached states a change invalidates | `TestNewMailNeverChangesExistingStates`, `TestTimeZoneNeverChangesStates` (both failed first) |
| 6 | Global `http.retry.statuses` could make 500 retryable | Schema `not_in` (new rule kind) + `Policy.Never`, not adjustable by overrides; providers validate against the same list | `httpx.TestNeverRetriedStatusesCannotBeConfiguredRetryable` (failed first), `config.TestNotInRule` |
| 7 | Two roles on one question; `RoleOf` map order | Rejected in validation; fixed question→role map | `taxonomy.TestAQuestionPlaysOneRole` (failed first) |
| 8 | Possibly billed failures counted $0; null price disabled the USD guard | `httpx.ErrAfterWrite` and non-declined 5xx accounted at the estimate (`UsageRecord.Estimated`); unpriced plans refused unless `triage.budget.allow_unpriced` | `decision.TestPossiblyBilledFailuresAreAccountedAtTheEstimate`, `TestUnpricedProviderIsRefusedUnlessAllowed` (both failed first) |
| 9 | Inconsistent probabilities accepted | Verified first: provider.example.test ("a probability for every option", score "probability-weighted") and all 335,870 legacy SubQ answers (sum 1.00, argmax, expected level, no exception). Complete sets, sum, argmax and expected level enforced within `probability_tolerance` (0.02, data) | `decision.TestInconsistentProbabilitiesAreRejected` (failed first), live run: 10/10 real answers pass |
| 10 | Malformed header blocks lost parents | Line-based, case-insensitive extraction after unfolding; bare ids bracketed | `mail.TestThreadIDsSurviveMalformedHeaderBlocks` (failed first); fixture: the 65 left are all cut by the export's 4,000-character header cap (unrecoverable; Outlook reads full headers) |

Escalation (tuning): the flag is role-aware profile data
(`mailsense_profile.json`, `taxonomy.Profile.Uncertain`): category
confidence < 0.40, urgency < 0.25, reply and suspicious within 0.10 of 0.5.
Calibrated without spend on the 33,587 legacy SubQ classifications (same
model): the old rule (any answer under 0.5 confidence) flagged 87.9%
(26/30 live); these thresholds (≈ each role's 5th–10th percentile) flag
19.9%, the least certain fifth, on the roles the owner sees first. Live
check: 2/10. `feedback.CalibrateEscalation` suggests per-role thresholds
from labels (`feedback.calibration.escalation_accuracy`).

Rules review:
- §1:
  - Decider built per run (`Engines`), so `triage.decider` and the providers file apply without restart.
  - Noul cutoffs from the profile (`Cutoff`, `RoleCutoffs`, new `noul_default`).
  - Suspicious categories, known relationships and `sentiment_positive_min` moved into the profile (two settings removed) and validated against the role questions.
  - Typed roles and thresholds; never-retry list and attempt bounds read from the schema.
  - DECISION_PROVIDERS drift fixed (it now points at providers.json).
  - Folder-role pattern tested against `mail.Roles()`; tests read settings through `SettingsFrom`; the live budget lives in the script only.
- §2:
  - `jsonx.Int` is the one integer rule (config, taxonomy, usage).
  - `jsonx.DecodeStrict` for schema, providers and rules.
  - `fsx.ReadOptional`, `digest.Hex`.
  - `engine.Question.Validate` is the one question check.
  - Monthly volume from the behaviour profile.
  - One reply matcher; `Estimate.Add/Sub`; `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys)`, `math.Abs`, `round3`.
  - Parsed template kept on the profile; `kv_get` shared by the scripts.
- §3: billing (above); single flight (above); `Decider.Plan` returns an error (`Plan.Unsendable`); package-level loggers; `threads.Analyze` is pure.
- §4:
  - The clock is used (lease) and the default profile is decoded once.
  - Explicit context keys; no duplicate worker minimum.
  - The generated taxonomy drops the legacy `_doc` (it described a CLI flag); everything else is byte for byte, and the fingerprint stays `9c9956169b0c`.
- §5:
  - `Options.Stores`, `Triager.Result(rowID)`, never-decided failures in `Read`.
  - `Engines.TestProvider` and `Status`, with `engine.provider` health events (`engine.Monitor`).
  - `feedback.Labeler` Put/Delete with `feedback.label` events.
  - `Triager.Analytics` assembles evaluation (weak reply labels), calibration, correlations, insights and volume.
  - `triage.rules.file` overrides the bands and wording.
  - The snapshot-pinned event is moot: there is no snapshot.
- §6:
  - New tests: mid-run budget stop, 16 MiB cap, corrupt cached answers, concurrent runs, unavailable provider with 4 workers, over-context plan.
  - `test.sh` says when the taxonomy check is skipped; the committed data is the reference.

Not changed, with reasons:
- The in-run budget guard counts in-flight calls at their estimate. If real costs run above the estimates, it can overshoot by at most the calls in flight (`TestBudgetStopsMidRun`). Waiting for each call before dispatching the next would serialize the workers.
- The urgency prior is banded on the causal history (median-low bucket), so its bounds are now exclusive (`< 120 min`) where legacy used `≤`.
- The triage cache keys on the store's in-process `Generation`. Another process writing the same database is not seen. The lease keeps triage single-run, and the app is the only writer.

Evidence:
- `scripts/test.sh` green: 311 test functions (was 281) plus the fuzz target, under `-race`.
- `scripts/build.sh` green.
- Fixture unchanged: 33,842 messages, 33,587 / 146 / 109.
- Fingerprint `9c9956169b0c`.
- Live: `triage-live.sh 10 3` cost 27 calls, 43,756 + 101 tokens, ≈ $0.003. All answers passed the stricter decoder; repeat-agreement was 51/51.

## 2026-10-14 — Phase 2a: engines, decision adapter, triage, threads, feedback

Built:
- `internal/engine`: kinds (decider; embedder and generator accepted as
  catalog data for 2b/3), the typed `Question`/`Answer` contract,
  `Decider` (`Plan` + `Decide`), `Usage`/`Estimate`, `engine.usage` topic +
  `UsageSink` (the store: `engine_usage` counters per day/provider/model),
  providers as data (`providers.json` presets for SubQ, Jev, Clef,
  Clef-flash, OpenAI Decisions with live/docs status, prices and notes;
  `engine.providers.file` merges per provider and per field, null removes,
  every problem reported), `Registry` (dialect → adapter, explicit
  registration), `ErrUnavailable`.
- `internal/engine/decision`: one adapter, codecs `systemone` (Cloudflare
  `result` envelope, `detail` object/array/string errors) and
  `openai_decisions` (array questions/answers, predicate ↔ noul with the
  provider's `noul_fold`, choices/levels arrays, legend rebuilt from the
  labels sent, refusals). Chunking at `max_questions` (answers merged,
  usage summed), the context budget checked for every chunk before the
  first call, strict decoding (missing, extra or mistyped answers, bools,
  strings, out-of-range numbers are `ErrContract`), error classes (402
  credits, 401/403 auth, quota codes, 400/404/422 rejected), per-provider
  retry overrides through `httpx.WithPolicy` (new; `Policy.Final` makes a
  quota 429 final by its body; 400/401/402/403/404/422/500 can never be
  configured retryable).
- `internal/triage/taxonomy`: the legacy taxonomy as embedded data,
  generated by `scripts/gen-taxonomy.sh` (`--check` runs in `test.sh`);
  fingerprint `9c9956169b0c` reproduced byte for byte (`jsonx.PyDumps`);
  overrides per key with null removing; PORTING §5 validation plus unknown
  keys (top level, question, context), deterministic order; labels parsed.
- `internal/threads`: header-first threading (Message-ID links, read from
  the transport headers when the fields are empty: 3,269 fixture inbox
  items carry In-Reply-To there), then ConversationID / ConversationIndex
  header, then the subject only without other evidence and never when

### Findings (new)

1. SubQ answered identically on a second call for all 170 answers; the
   docs' "outputs can vary" was not observed (small sample). Caching and
   evaluation still assume nothing.
2. With the legacy `low_confidence` 0.5, 26 of 30 results carry the
   escalation flag (choice/score confidences are often below 0.5): the
   flag is too broad to drive the Generator; calibrate it first.
3. `chars_per_token` 3 overestimates SubQ tokens by ≈30% (3.9 measured):
   plans err on the safe side.
4. Legacy leaks beyond PORTING §8: a message's own reply excerpt and its
   own label could appear in its own state. Both are excluded now.
5. The legacy caps regex `\b[A-ZÀ-Þ]{3,}\b` includes `×` (not a word
   character): "ABC×DEF" is one match. Ported exactly.
6. Python's banker's `round()` chose p90 index 4 of 6 values; half-up
   picks 5. Score groups round half-up (2.5 → level 3; legacy floored).
7. The threshold sweep drifted (12 × 0.05 = 0.6000000000000001), so 0.6
   could be skipped; steps are rounded now (legacy accumulated the same).
8. `jsonx.DecodeOne` accepted `{} }`: `Decoder.More` is false before a
   stray closing bracket. Fixed for both decoders (regression test).
9. A message removed between plan and dispatch made its failure record hit
   the foreign key and abort the run; it is skipped now (regression test,
   failed first).

### Open

- Few-shot label selection keeps the legacy score (> 0 on any shared
  subject token), so one new label can change many states and re-bill
  them; the plan shows it, the budget bounds it. A minimum score would
  make labels as cheap as behaviour (needs a decision).
- Embedder (2b, done) and Generator (3) are catalog kinds without adapters.
- The snapshot is pinned on every plan/read (derived data, a version only
  when a standing changed); nothing prunes old versions yet.
- No full-archive triage was run (needs explicit approval).

## 2026-10-14 — Phase 1b: Outlook connector, live on <agent>

Built:
- `internal/source/outlook`: classic Outlook over COM (`OUTLOOK_SYNC.md`, "As
  built"). One STA thread. A read-only guard admits only the members in
  `model.go` (no Save/Delete/Move/Send/put exist), retries busy calls with
  the `outlook.com.retry.*` backoff, caches DISPIDs per class and counts and
  times every member. The package has its own `IDispatch::Invoke`, because
  go-ole's leaks a BSTR per string-array element. It reads 2-D SAFEARRAYs
  (layout checked on every row) and builds the `VARIANT(BSTR)` array for
  `GetProperties`. Preconditions are named errors: elevated, classic Outlook
  missing, new Outlook, integrity mismatch, not running/cannot start,
  session lost, store offline. Discover covers every store and mail folder:
  roles by `GetDefaultFolder` identity, owner by `PR_MAILBOX_OWNER_ENTRYID`
  (primary: CurrentUser), one `GetProperties` per folder. Sync diffs a
  snapshot, then one sorted table pass streams the changed rows as partial
  messages. `ReadDetails` reads body, headers, References and recipients
  through the SMTP chain with a DN cache.
- Contract changes: `source.Sink.Snapshot` (id/stamp diff, end-of-run
  removals classified as moves vs deletes), `source.DetailReader` +
  `ItemError`, `mail.Message.Partial`, `mail.Details`, `ChangeStamp`,
  `UTF16Len/TruncateUTF16` (the archive reuses it), `mail.Folder.StoreKind`
  and `StoreOwner`. `store`: partial writes keep stored details,
  `PendingDetails`/`ApplyDetails`/`FolderVersions`/`RemoveAbsent`, and
  identities keyed by store (migration 0001 edited: unreleased).
- `syncer`: snapshot diffs, removals after all folders, a detail pass newest
  first (`sync.details.batch_size`, `sync.details.pause`), and per-store scope
  (open item of 1a closed). A failing folder no longer aborts the run; only
  output failures and cancellation do.
- Scope per store: the user's mailbox uses `scope.owner_address`, else the
  reported owner, else Sent discovery. Every other mailbox uses its reported
  owner, else its own Sent minus the user's addresses. The user's identity
  is never learned from a delegate, and the user is never made one's owner.
  The fixture result is unchanged: 33,587 / 146 / 109.
- 11 settings (`outlook.*`, `sync.details.*`), all read (`TestEverySettingIsUsed`).
- User decisions (2026-10-14): by default only the primary store
  (`Namespace.DefaultStore`, key `primary`) syncs. Every other store is
  discovered and listed (`Connector.Stores()`, `outlook.stores` topic: key,
  kind, cached/online, folder and item counts), and syncs once its key is
  in `outlook.stores.enabled`. Keys hash the StoreID, never the localized
  display name. Phase-2 triage is also primary-only by default, as a list of
  the same keys (nothing added before its consumer exists). This replaced
  `outlook.stores.kinds` and `outlook.stores.exclude_names`. Cross-store
  parallelism is not adopted (one STA in Outlook; reasoned, not measured).
- Tooling: `scripts/relay/` is bash + curl + jq, parameterised by agent, and
  the token goes to curl on stdin. It covers exec, ps, upload, download
  (SHA-256 checked), deploy, detach, poll, logs, cleanup and 9 read-only
  probes. `detach.sh` uses WMI `Win32_Process.Create`: measured, the relay
  waits for every process in its own tree (even `start /b`), while a WMI
  process returns at once and runs in session 1 next to Outlook. No
  scheduled task is used. `scripts/outlook-live.sh <agent> smoke|full` wraps
  build, deploy, run, report and cleanup.
- Live test: `go test -c -tags outlooklive` (windows), not a `cmd/`. It
  reuses unexported internals without exporting them, and a test binary
  cannot ship in the app exe.

Evidence:
- `scripts/test.sh` green: gofmt, vet ×4 (host, windows, windows+outlooklive,

- Live run 2 (all stores, with the fixes):
  - 100,720 items in 2 h 21 min: 0 detail failures, 0 pending, 0 folder

    scratch directory is empty afterwards and no exe is kept.

### Findings (new)

1. Outlook tables refuse `PidTagLocalCommitTime` (E_FAIL fails the whole
   `GetArray`). It is now read per item, and it is empty on this whole
   profile, as in the legacy export.
2. Read/unread flips do not move `PR_LAST_MODIFICATION_TIME`. Change
   detection now uses `PR_CONTENT_UNREAD` plus the read state in the stamp.
3. 2.2 % of items have no `Recipients` member (non-mail classes). A missing
   member reads as empty.
4. On this profile `PR_LOCAL_COMMIT_TIME_MAX` exists on 1 of 29 primary
   folders but on every folder of the online archive. Elsewhere the newest
   modification time stands in: one sorted 1-row table, 20 folders, 0
   refusals. A schema name as the sort key is refused (E_INVALIDARG); the
   built-in `[LastModificationTime]` works.
5. Online mailboxes dominate the cost: 23 ms per COM call against the online
   archive and 114 ms per item for details, against 0.3 s and 15 ms on the
   cached primary. Incremental cost is mostly Discover's walk of one online
   store (23 of 35 s).
6. `GetArray` = rows × columns as PowerShell shows it. The Go reader's
   column-major assumption held on every one of the 1,262 pages.
7. Every recipient but 85 of 150,538 carried `PR_SMTP_ADDRESS` on the row:
   the address book is nearly never needed.
8. PowerShell `foreach`/`Item(i)` folder walks cost 3–7× a `GetFirst/GetNext`
   walk.

### Open

- Incremental cost with all stores enabled: Discover walks every enabled
  folder each run (35 s, mostly the online archive). With the primary-only
  default it is the primary walk (≈0.3 s). Walking the hierarchy less often
  than folder states are read remains an option if users enable archives.
- With delegates enabled, the first detail pass over online mailboxes takes
  about 2 h (server latency). It runs in the background, newest first, and
  resumes where it stopped.
- One subject sits at exactly 255 characters. Table strings may be capped,
  and the detail pass does not re-read Subject yet.
- No message pump or Outlook events yet (`LiveEvents` false); a timer-driven
  incremental sync is the phase-4 plan. Object Model Guard prompts are not
  detected: Defender is current here, and no prompt or modal dialog was
  seen (`probes/dialog-probe.ps1`).
- `addressed_to_me` is empty on 44 % of items (archives, Sent, and stores
  whose items lack the flags). Scope falls back to recipients as specified.
- The live-test exe is not kept on the machine: phase 4 deploys the app exe
  instead. The scratch directory is emptied after every run.

Not changed, with reasons:
- Three real deadlines remain in tests: SQLite `busy_timeout`, `query.timeout`
  against an endless recursive query, and net/http `ResponseHeaderTimeout`
  against a handler that never answers. These timers live inside
  SQLite/net/http and cannot take an injected clock. Each guards an operation
  that can never succeed, so the result does not depend on timing.

## 2026-10-14 — Phase 1a: Go foundation built

- Module `mailsense` (go.mod at the repo root, Go 1.27). Direct deps are only
  `modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1` (SQLite 3.53.4) and `golang.org/x/sys`.
  Packages: `config` (embedded `schema.json`, 53 settings), `events`,
  `logx`, `fsx`, `httpx`, `secrets`, `mail`, `scope`, `store`, `source`,
  `source/archive`, `jobs`, `syncer`, `buildinfo`, `cmd/mailsense` (wiring
  only). Scripts: `build.sh`, `test.sh`, `fixture-import.sh` (+ `lib.sh`).
  How-to: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`.
- Evidence:
  - `scripts/test.sh` passes: gofmt, vet (host + windows + fixture tag), and
    90 test functions plus 1 fuzz target (7 seeds) under `-race`. The SQL
    guard fuzz ran ~1M execs in 15 s with no failure.
  - `scripts/build.sh`: `dist/mailsense` 11.8 MB (linux) and
    `dist/mailsense.exe` 7.75 MB (PE amd64, subsystem 2 = GUI, version stamp
    embedded).
  - `scripts/fixture-import.sh` on `out/mailbox.jsonl` (244 MB): 33,842
    messages (19,999 inbox + 13,843 sent), 0 skipped, 0 duplicates. Scope
    33,587 owner / 146 shared / 109 unattributed, exactly the legacy ground
    truth. Identity: 1 SMTP + 2 legacy-DN aliases. Import wall time 13.0 s
    (WSL2); an unchanged rerun takes 0.24 s because cursors skip both folders.
    The DB is 305 MB after a WAL checkpoint. FTS returns the same hits with
    and without accents: réunion/reunion 436, ébauche/ebauche 35, déjà/deja 3,315.
- Verdicts by rule (fixture): 13,843 sent_folder; 19,744 addressed_to_me
  flag (to/cc); the 255 inbox items without the flag split 146
  recipients_are_others / 109 no_recipients. None of those 255 reaches the
  owner through recipients.
- Decisions (ARCHITECTURE "Decision changes"): `schema.json` replaces
  `defaults.json`; owner identity lives only in `scope`; FTS5 is contentless
  with `contentless_delete=1`. A content copy cost 124 MB (DB 435 → 305 MB);
  snippets will be built from `messages.body` in phase 3.

### Findings (new)

1. **Legacy body cap is UTF-16, not code points.** 4,009 fixture bodies sit
   at exactly 8,000 UTF-16 units and none exceed it. Python's `len()==8000`
   finds only 2,416 and misses the 1,593 that contain astral characters
   (emoji). Go flags `body_truncated` on all 4,009 (`archive.legacy_body_chars`).
2. **The legacy SQL guard had gaps.** These all passed its regex:
   `UPDATE "main"."t" SET`, `UPDATE t AS x SET`, `UPDATE t INDEXED BY i SET`
   and `UPDATE [t] SET` (bracket quoting). The Go guard matches any
   `UPDATE … SET` in the literal-blanked text and treats `[ ]` as quotes.
   The runner also uses a separate `mode=ro` + `query_only` pool, and writes
   through it are tested to fail.
3. **67 inbox items have no `received_at` or `sent_on`.** All are
   `REPORT.IPM.Note.NDR` (non-delivery reports). Time-windowed stats must
   disclose them rather than drop them silently.
4. **Identity tie-break.** Python `Counter.most_common` breaks ties by
   insertion order, which depends on input order. Go breaks ties by address
   (ascending). This does not change the fixture result.
5. A whitespace-only Sent sender is `unattributed` in Go. Legacy treated
   any non-empty string as `owner`. This does not affect the fixture.
6. 166 Sent items still carry a legacy DN in `sender_address`; the two
   distinct DNs became identity aliases. This matches NOTES.md. PORTING §3's
   "12,740 Sent items carry the owner's own DN" counts
   `sent_representing_address`, not `sender_address` (12,750 DN-form values
   in that field on this export). Scope never needed that field: legacy and
   Go both use the sender.

### Open

- Run `dist/mailsense.exe` and the DPAPI secret store on Windows (the code
  compiles under `GOOS=windows vet` but has not run). Do this in the next
  Windows session.
- Identity is computed over all Sent-role mail across sources. When the
  Outlook connector brings several stores (delegate, shared, archive), scope
  must run per store (PORTING §2). (Done in phase 1b.)
- The archive connector reads the file once per folder (two passes, about
  6 s each). This is acceptable for a one-off migration; a single pass would
  need a multi-folder Sync contract.
- `Config.Reload` exists but nothing watches `settings.json` yet; the API/UI
  will trigger it (phase 4). Settings flagged `restart_required` (transport
  timeouts, log file location, store/pool options) apply on the next start.
- Job history is in memory; sync outcomes persist in `sync_runs`.

## 2026-10-14 — Decisions and spike

- User decisions: native Windows desktop app (no CLI); Outlook desktop (local)
  as first source; per-task engines — decision model for triage, local
  embeddings for search, Claude for Q&A (no local/private generator).
- Research (cited in session): local LLMs on this box (Core Ultra 9 285H, Arc
  140T, DDR5-5600) ≈ 40–90 h to triage 34k mails and 3–5 min per hard question;
  NPU not useful. Decision models (SubQ, Jev, Clef, OpenAI Decisions) share
  one contract and cannot generate text or extract values.
- Spike: pure-Go SQLite FTS5 + go-ole + go-webview2 cross-compile to a 6.6 MB
  Windows exe (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) and run on Windows 11 24H2.
- Constraint found: the dev machine has no Outlook; Outlook lives on
  <agent>. Classic Outlook is required (new Outlook has no COM). Phase 1
  tests run against a fake COM layer and the 33,842-message legacy export.

- Decision-provider contracts verified → `docs/DECISION_PROVIDERS.md`. SubQ,
  Jev, Clef share the `systemone` wire format (config differences only);
  OpenAI Decisions needs its own codec.
- **Finding:** SubQ's docs state "outputs can vary between requests", which
  contradicts the legacy NOTES claim that the API is "fully deterministic".
  The Go triage cache and evaluation must not assume determinism; measure
  repeat-agreement instead (add a test-harness probe in phase 2).

- Legacy porting spec → `docs/PORTING.md`. New findings from that review (not
  in the legacy NOTES), each to be acted on in the Go design:
  1. **UTC double conversion (latent bug):** the PS export calls
     `.ToUniversalTime()` on `PropertyAccessor` PT_SYSTIME values, which are
     already UTC → `last_verb_execution_time` / `local_commit_time` likely
     shifted by the UTC offset. Go: OOM VT_DATE = local→UTC; PropertyAccessor
     dates = UTC as-is. Needs a fixture test + live check on a real mailbox.
  2. **Cache-busting state:** history/examples blocks embed live global counts,
     so every `analyze` changes every state hash and re-bills the full archive.
     Go: triage state uses a bucketed/pinned behavior snapshot, never live totals.
  3. **Evaluation leak:** weak-label reply evaluation scored the blended value
     (70% learned from those same replies). Go: evaluate `model_value`.
  4. Two diverging owner-identity functions (`scope.discover_identity` vs
     `history.detect_owner`). Go: one identity owner in `scope`.
  5. Threading ignores captured Message-ID/In-Reply-To/References and lumps all
     empty-subject mail into one thread. Go: header-based threading first.
  6. Inbox count of exactly 19,999 is suspicious (Cached Exchange sync window
     or a cap?) — verify on the live Outlook.
  7. Correlations floor with `int()`, report rounds half-up — Go: one rounding rule.
  8. All behavior times are UTC, not the owner's local time — Go: local-time
     aware stats (timezone setting).

### Open

- Verify Jev and Clef API contracts against vendor docs before adding presets.
- French accuracy of decision models is undocumented — measure with `evaluate`.

## 2026-11-04 — AGPL license and one owner for public copy

The release decisions were settled: AGPL-3.0-or-later, the legacy Python
prototype and every environment-specific script removed, the module path moved
to `github.com/LLM-4-People/mailsense`, and publication under the
`LLM-4-People` organization. The goal, the decisions, the current state, and the
ordered next actions now live in `docs/RELEASE_PLAN.md`, which is the single
owner of release status. This entry is the chronological record.

`LICENSE` is the canonical FSF AGPL-3.0 text (661 lines, 34,523 bytes), copied
verbatim. `NOTICE` carries the copyright, the warranty disclaimer, and the
third-party notices. `README.md`, `README.fr.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the release
plan now state the real license instead of "all rights reserved".

`internal/prose` is the single owner of the public-copy rules: no em dash, no
spaced en dash used as punctuation, no double hyphen used as punctuation, and a
short list of stock marketing phrases. It skips fenced code blocks and inline
code spans, so a command flag such as `--ignore-missing` and a Markdown table
separator stay legal, while a numeric range such as `1,3–1,8x` stays legal
because the en dash is not spaced. `internal/ui/i18n_test.go` now calls the same
owner instead of keeping a second dash check inline. Four em dashes in the
privacy pages and two in an `app.js` comment were fixed.

**Regression.** `TestPublicCopyFollowsTheRules` scans the closed list of public
files; `TestEveryRuleBites` proves each rule has an input that triggers it;
`TestCheckDocumentSkipsCode` proves code and inline spans are skipped;
`TestCatalogCopyHasNoDashes` now consumes the same owner for both catalogs.

**Mutation.** Appending "A sentence — with an em dash." to `README.md` made the
public-copy test fail at `README.md:82` with `em dash`, then passed again after
the file was restored.

**Evidence.** `go test ./internal/prose -count=1` passed; `go test ./internal/ui
-run TestCatalogCopyHasNoDashes -count=1` passed; a previous `go build ./...`
and `make fast-check` from the other repository are not evidence for this tree.
The full `scripts/test-fast.sh` run on this tree is still required.

**Residual risk.** The guard covers a fixed list of public files. A new public
page outside the list is not scanned until it is added. The stock-phrase list is
a proxy for tone, not a grammar check. The remaining real-looking client
fixtures and the generated brand assets are the next release items. The deleted
`.env` keys still need to be revoked by the owner. The session must stay in
`<repo root>`; it must not be moved.

## 2026-11-04 — Generated public surface, in progress

The owner asked for a repository that is unique but largely generated rather
than hand-written: brand assets, landing pages, READMEs, documentation,
installer, first-run setup, and GitHub automation. This entry records the
generator's state so the work is resumable after a context compaction.

`docs/site.json` is now the single machine-readable source for the public
surface. It carries the product name, repository, tagline, intro, bilingual
feature list, the "what runs where" table, the getting-started steps, status,
build instructions, license copy, navigation, and the banner line. French and
English live side by side, so the two trees can no longer drift.

`internal/site` renders that source:
- `site.go` loads and validates it, rejects an empty translation, a row whose
  cell count differs from the declared columns, an unknown navigation key, and
  an unresolved `{placeholder}`;
- `render.go` renders `docs/index.md`, `docs/fr/index.md`, `README.md`, and
  `README.fr.md` from the same source, with one link map per output;
- `brand.go` renders `docs/assets/mark.svg`, `logo.svg`, and `banner.svg` from
  one palette and one mark geometry, each with a generated-by header, a title,
  and a description;
- `site_test.go` proves the outputs are current, deterministic, complete in both
  languages, valid XML, and that a hand edit is detected by `-check`.

The generator command `cmd/gensite` and the `-write` run are the next step; the
tests will fail until the generated files are written. The public copy rules
from `internal/prose` apply to the rendered pages as soon as they land.

**Evidence so far.** `go test ./internal/prose` passes; the mutation that
appended an em dash to `README.md` failed at `README.md:82`; `go test
./internal/ui -run TestCatalogCopyHasNoDashes` passes with the shared rule.

**Residual risk.** The generator is new and has not yet written the tree. The
French copy in `docs/fr/index.md` still has the old table until the first
`-write`. The remaining real-looking client fixtures are still present.
